author: Thaladar
subject: Decurse Feels Outdated, Here’s How to Fix It Without Nerfing Warlocks
content_md:
In battlegrounds, curses often go untouched and it’s easy to see why. The current Decurse ability feels underpowered and impractical compared to other dispel tools in the game.

 **Suggestions for Improvement**

To bring Decurse in line with other dispel mechanics:

 * Allow Druids to Decurse in Feral Form – So Ferals can contribute without crippling their damage.
 * Introduce “Abolish Curse” to Druids and Mages – A short-duration buff that removes curses over time, like Abolish Disease/Poison.
 * Intoduce Decurse to more classes that have a natural affinity to support their teams directly

 **Why It’s a Problem**

Affliction Warlocks can apply two curses in one GCD (e.g., Curse of Agony combined with Curse of Recklessness, Shadows, or Elements via talents). They also have a talent that reduces the chance their curses are removed by 15%, meaning each decurse attempt has an 85% success rate. In practice, this often requires multiple GCDs to clear curses, especially in BGs where several allies are affected. Meanwhile, oppressive effects like Curse of Tongues can shut down healers and casters for entire fights with almost no counterplay. A single Warlock GCD can cripple an entire team’s chance of winning by gimping their healer.

For instance, Warlocks spend 1 GCD for two curses on one target, that’s about 2.36 GCDs of decursing. Now imagine you're having a whole team that are getting spammed with these curses.

 **Classes that can decurse face major trade-offs:**

Mages: Limited instant casts; decursing means sacrificing damage and control.
Boomkins: Same issue as Mages, losing pressure for utility.
Feral Druids: Decursing is practically impossible without destroying their damage output.
Restoration Druids: The best decursers due to HoTs, but even they lose healing time and often fail multiple times due to dispel protection.

Effectively, only one spec (Resto Druid) can realistically handle decursing as part of its gameplan. Everyone else pays too high an opportunity cost.

 **Comparison to Other Dispel Mechanics**

Priest – Dispel Magic: Removes two magic effects per cast.
Paladin – Cleanse: Removes magic, poison, and disease in one GCD.
Priest/Druid - Abolish Disease/Poison: Provides ongoing protection against reapplication.

 **My Experience as a Healer**

I often play as a Discipline Priest and team up with Paladin healers. When we’re together, it feels incredible. Between us, we can handle almost every type of debuff: magic, poison, disease. It’s like having a complete toolkit for keeping our team alive. But there’s one glaring weakness: curses. The moment we face a Warlock team, everything changes. A single Curse of Tongues can completely shut down our healing, especially for Paladins who rely on fast casts. Suddenly, our strength disappears, and there’s no reliable counter unless we have a Restoration Druid on the team.

What makes this worse is how much fun it takes out of the game when you’re impacted by this and it’s almost never removed. For Alliance players, this problem is amplified because we generally have fewer Warlocks ourselves due to racial balance, Horde has WOTF, Tremor Totem, and Fear Ward, which makes Warlocks far more attractive on their side. So not only do we face more Warlocks, but we also lack the natural counters they bring.

That’s where the problem lies. Resto Druids are rare in PvP, and they’re one of the least developed healing specs in TWOW. When they do show up, it feels amazing. I love that as a Resto Druid I can cleanse Viper Sting from Priests, throw out an Innervate when someone is running dry, and remove curses. That kind of utility feels rewarding and impactful and it makes me feel like I’m contributing something unique to the team. However, for pure healing output and to actually keep your allies topped, just having one Resto Druid is not enough - you need another healer to consistently make sure your friends don't die.

And let me be clear: I love that Warlocks have so many tools. Don’t take that away from them. Their design is great, and their curses add depth to the game. The issue isn’t that curses are too strong; it’s that other classes simply don’t have enough tools to deal with them. When one ability can cripple an entire healing core, the counterplay shouldn’t hinge on the presence of a single rare spec.

The only other class that can apply a similar debuff is the Rogue with Mind-numbing Poison. But for that to work, they need to coat their weapons with it, a huge opportunity cost, and then land melee hits on every target they want to affect. That’s not realistic in a team fight, especially when a Warlock can comfortably sit in the backline and apply Curse of Tongues instantly to multiple targets without risk.

Adding more options for curse removal would create a healthier, more dynamic experience for everyone. It would spread the responsibility across classes instead of leaving it all on one spec and that means more teamwork, more strategy, and more fun for everyone. :)

>
>

>
>  I also want to be able to fly without having to go to the flightmaster.

You probably know that Warlocks have DoTs in their toolkit that are magic in nature. None of the decurse classes can remove all Warlock debuffs, since they’re a mix of magical and curse-based effects. So the idea that these classes could “just dispel everything” doesn’t hold.

With Affliction, Curse of Agony is often paired with Curse of Shadows, meaning you get two curses in a single GCD. On top of that, both have around a 15% chance to resist dispels, which makes decursing unreliable. In practice, a Restoration Druid may need to spend more than two GCDs just trying to remove them, which makes it inefficient and often not worth it.

The biggest issue, though, is Curse of Tongues. It heavily disrupts classes like Shamans, Holy Paladins, Priests, and other casters. It lasts a long time and significantly slows gameplay in a way that feels frustrating rather than interactive. One Curse of Tongues on those classes effectively takes them out of the game instantly. The only comparable effect is Rogue’s Mind-numbing Poison, but that requires actual commitment and can’t just be spread freely across a 30–40 yard caster radius.

On top of that, it even affects communication, you literally start typing in demonic, which is a fun flavor detail, but in practice it makes it harder to coordinate with teammates in-game. That ends up pushing players toward external tools like Discord just to function properly, gameplay should never force that.

If decurse mechanics aren’t improved, then Curse of Tongues needs a heavy nerf. It should have a meaningful cooldown (something like 5–10 seconds) so it can’t just be spammed, and its duration should be significantly reduced. The same goes for Curse of Shadows, the duration is excessive.

To be honest, I had only one occasion of this.
Some guy got to unreachable location on horde ramp. Pet couldn't get him, he was out of LOS. After the ticket, this guy was teleported down.

I personally consider tunnel roofs as "fine" places. Jump is easy there. Player is not in total safety - you can shoot him and sometimes send pet. Also, player is pinned to one place. He is able to get out only with help of his team.

Gnome-only passages are kinda funny, but horde has goblins now - they can sneak there too. Pets get there just fine.

Walljumping is questionable. I think it should be symmetric for horde and alliance to be fair.

Think about it from different angle. If you remove skill cap provided by jumping, then the only thing that win battleground would be gear. There will be even less oportunities to outplay enemy team.

author: Vega12
subject: Re: WSG is becoming unplayable with all the roof + GY abuse. Just fix it.
content_md:
“**WSG jumps were never intended, so they should be removed**” is a bad argument.

Almost every competitive game in history has high-skill mechanics that started as unintended, but became core parts of gameplay:

- Bunnyhopping & rocket jumping (Quake/TF2)

- Strafe-jumping (CS)

- Wavedashing (Smash Melee)

- Creep pulling & aggro tricks (DotA)

- Mutalisk stacking (StarCraft BW)

- Slope boosting in Titanfall 2

- Tap-strafing in Apex/Titanfall
If developers removed everything unintended, these games would lose the very depth that made them great.

WoW is no different.
Classic/Vanilla are full of emergent mechanics Blizzard never planned but players turned into real skill expression:

- Heroic Strike queuing

- Spell batching tricks (In 1.12 you could "jump" cancel the stun of charges/intercept, you still can vanish incoming CCs like death-coil or rocket-helm, you can still "target dummy" the hunter trap)

- wsg / ab / av jumps

- Countless PvP techs like LoS jukes and timing abuses
These weren’t designed — but they became core to how Vanilla actually plays.

WSG jumps are the same category.
They don’t make you invulnerable, they don’t break the map, and they have counterplay.
What they do is reward:

- mechanical skill

- map knowledge

- movement mastery

- creative flag-carrying routes

- coordinated counterplay
Without jumps, FCing becomes almost entirely a gear/gold check. With jumps, it has a real skill ceiling and enables even green geared players to pick up the flag — just like every other competitive game.

If “it wasn’t intended” was a valid reason to delete things, WoW would lose half of the mechanics that define Vanilla gameplay today.

Unintended ≠ bad.
Unintended is where most of the depth in competitive games comes from.

Was it ever intended that raids leave two-thirds of the trash mobs alive in Molten Core? Even Warcraft Logs—the largest parsing site—requires guilds to kill a minimum number of mobs just to make runs count.

Was it intended that players use Invis Pots to skip entire sections of Blackwing Lair?

Unintended ≠ bad.
Unintended is where most of the depth in competitive games comes from.

And also, always keep in mind we play on turtle wow, where stamina values remain the same for most of the time, but the dmg is trippled. I imagine you all got hit with a 3k earthshock or something similar, how very often do jumps not matter because you get rofled into graveyard...  dead_turtle_head

Personally i would rather have a rated BG option, where i can play against people who use every consume & know the map like their own house. This would leave the more casual players to play warsong like they want - clash mid & the team with more gear wins.

Also: Fix the Roof Jumps + China Jump. Rest is piss easy and doable by every race/gender/0% Movement speed

> Personally i would rather have a rated BG option, where i can play against people who use every consume & know the map like their own house. This would leave the more casual players to play warsong like they want - clash mid & the team with more gear wins.

With all respect, this won't work.
It is the same argument that killed twinking in retail. Twinks were saying "we like to play against eachother", but when blizz made separate queues for enabled and disabled xp, twinking suddenly died.
People don't want to fight their own kin. They want to dominate. There is nothing wrong in it, but lets just be honest with eachother.

Rated arena worked in TBC because it also featured stonger rewards than non-rated battlegrounds.
Rated battlegrounds without any special reward won't be played at all. At least while we have vanilla honor system.
In vanilla honor system people don't want to play against eachother and they don't want hard fights. People want to optimize honor per hour. Easiest way to do so is to play against afk random players.

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: Curse of Exhaustion in BGs – No Counterplay Issue
content_md:
The issue with Warlock spells like CoE and Death Coil (a spell that never should have been added to the Lock kit in the first place) is that you have arguments like "it's the only way for Warlocks to create distance", which by the sounds of it will have you believe that these are only defensive options. On the contrary, these can be used quite offensively as well.
CoE is an issue just as much as CoT is an issue. These would have been far more OK if they actually had cast times of their own.

Also, decurse is quite weak in the current state of the game. I wrote a thread about it: [viewtopic.php?p=161905&hilit=decurse#p161905](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=161905&hilit=decurse#p161905).
The amount of filler curses flying around everywhere makes decursing a team extremely mana-draining, you effectivelly CC yourself due to the sheer amount of curses that also benefit from anti-decurse talents.

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: PVP UPDATE KEKL
content_md:
People need a bit of proportionality here.

The number of players who actually did the old high-rank grind is **tiny** compared to the total playerbase. For most people, that system was never a meaningful or realistic path. It was an extreme time sink that favored a very specific minority. So making PvP rewards more accessible is not some apocalypse for the server. For the vast majority, it is simply a healthier design choice.

Also, the old system was not some pure noble test of skill and honor. It heavily rewarded selfish behavior. We even had a good Alliance honorstacking community at Tel'Abim at one point, and it got ruined fast by players who only cared about themselves. So when people now act like the old system represented some untouchable ideal, that feels pretty dishonest.

And yes, the game changes. You cannot expect an evolving server to keep every prestige structure permanently frozen just because a small group benefited from it first. So the doomsaying is ridiculous. The game did not die because more players can access PvP gear. On the contrary, if it helps weed out selfish players I think this is the best outcome.

author: Jeeboheebo
subject: Re: PVP UPDATE KEKL
content_md:
I'm just going to write something here, in hopes of the devs(one can hope)/people reading this to understand.

Originally PvP R12-14 AND PvE T3 was never intented for casual players to achieve.
Both take time. Both take effort. Both require investing in the game HEAVILY.

On Turtle WoW (since start) this was and has been the same. With changes of course.
The PvP R12-14 was the same. The PvE T3 was slightly easier, because the "pVe MeChAnIcS" were solved decades ago.
Both did and do still require time, effort, and investment.

Just one or few years ago seeing someone on Turtle WoW with R12-14 gear had a meaning. Seeing someone with T3 still had a meaning.

And now with the most recent PvP-r1-2-3 update and what i would ideally compare to that would be PvE T3-T3.5.

The R12-14 gear&weapons do not have a meaning anymore.
As mentioned, you can play a weekend of BG's and acquire the r1 gear&weapons.
NEW Gear shares the same model as R7-10 had, which took many weeks to get.
NEW Weapons share the same models as R14 had, which took the intense 2-3 month grind to get.
I could ding 60 today on an alt and acquire ALL OF THESE in a week or less - The full r1 gearset and weapons.

The T3-T3.5 gear/weapons still have a meaning (less Naxx/more K40).
You cannot argue that you can ding 60 today with 39 other people and go into Naxx or K40 and get full sets/weapons in a week. That is not realistic.

I understand the following will be extremely hypothetical way of speaking/arguing, but the truth is there for anyone reading it to understand.

Now imagine if the PvP/PvE roles were reversed.
Let's think of a player who spent the last 12months in Naxx/K40 to get full T3-T3.5+Weapons.
And tomorrow we get an update that changes how everyone acquires T3-T3.5+Weapons from each raid;
"The new way to acquire full set of T3/T3.5+Weapons is just to participate in ONE(1) week/raid ID of either Naxx or K40 and you get rewarded the new r1 T3-3.5+Weapons corresponding to the raid you attended. 2nd week you attend rewards you the new r2 T3-T3.5+Weapons and third the final week you will get r3 T3-T3.5+Weapons as the max quality that you can get."
Do one ID of Naxx? Full r1 T3+Weapons. Same models as before.
Do one ID of K40? Full r1 T3.5+Weapons. Same models as before.

Oh and that player who spent the last 12 months farming Naxx/K40 T3-T3.5+Weapons?
Yeah he has to acquire all of them again. He has to spend another three weeks farming the SAME raids for the SAME tokens for T3-T3.5 gear and the SAME weapons just because the items got slightly tweaked.

Now how do you think this PvE-player would feel at this point?
The 12months he spent farming T3-T3.5+Weapons that are NOW accessible to literally ANYONE with ONE week of effort just by visiting the corresponding raid to get the r1 T3-T3.5+Weapons.

Turtle WoW seems to be following the literal footsteps of Blizzards own WoW.
The PvP players always get fucked one way or another.

As someone already wrote in the comments: This is not the Turtle WoW i signed up for.

I very highly understand this is classic+ and ALWAYS knew that there are changes to come.
But so far the changes are: Favor and spoon feed PvE players. PvP players? Yeah let's give them some false hopes (two years ago) of upcoming Capital City Boss&Loot tables, but never really do anything about that.
Oh and while we're at it, let's just throw all of the effort they ever did down the drain.
You farmed 2-3months to get R14? Cute. Now we let anyone look like you in one weeks farm.

But hey! We had the time and effort to create new dungeons, new raids, A LOT of new gear&weapon models.
Why didn't you do this for the new PvP r1-3 gearsets+weapons?

author: Grizb37
subject: Re: afk players with r14 tmog
content_md:
If someone AFK’d in a Naxx or Kara raid, they’d be kicked instantly.

So why are we now basically handing out Rank 14 gear for free?

Right now, people can AFK their way through battlegrounds with zero consequences. I’ve reported the same players over and over, and all we get is the usual copy-paste “We’ll look into it.” Nothing changes.

A week later, those same players are still AFKing except now they’re walking around with half a Rank 13 set and Rank 14 weapons.

This completely destroys the integrity of the ranking system. What’s the point of putting in effort if others can just leech their way to the top?

At this point, it doesn’t feel like a competitive system — it feels like free handouts.

author: Anur
subject: Re: New dampening
content_md:
From what I've heard from most players, nobody likes dampening. Most people straight up hate it. Others choose to adapt as it is beyond their power to change this. I will still try to change. I am not giving up to this retail-impotence - like change.
There is retail for lovers of slow pvp where nobody dies. Classic, and even BC are about power. You oneshot, they oneshot you. You cc, they cc you. Fast-paced, high stakes. High requirement to reaction and awareness. Bursty PVP is fine. Look at Counter-strike.

On top of that, dampening doesn't really address the burst in a proper way.
Classes that were known for oneshotting still oneshot (shaman wf + strikes) - nothing changed. Instead of 30% overkill its 5% overkill now. So the problem is not addressed. Other classes at the same time lost what made them threatening.

It was a good experiment, but I beg you, see reason, dear TWOW devs, with all respect. You are destroying it. You are destroying fun.

If for arenas oneshots are a problem - introduce this dampening on arenas only. And then you can weaken it similar way as in retail - retail does it through healing nerf over time, you can do it through damage reduction nerf over time. But please, leave normal/bg PVP alone. 20% was more than enough, honestly, even a bit too much. ~40% is just wrong.

author: Bjorn88
subject: Re: New dampening
content_md:
Pvp is basically unrecognizable with the current combination of dampening and resilience. It's a disaster.

The apparent current numbers of 30% reduction for casters and 20% for melee, combined with the ability to stack resilience, is way overtuned. Casters are doing MC-level damage versus the stamina pools of T3+ geared opponents. It is obvious that they have not done any calculations on the gameplay impact of dampening and resilience being in the game at the same time.

Moreover, devs refuse to be transparent with the forthcoming class/talent-specific dampening numbers. I've tried to poke one of the responsible devs in discord and it would not give any intel or rationale behind this. The only thing I managed to gather is that winrate is one of the key variables. Which is INHERENTLY stupid in itself.

This leads to another question: Is the endgame devs have in mind to have an "equality of outcome" pvp setting where the aim is to have a 50/50 win ratio for players? in other words, do they want to remove player agency ("skill", or the ability to make tactical decisions in BGs) as the key variable to winning the game? This is the effect of the current level of dampening. Spinning flags in AB is all too easy and the flagcarrier debuff (which I think they forgot about) means that fc with enough stacks is practically unable to defend itself versus even a single opponent with dampened damage.

If devs insist on keeping this stupid idea of dampening in the game, and resilience (which is already way more powerful than it was in TBC), they need to lower the numbers.

I suggest, for a start:
 15% for casters
 10% for melee

Also: Devs need to be FULLY transparent with class/talent-specific dampening numbers moving forward. If it's gonna be a permanent feature, it needs to be a stat as visible as any others.

author: Alfredostfu
subject: Lack of communication and worst version of PvP we've seen...so far
content_md:
The much awaited pvp patch has been around for 2 weeks now and yet the state of pvp has been the worst it has ever been. Please note that the points below are seen from an Ambershire perspective. Some will no doubt be in line with Tel'Abim and Nordanaar but some issues could be different or be different degrees of the same problem.

From a purely transparency perspective:
 - World PvP event and Ranked Arena progession were announced for the 1st of April. They have not come out as of today and there doesn't seem to be any effort to at least communicate there have been setbacks even if twow couldn't provide an ETA at this point.
 - Regular Arena Skirmishes have also been disabled for over 2 weeks even though they should be an entirely separate thing from ranked arena progression and leave the player base with 1/2 less bonus honor days.
 - Dampening has been in effect for 3 days now and once again no communication on it nor on the values applied. The playerbase is once again left to figure out on their own what's going on.
 - As for the new ranking system. The previous one lacked transparency as well but at least the playerbase had it figured out. Right now there has still been no communication on exact decay values. Vague replies given by devs on twow disc state that 62k honor is what you need from r13 to r14 yet that doesn't make sense when the people at r13 are decaying all the way to 0 after hitting even past their 20k honor per week.

PvP sets:
 - Some specs got unusable sets with dreadful stats or single sets even though the playstyle and stat requirements of their different specs is entirely different.
 - Prohibitive cost of the sets particularly for the classes that got 2 or more sets. This would standalone be an issue but once you add a blocker on weekly farmed honor it becomes even worse. The only certainty is that by the time you have somehow managed to accumulate enough honor to buy the full set there's a good chance that new content has been released that overwrites it entirely.
 - Everyone and their mother having a r14 weapon transmog. Before this would be a beacon of pride, sweat, tears and most likely a lack of showering. Now it's something you do within 1 AB day only to be awarded with what is now the new pre-bis MC weapon entirely unusable to anyone that has been here since server launch.

PvP itself:
 - Thorn Gorge. Visually? Fantastic, I would daresay it looks better than Eye of the Storm ever did. Shame noone plays it because it doesn't give marks of honor, it doesn't have a bonus honor day, the map is bugged and sometimes you can't see who or if anyone has a particular base, Warriors and Druids are easily charging under the battleground to their death, Shifting to Travel,Cat, ghost wolf forms drops the flag, players able to cap bases in stealth, there are invisible blockers in certain areas of the map that you have to jump over even though visually they aren't there(such as the bridge on the right side), flags that randomly switch to horde/alliance banner even though they have been fully captured by the opposite team - These are only the issues off the top of my head and that I've experienced within the few opportunities I had to play it. Feel free to add more below so that hopefully we can get some traction and hopefully fix what can potentially be a fantastic addition to the battlegrounds.
 - As mentioned earlier arena skirmishes aren't working which leaves players with 2 bonus honor day removed entirely.
 - Dampening. Damagewise it doesn't feel like a terrible change although it's still difficult to understand why the nerf is bigger for casters than for melee but that isn't the main issue. The lack of any apparent new restrictions to healing is particularly concernening specially at a moment where healers are getting a 15% silence resist and 40% interrupt reduction with the new sets.
 - Massive queue times are back. Again, this comes from an Ambershire perspective and from what I've been able to ascertain next to Nordanaar players it hasn't been an issue there. But after an announced "fix" to the queue system that started this week it appears that from time to time the queues on Ambershire are over 20 minutes even with enough players to open the battleground and this is for solo players and not from a full premade perspective.

There are certainly many more issues and there are naturally class/spec specific issues I did not address at all but I've tried to mostly avoid those because they are not the core problem of what has been going on for the past 2 weeks nor do I play enough of every class to give an informed opinion on them.

Most of all it's the lack of communication and transparency and one random message tossed every once in a while by a dev in between the ruckus of twow discord's pvp-general channel isn't really providing clarity to most if any of the playerbase.

Shame noone plays it because it doesn't give marks of honor, it doesn't have a bonus honor day, the map is bugged and sometimes you can't see who or if anyone has a particular base, Warriors and Druids are easily charging under the battleground to their death, Shifting to Travel,Cat, ghost wolf forms drops the flag, players able to cap bases in stealth, there are invisible blockers in certain areas of the map that you have to jump over even though visually they aren't there(such as the bridge on the right side), flags that randomly switch to horde/alliance banner even though they have been fully captured by the opposite team - These are only the issues off the top of my head and that I've experienced within the few opportunities I had to play it. Feel free to add more below so that hopefully we can get some traction and hopefully fix what can potentially be a fantastic addition to the battlegrounds.
- As mentioned earlier arena skirmishes aren't working which leaves players with 2 bonus honor day removed entirely.
- Dampening. Damagewise it doesn't feel like a terrible change although it's still difficult to understand why the nerf is bigger for casters than for melee but that isn't the main issue. The lack of any apparent new restrictions to healing is particularly concernening specially at a moment where healers are getting a 15% silence resist and 40% interrupt reduction with the new sets.
- Massive queue times are back. Again, this comes from an Ambershire perspective and from what I've been able to ascertain next to Nordanaar players it hasn't been an issue there. But after an announced "fix" to the queue system that started this week it appears that from time to time the queues on Ambershire are over 20 minutes even with enough players to open the battleground and this is for solo players and not from a full premade perspective.

There are certainly many more issues and there are naturally class/spec specific issues I did not address at all but I've tried to mostly avoid those because they are not the core problem of what has been going on for the past 2 weeks nor do I play enough of every class to give an informed opinion on them.

Most of all it's the lack of communication and transparency and one random message tossed every once in a while by a dev in between the ruckus of twow discord's pvp-general channel isn't really providing clarity to most if any of the playerbase.

author: Ellifta
subject: 30% Dampening on Casters is Well Deserved
content_md:
For the entire duration of 1.18, the outcome of a BG could be more or less guessed based on how many casters one team had versus the another, assuming gear was mostly equal. Warlocks, elemental shamans and scythe mages were blasting people from full HP to 0. People were joking about apologizing in advance if you joined a BG as a warrior.

If anything, in an ideal PvP setting physical damage should have 0 dampening except for rogues. The way this dampening was implemented was bad, it should have been announced by developers and made explicit instead of letting the community figure out the numbers, but the number itself is actually good.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Diminishing crowd of control is doen't working
content_md:
Diminishing returns in Turtlewow are very much a thing.

But classic wow behaves quite differently from wotlk in many ways. One of which is CC.
Short form CC's usually have a fixed duration (Cheapshot, Death Coil, Intercept etc.) and if you are hit by multiple of the same category, their duration is halfed on the second application and quartered on the 3. application until it resets after 15 seconds. So far, thats the same way it did in wotlk afaik.

But the longer from CCs like Polymorph and Sap behave different. Instead of having a fixed duration, each second you are in these CC effects, the game rolls you a chance for the effect to end prematurely. That chance increases and without diminishing returns usually breaks around 9-12 seconds. But if you get rotten luck, its possible to sit in CC for up to 20 seconds from a single CC spell.
Diminishing returns on repeated long form CC of the same type increases the chance to break out prematurely. Its less likely you will sit in CC for 10+ seconds, but its not impossible.

Additionally, different forms of CC do not share Diminishing return. If you get Sapped into Sheeped into Ice Trap, those effects are not sharing DR. So you will likely be CCd for longer than 30 seconds.

But, if you sit in CC for long periods of time, that is usually something that can be remedied by better play. As a ranged character, you want to keep close to cover, so if someone wants to sheep you, you can duck behind cover. If you suspect rogues nearby, try to buff someone who is in combat to also get you in combat so you can not be sapped and so on.
Dealing with CC and utilizing your own CC is a large part of what classics PvP is all about.
Additionally, make sure, once you unlocked rank 3 in pvp (should be doable in a couple hours playtime) to visit your factions PvP vendors located in Orgrimmar and Stormwind respectively and grab the Insignia. Compared to other classic servers, on turtlewow the insignia cleanses all CC effects on you uppon using. Greatly saving yourself frustrations every 3 minutes

author: Zvyrhol
subject: Failure of New Rank Progression System
content_md:
Having played in new patch, I have overviewed new PvP Rank progression system and I confront it with the goal devs wanted to achieve with new PvP system. Sadly, I've got no good news. The issue of the old system not only wasn't fixed but what is more suprising - this issue became even deeper. But more on that later...

---
 **GOAL OF THE NEW SYSTEM**

Here are devs' quote on what new system was going to fix:

> **Jamey wrote: Tue Jun 10, 2025 3:05 am**
> **Patch 1.18.1**
> ---
>  The follow-up patch focuses on broadening PvP's appeal:
> - Partially rework the current **Honor System** to reduce the brutal race against the clock at high PvP ranks.

So in other words, the idea of new rank progression system was to remove race against time to progress PvP rank. Vanilla was known for having this infamous system where you had to keep playing PvP to preserve your rank. If you stopped playing PvP - rank decay would brutally kill your progress. Turtle kept the core of this system.

Patch 1.18.1 changed the system slightly:

> **Jamey wrote: Mon Mar 02, 2026 12:23 am**
> - **PvP Ranks**
>
>     - **PvP Ranks** remain in the game. Every time you would gain **Honor** points you will also gain a portion of that amount as **Rank Points**.
>
>     - **Rank Points** are immediately credited as well. Having enough **Rank Points** immediately promotes you to a higher Rank.
>
>     - **Rank Points** decay every week, as before. You can't drop **Ranks** from this decay as before as well.
>
>     - **Rank Point** gains are not capped.
>
>     - Most PvP Rewards that can be bought for **Honor** will also have a **Rank** requirement. Buying these items will not consume or drop your **Rank**.

One of the biggest changes was that new rank progress updates automatically in the game. In the past it was updated once a week. Decay still remains and happens once a week.

Second big change is that there is no limit of pushing PvP rank.
In the old system there was a limit of RP you could get. If you were a player with most Honor in your faction, further Honor farm on that week was a waste of time because it wouldn't increase your rank progress at the end of the week. It's ironic that old system that was considered inhuman, had a barrier to stop exploiting top PvPers' mental health.

On Turtle WoW, however, there is literally no limit on how much you progress your rank - and that's core issue why this new system didn't fulfill its expectation. But why?

---
 **THE ISSUE**

To answer this question, you must understand how ranker's brain works. Ranker wants to optimally progress his rank. In the old system, the only limit was his standing. Having standing 1 was the barrier - further grind didn't make sense. Keeping standing 1 was the challenge of its own because only 1 player could have it. But because usually there weren't many people who farmed Rank at the top and none of them wanted to spend unhealthy amount of hours, they often agreed to set specific Honor cap for the server in that week. That effectively allowed rankers to "save" some time by this informal community agreement.

All of this was in the past. It's no longer relevant in new patch since players no longer compete against each other in new system. Thus, this community-invented limit no longer exists. Instead, now rankers compete against server-set decay. Decay is now the only enemy of ranker.

Ranker's brain wants to get as much rank progress as possible. In the old system, amount of RP was limited so it prevented players from farming 24 hours a day. In the new system, to get progress you just play some PvP and that's it. Each match grants similar amount of RP. So to progress their rank, now PvPer must fill Rank bar to the next level. All of this before decay that occurs once a week kills your progress. So the PvPers still must face race against time - to play as many BGs as possible before decay occurs. WITH NO LIMIT. New system encourages this behaviour.

This problem is especially seen on last ranks where decay is the most impactful. From my experience, from Rank 12 to 13 weekly decay equivalent in honor is about 15 000 Honor (150 000 Honor in the old system). Here is the clue: after hitting this 15 000 Honor barrier, rankers are discouraged from leaving PvP because from now on, they make actual progress beyond that decay. Ideally, you shouldn't go to sleep, shouldn't spend unnecessary time on raiding or farming gold because you lose opportunity to progress your rank beyond decay - you should spend all of this time on further rank grind. Result is that the new system promotes even unhealthier grind on higher ranks that was in the past.

Historically, here is the experimental chart that shows amount of RP awarded based on weekly Honor got in the old system (old screen from OG Vanilla).

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/gbZpQJN.png)

You can see that it isn't linear, more Honor doesn't mean proportionally more RP. Though this is only experimental, chart shows that there is no point in spending more time on Honor grind at some point.

New system is linear. More Honor means proportionally more RP.

---
 **CONSEQUENCES**

New patch was to "reduce the brutal race against the clock at high PvP ranks". It failed to achieve its goal because rankers are encouraged to spend even more time than before when they break decay value.

You can compare that to this imaginary situation: there is a race between multiple runners. Before the change, race course was 50 km long and runners had to keep an average speed of 20 km per hour to win the race. After the change, race course was reduced to 25 km so runners are encouraged to sprint to spend similar effort - let's say an average speed of runner is 30 km per hour now.

Similarly, all of this happened in patch 1.18.1. Rank grind across multiple weeks was reduced but at the cost of spending much more time in a weekly session. Rankers are forced to play even more per week than in the past to quickly progress their rank before decay ruins it.

One of the consequences is clear. Marathoners (rankers who play regularly but can't "sprint") are still being gatekept by this system. Highest ranks are beyond reach for them even if some of them play PvP regularly. Instead, server officially promotes unhealthy grind of 12 hours a day to quickly progress rank. They didn't abolish the need of "sprint", instead they shortened the length of this "sprint".

"Casual" PvPer who got 1 000 000 Honor in one year by playing regularly each week can't have access to highest ranks.
Meanwhile, sweaty PvPer who got only 200 000 Honor total in that year and who spent long hours in BGs during a few weeks can get R14 without a problem. Then he quits the PvP. Is that how this system should work?

---
RMT AND ACCOUNT BOOSTING
SHADY BACKGROUND OF THE NEW SYSTEM

Another consequence is that account-sharing service becomes optimal way to obtain PvP rank. Decay is set to specific constant value on specific rank. If many people rank on one character, decay is still only one. This has already been abused by boosting companies. The following screenshot might blow your mind and is taken directly from one of these shady websites (it concerns Nordanaar server and is adjusted to patch 1.18.1):

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/iQKKDDU.png)

In the old system, obtaining R14 from zero in just one month was impossible. But there is nothing impossible for organised groups. Since account sharing is now optimal, you can imagine how organised groups abuse it and how limited it is for normal players. The old system required spending months on that. One thing is certain - their bussiness is now thriving.

Whether the change of the system was intended to benefit those sites or if it was an effect of pure stupidity of the designer, I'm not certain. But one might connect the dots if they know the past.

content_html:
Having played in new patch, I have overviewed new PvP Rank progression system and I confront it with the goal devs wanted to achieve with new PvP system. Sadly, I've got no good news. The issue of the old system not only wasn't fixed but what is more suprising - this issue became even deeper. But more on that later...

GOAL OF THE NEW SYSTEM


Here are devs' quote on what new system was going to fix:
Patch 1.18.1
The follow-up patch focuses on broadening PvP's appeal:
  • Partially rework the current Honor System to reduce the brutal race against the clock at high PvP ranks.

So in other words, the idea of new rank progression system was to remove race against time to progress PvP rank. Vanilla was known for having this infamous system where you had to keep playing PvP to preserve your rank. If you stopped playing PvP - rank decay would brutally kill your progress. Turtle kept the core of this system.

Patch 1.18.1 changed the system slightly:
  • PvP Ranks
    • PvP Ranks remain in the game. Every time you would gain Honor points you will also gain a portion of that amount as Rank Points.
    • Rank Points are immediately credited as well. Having enough Rank Points immediately promotes you to a higher Rank.
    • Rank Points decay every week, as before. You can't drop Ranks from this decay as before as well.
    • Rank Point gains are not capped.
    • Most PvP Rewards that can be bought for Honor will also have a Rank requirement. Buying these items will not consume or drop your Rank.
One of the biggest changes was that new rank progress updates automatically in the game. In the past it was updated once a week. Decay still remains and happens once a week.

Second big change is that there is no limit of pushing PvP rank.
In the old system there was a limit of RP you could get. If you were a player with most Honor in your faction, further Honor farm on that week was a waste of time because it wouldn't increase your rank progress at the end of the week. It's ironic that old system that was considered inhuman, had a barrier to stop exploiting top PvPers' mental health.

On Turtle WoW, however, there is literally no limit on how much you progress your rank - and that's core issue why this new system didn't fulfill its expectation. But why?

THE ISSUE


To answer this question, you must understand how ranker's brain works. Ranker wants to optimally progress his rank. In the old system, the only limit was his standing. Having standing 1 was the barrier - further grind didn't make sense. Keeping standing 1 was the challenge of its own because only 1 player could have it. But because usually there weren't many people who farmed Rank at the top and none of them wanted to spend unhealthy amount of hours, they often agreed to set specific Honor cap for the server in that week. That effectively allowed rankers to "save" some time by this informal community agreement.

All of this was in the past. It's no longer relevant in new patch since players no longer compete against each other in new system. Thus, this community-invented limit no longer exists. Instead, now rankers compete against server-set decay. Decay is now the only enemy of ranker.

Ranker's brain wants to get as much rank progress as possible. In the old system, amount of RP was limited so it prevented players from farming 24 hours a day. In the new system, to get progress you just play some PvP and that's it. Each match grants similar amount of RP. So to progress their rank, now PvPer must fill Rank bar to the next level. All of this before decay that occurs once a week kills your progress. So the PvPers still must face race against time - to play as many BGs as possible before decay occurs. WITH NO LIMIT. New system encourages this behaviour.

This problem is especially seen on last ranks where decay is the most impactful. From my experience, from Rank 12 to 13 weekly decay equivalent in honor is about 15 000 Honor (150 000 Honor in the old system). Here is the clue: after hitting this 15 000 Honor barrier, rankers are discouraged from leaving PvP because from now on, they make actual progress beyond that decay. Ideally, you shouldn't go to sleep, shouldn't spend unnecessary time on raiding or farming gold because you lose opportunity to progress your rank beyond decay - you should spend all of this time on further rank grind. Result is that the new system promotes even unhealthier grind on higher ranks that was in the past.

Historically, here is the experimental chart that shows amount of RP awarded based on weekly Honor got in the old system (old screen from OG Vanilla).



You can see that it isn't linear, more Honor doesn't mean proportionally more RP. Though this is only experimental, chart shows that there is no point in spending more time on Honor grind at some point.


New system is linear. More Honor means proportionally more RP.

CONSEQUENCES


New patch was to "reduce the brutal race against the clock at high PvP ranks". It failed to achieve its goal because rankers are encouraged to spend even more time than before when they break decay value.

You can compare that to this imaginary situation: there is a race between multiple runners. Before the change, race course was 50 km long and runners had to keep an average speed of 20 km per hour to win the race. After the change, race course was reduced to 25 km so runners are encouraged to sprint to spend similar effort - let's say an average speed of runner is 30 km per hour now.

Similarly, all of this happened in patch 1.18.1. Rank grind across multiple weeks was reduced but at the cost of spending much more time in a weekly session. Rankers are forced to play even more per week than in the past to quickly progress their rank before decay ruins it.

One of the consequences is clear. Marathoners (rankers who play regularly but can't "sprint") are still being gatekept by this system. Highest ranks are beyond reach for them even if some of them play PvP regularly. Instead, server officially promotes unhealthy grind of 12 hours a day to quickly progress rank. They didn't abolish the need of "sprint", instead they shortened the length of this "sprint".

"Casual" PvPer who got 1 000 000 Honor in one year by playing regularly each week can't have access to highest ranks.
Meanwhile, sweaty PvPer who got only 200 000 Honor total in that year and who spent long hours in BGs during a few weeks can get R14 without a problem. Then he quits the PvP. Is that how this system should work?

RMT AND ACCOUNT BOOSTING
SHADY BACKGROUND OF THE NEW SYSTEM


Another consequence is that account-sharing service becomes optimal way to obtain PvP rank. Decay is set to specific constant value on specific rank. If many people rank on one character, decay is still only one. This has already been abused by boosting companies. The following screenshot might blow your mind and is taken directly from one of these shady websites (it concerns Nordanaar server and is adjusted to patch 1.18.1):




In the old system, obtaining R14 from zero in just one month was impossible. But there is nothing impossible for organised groups. Since account sharing is now optimal, you can imagine how organised groups abuse it and how limited it is for normal players. The old system required spending months on that. One thing is certain - their bussiness is now thriving.

Whether the change of the system was intended to benefit those sites or if it was an effect of pure stupidity of the designer, I'm not certain. But one might connect the dots if they know the past.
It's very difficult for me to judge, I don't see my rank, it's broken, are you sure that after 20,000 honor, the progress of the rank is moving forward?

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Failure of New Rank Progression System
content_md:
Couldn't agree with OP more, i found it already questionable back when the rank decay was capped to not lower your rank instead of killing the decay.

The reason why pvp ranking is considered so unhealthy is because the game wants you to complete it in as short of a time as possible. (Both the old and the new system) Players who don't complete it within a certain threshold are locked out completely from ever achieving their goal in pvp.

MMO players are often the kind of players who want/need a carrot on a stick to motivate them to do anything. The PvP system had - and sadly still does - dangled the carrot and moves it just out of reach for many of the less dedicated players.

If the ranks were only used for title and fame, i'd be okey with a system that is somewhat restrictive. But considering the high ranking gear is still tied to a minimum weekly earning is a massive failure of the system and ensures people who might be PvP curious but not able or willing to spend 30+h of PvP a week will more often than not decide not to pursue PvP.

But thats not even the only problem with the new pvp gear and the changes to ranking.
The old gear still being in the game but no longer being available for new players trying to get into pvp creates a potential powergap. Mages who held onto their old PvP gloves can combine it with the new setbonus to get a Manashield that is 570pts stronger than default. Twice the intended amount from wearing the PvP set.
In the case of the Druid, Old rankers still have the stealth detection bonus which new PvP players can currently not get.

Having the Transmog being completely devalued to single days worth of effort for single pieces of the R13 gear and R14 weapons is just the icing on the cake.

I am very happy twow staff tried to work on the PvP set and we got what we did, Its objectively already much less bad than the system used to be by removing the competition with your own faction as an element. But It would be a mistake to leave it as is. More polish is desperately needed.

author: Urthius
subject: WSG: discussion on allowable geometry
content_md:
The geometry of WSG allows many "jumps" that have become part of the game, even being included in the [Wowhead guide](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/guide/classic-wow-warsong-gulch-advanced-map-strategies-wsg#jump-spots).

However, since TWoW isn't exactly Classic, the permissibility of jumps has been subject to [debate](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=23177).

The goal of this thread is to generate a **public consensus** on what is and isn't allowable in WSG on TWoW.

When I asked a GM, I received the following reply: "Use this simple rule: if place can be reached with normal walking or jumping (no walljumping), this place is okay to use."

My interpretation of the rule:
1. "Normal walking or jumping" means for all races/classes/genders **without speed buffs or slow fall effects**.
2. Alliance Fence Jump (slipping through fence) is **allowed**.
3. Alliance Graveyard Jump is **allowed** (a "walljump" to an accessible place, and devs seem to allow it).
4. Horde Graveyard Jump is **allowed** (a speed buff to an accessible place, and devs seem to allow it).
5. Alliance Top of Tunnel Jump is **allowed**.
6. Horde Top of Tunnel Jump is **allowed**.
7. Horde Fence Jump is **not allowed** (warned by GM, and not all races/classes/genders can do it).
8. Horde Caravan Jump is **not allowed** (warned by GM, even though it is theoretically a normal jump).
 - Presumably the same applies for Alliance.
9. Fence walking is **not allowed**.
10. Stump Jump is **not allowed**.
11. "Safespotting" (e.g. on hut) is **not allowed**.
12. Mage blink to inaccessible locations is **not allowed**.

The geometry of WSG allows many "jumps" that have become part of the game, even being included in the Wowhead guide.

However, since TWoW isn't exactly Classic, the permissibility of jumps has been subject to debate.

The goal of this thread is to generate a public consensus on what is and isn't allowable in WSG on TWoW.

When I asked a GM, I received the following reply: "Use this simple rule: if place can be reached with normal walking or jumping (no walljumping), this place is okay to use."

My interpretation of the rule:

  6. Horde Top of Tunnel Jump is allowed.

  8. Horde Caravan Jump is not allowed (warned by GM, even though it is theoretically a normal jump).

  9. Fence walking is not allowed.
  10. Stump Jump is not allowed.
  11. "Safespotting" (e.g. on hut) is not allowed.

I view #3 and #4 above (the graveyard jumps) as debatable - devs seem to know about them and allow them.

The Wowhead article includes videos of the above jumps. Vega12 posted some videos of other jumps, but these videos have since expired. Here's another video of WSG jumps. And another.

Ideally walljumping would be fixed, but until devs can devote their limited resources to patching it, community enforcement is the only option.

author: Vega12
subject: Re: WSG: discussion on allowable geometry
content_md:
“**WSG jumps were never intended, so they should be removed**” is a bad argument.

Almost every competitive game in history has high-skill mechanics that started as unintended, but became core parts of gameplay:

- Bunnyhopping & rocket jumping (Quake/TF2)

- Strafe-jumping (CS)

- Wavedashing (Smash Melee)

- Creep pulling & aggro tricks (DotA)

- Mutalisk stacking (StarCraft BW)

- Slope boosting in Titanfall 2

- Tap-strafing in Apex/Titanfall
If developers removed everything unintended, these games would lose the very depth that made them great.

WoW is no different.
Classic/Vanilla are full of emergent mechanics Blizzard never planned but players turned into real skill expression:

- Heroic Strike queuing

- Spell batching tricks (In 1.12 you could "jump" cancel the stun of charges/intercept, you still can vanish incoming CCs like death-coil or rocket-helm, you can still "target dummy" the hunter trap)

- wsg / ab / av jumps

- Countless PvP techs like LoS jukes and timing abuses
These weren’t designed — but they became core to how Vanilla actually plays.

WSG jumps are the same category.
They don’t make you invulnerable, they don’t break the map, and they have counterplay.
What they do is reward:

- mechanical skill

- map knowledge

- movement mastery

- creative flag-carrying routes

- coordinated counterplay
Without jumps, FCing becomes almost entirely a gear/gold check. With jumps, it has a real skill ceiling and enables even green geared players to pick up the flag — just like every other competitive game.

If “it wasn’t intended” was a valid reason to delete things, WoW would lose half of the mechanics that define Vanilla gameplay today.

Unintended ≠ bad.
Unintended is where most of the depth in competitive games comes from.

Was it ever intended that raids leave two-thirds of the trash mobs alive in Molten Core? Even Warcraft Logs—the largest parsing site—requires guilds to kill a minimum number of mobs just to make runs count.

Was it intended that players use Invis Pots to skip entire sections of Blackwing Lair?

Unintended ≠ bad.
Unintended is where most of the depth in competitive games comes from.

And also, always keep in mind we play on turtle wow, where stamina values remain the same for most of the time, but the dmg is trippled. I imagine you all got hit with a 3k earthshock or something similar, how very often do jumps not matter because you get rofled into graveyard...  dead_turtle_head

Personally i would rather have a rated BG option, where i can play against people who use every consume & know the map like their own house. This would leave the more casual players to play warsong like they want - clash mid & the team with more gear wins.

Also: Fix the Roof Jumps + China Jump. Rest is piss easy and doable by every race/gender/0% Movement speed

Edit: If you dont believe me that jumps are easily reproducable - contact me. Within 20 minutes i will teach you and you will never forget on how to do them...

EditEdit: People who still say it's unintended and blizzard removed them, so should twow - Yes, blizzard removed them on Retail. On Classic 2.0 / SoM / SoD / Anniversary they activelly added more.

author: Zvyrhol
subject: Alterac Valley Guide to Turtle WoW
content_md:
Turtle Forum closes in October. It's a pity, some posts were very interesting and it's sad they probably won't be archived.

One of such posts (sorry for being not modest) was something that was regularly updated by me and that sit in a cozy corner of my hard drive and was to be released eventually. Unfortunately, this day has never came. I've planned to write full Alterac Valley guide adjusted to Turtle WoW version of the game. Turtle WoW closes soon so I release it in unfinished state. Who knows, nothing is lost in the Internet, maybe this knowledge will become useful for someone in the future. I wrote whole this guide about during Q3-Q4 of 2025 before I started creating my own AV on VMaNGOS. Last edit was made on 12th October 2025. This guide was abandoned for a while so I release it now.

The guide is in WIP state. Thus, sometimes the information isn't as precise as it could be and sometimes it even contains false information - Winterax Ritual Dagger actually had third effect that allowed to deal AoE damage, I still don't know when it activates though. Wing Commanders topic was a big mystery to me. While reading all AV guides including Wowhead one, I had impression that the people who wrote it didn't really know how exactly they worked. They just copy-pasted something that someone claimed on Nostalrius forum without verifying it.
By the way I replicated Wing Commanders behavior on VMaNGOS and I'm afraid even people who made it, didn't really know how exactly Wing Commanders work. This objective was simply very unlikely to experience during normal game in Vanilla and even now on WoW Classic it's almost impossible to organise AV match to test it.

Lastly, I want to thank whole Turtle team for bringing back undoubtedly the best iteration of Alterac Valley in the world and letting players experience it. No other private server, no Blizzard-Classic has ever done greater favour for our small AV community. You see, we had been waiting to experience legendary pre-nerfed Alterac Valley since patch 1.8 during late Vanilla that drastically changed the design of this battleground. Our community had no home to return to for more than 10 years. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

Honorable mention of AV legends: Jinro, Melg, Sotra and annonymous dev who gave us this pre-nerfed AV.
Here is the guide.

 **Alterac Valley Guide to Turtle WoW** by Zvyrhol

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) - alliance
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) - horde

---

!!! DISCLAIMER !!!

This is the only relevant guide to Alterac Valley battleground on Turtle WoW. The server uses old map from Wow's patch 1.5 developed by Blizzard with all old features included that were removed later. Presented information and strategies might not be relevant on WoW Classic and other Vanilla private servers that rely on final patch 1.12.

Custom content or slightly modified things of Turtle WoW that were never present during OG Vanilla are marked next to chapters with [CUSTOM CONTENT] tag.

---

Introduction

Welcome to my guide to Alterac Valley! The guide concentrates all AV content in one place and serves purpose of AV encyclopedia. It also contains suggested and optimal strategy for both teams as well as tips from the guy who spent hundreds of hours on Turtle WoW's version of this battleground. Whether you are completely new player or OG Blizzard's fan that came here by accident through Google, you will find something useful here.

---

Lore background

 *Long ago, the warlock Gul'dan exiled a clan of orcs called the Frostwolves to a valley hidden deep in the heart of the Alterac Mountains. The Frostwolf Clan eked out a living until Thrall triumphantly united many of Azeroth’s orcs. The Frostwolves, however, chose to remain in the valley rather than joining Thrall in Orgrimmar – and their relative peace has since been challenged by the arrival of the dwarven Stormpike Expedition. The Stormpike Expedition’s desire to mine and plumb the underexplored caves for relics has invited conflict with the Frostwolf Clan, but opinions are divided on who struck first. Were the dwarves who arrived in the valley peaceful explorers who were massacred by the orcs, or did they plan to poach and conquer?*

[~ Blizzard Entertainment](https://web.archive.org/web/20181006111423/http://eu.battle.net/wow/en/game/pvp/battlegrounds/alterac-valley)

---

How to enter Alterac Valley? [CUSTOM CONTENT]

On Turtle WoW you can access AV from any place in the world by clicking Battleground Finder icon (it's somewhere near the minimap by default). Level 51 is required to join.

---

How to win?

To win Alterac Valley battleground, your team must defeat enemy's faction boss: Vanndar Stormpike or Drek'Thar. Sounds like an easy job but it is not.

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/t5Xm7NY.png)

The boss sits in the building surrounded by his elite guard at the core of enemy base deep in enemy's territory. He has more than 100 000 HP and hits very hard.

The boss is guarded by Marshals/War Masters in his building. Practically, slaying boss without killing all of these guardians is impossible. So before you attack the boss, first you must lure out Marshals/War Masters and slay them.

But before you do it, you should first capture the graveyard at enemy's base - without respawn your team can't do much. The way to graveyard is filled with numerous NPCs so you won't have an easy job.

But it's not all. The base is also guarded by 2 Towers/Bunkers where the archers shoot anyone on a line of sight. Without these points burnt, the base will be hard to capture.

And before all of that, you must travel a long way to enemy's base without dying.

This guide will delve into all the details later.

---

REP & VENDORS:
 *amazing pots*

 *banner*

 *mount*

 *pre-raid bis items*

PVE OBJECTIVES

---

Armor Scraps to do: image of armor scraps icon, blacksmiths location

Armor Scraps are the quest items you can get from almost any enemy NPC in Alterac Valley. You can turn in large quantities of these to permanently upgrade your team's NPCs.

You turn them in to blacksmith NPC in your base (Murgot Deepforge in Alliance and Smith Regzar in Horde).

There are 4 levels of strength of your NPCs:

- 1. Normal - game starts with this level of troops.

- 2. Seasoned

- 3. Veteran

- 4. Champion
Each next level grants your NPCs more damage and health massively increasing your team's defense.

 500 Armor Scraps are needed to upgrade troops to the next level - 1500 total. After turning in 500 Armor Scraps to the blacksmith, the new dialogue will appear. Click it so new stronger units will join the game.

After upgrading your troops to Champion ones, Armor Scraps become pointless because the Champion units stay in the match forever.

Good places to farm Armor Scraps are Coldtooth Mine and Irondeep Mine as well as surrounding of Captain Balinda and Captain Galvangar. Armor Scraps drop from Troggs, Kobolds and enemy NPCs.

---

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) Lokholar the Ice Lord and ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) Ivus the Forest Lord to do: blood and crystal image, shaman/druid location, summon location

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/esZ0GsQ.png)

Lokholar the Ice Lord and Ivus the Forest Lord are probably the most iconic and powerful NPCs in the entire Alterac Valley. Each faction can summon their own mighty elemental that will lead their team to the victory.

 **How to summon?**

Horde can collect Stormpike's Soldier Blood and Alliance can collect Storm Crystal from any enemy dead player or NPC. These items have 100% drop chance though only one random player nearby can loot these. If farm the items for yourself, it's recommended to loot enemy corpses away from your team mates.

Your team must bring 200x of these items to ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) Primalist Thurloga in the cave in the Frostwolf Village or to ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) Arch Druid Renferal who is located behind the Dun Baldar North Bunker.

You can ask these NPCs via dialogue to find out how many items are still needed to start the ritual of summoning. They won't directly tell you the number but below is the approximate formula:

First dialogue "still much work to do" tells you that your team has collected below 100 items, second one "I've made contact" informs you that your team has already turned in more than 100 but less than 150 items. Last dialogue "summon is near" informs you that there are less than 50 items needed to start the summon.

After turning in last item, the Shamans or Druids start moving to the place of summoning. Be ware. If they die to enemies during the escort, the summoning will fail. These locations are: ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) small hill north of Galvangar's building or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) at the north-eastern edge of Field of Strife.

When Shamans or Druids are there, everyone in your team can click the circle to be part of the ritual of summoning. In order to summon the elemental, your team needs 10 clickers at the same time. When 10 people simultaneously click the circle, after a few seconds the Lokholar or Ivus appears and moves to the middle of the map.

 **The route**

They stop in the Field of Strife for about 3 minutes.
They soon start moving into enemy's territory. Their next stop is ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) Stormpike Graveyard or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) Frostwolf Village.
Next check-points are Aid Station or Relief Hut though usually enemy players kite them to the boss room so it rarely happens. Lastly they go to the Vanndar's or Drek'Thar's room.

 **Loot**

When elemental dies, it drops some unique [items](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13419). It's worth to note that [Cold Forged Blade](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=19110) is the only item with this look in the entire game.
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/SytENJh.png)

 **Tips**

- Elemental Lord is very good choice to break stalemate.

- Good spots to farm Stormpike's Soldier Blood and Storm Crystals are Irondeep Mine and Coldtooth Mine supposing enemy team has captured these points. NPCs there have low HP and this area isn't crowded.

- Once your team summons the elemental, you can buff them.

- Entrance caves are good spots to kite elementals - your friendly NPCs will help you much.

- Healing the elemental should be priority for every nearby player that has healing spells.

- Hunters can kite the elementals. If your elemental is being kited by enemy Hunter, you should focus on the Hunter and stop him from ruining your team's effort.

---

Cavalry to do: cavalry banner in the title

Alterac Valley is the place where swift Frostwolves and mighty Alterac Rams dwell. These animals are used by Frostwolf Clan and Stormpike Guard as loyal mounts for their trained troops. Your team can tame these animals in order to summon the cavalry that will pierce through enemy defense.

 **How to summon?**

In order to summon the cavalry, your team must meet 2 conditions:
- Tame ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) 25 [Frostwolves](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=10981) or 25 ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Alterac Rams](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=10990)

- Turn in ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) 25 [Alterac Ram Hides](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17642) or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) 25 [Frostwolf Hides](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17643)
 **Part 1:**
First, you must take the quest to tame Frostwolf or Alterac Ram. It can be picked up from ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Frostwolf Stable Master](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13616) located in the stables east of Frostwolf Village or from ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Stormpike Stable Master](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13617) who stays in the base of Dun Baldar.
You will receive the item that allows you to tame the animal. Use the item on the animal and after taming is complete, escort it back to the stables. Talk to NPC and turn in the quest.

 **Part 2:**
Second, you must turn in ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) 25 [Alterac Ram Hides](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17642) or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) 25 [Frostwolf Hides](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17643) to ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Frostwolf Wolf Rider Commander](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13441) or to ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Stormpike Ram Rider Commander](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13577).
Unlike in the first part, you don't need to accept the quest to loot these items. You can loot all 25 items and then turn them in to that NPC.

Beware!
- There is no way to find out exactly how many animals are still needed to be tamed. However, every 5 animals you tame, the animals appear in the stables. When stables are full - that means there are 5 more animals needed to be tamed. It's visual bug.

- There is no way to find out exactly how many hides are still needed for your team to complete the objective. That's why it's recommended to turn in all 25 at once.
When both conditions are fulfilled, talk to the same Commander that gave you the quest for hides. Special dialogue will appear. Click it and observe how the cavalry charges and destroyes everything that stands in their way.

 **Tips**

- Riders move very fast and their route goes by all graveyards. Make sure to follow them and capture the graveyards along the way.

- Although Riders don't as much damage as upgraded Ground Assaults, they stick together and are very tanky. If they all focus on one target, they can still one-shot an undergeared player.

- The best strategy to fight cavalry is to slow and separate them.

- Summoning cavalry is one of the easiest things low level players can do to influence the outcome of the game.

- All Riders can be buffed.

- It's possible to kill enemy's tamed Wolves or Rams that sit inside the stables to stop enemy from summoning the cavalry.

---

Infantry [CUSTOM CONTENT]

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/RkJLzTu.png)

Infantry - also known as Ground Assaults - is the elite group of ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) Reavers or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) Commandos that are the strongest soldiers of Frostwolf Clan or Stormpike Guard. They are possibly the strongest summonable units in the Alterac Valley.

The infantry consists of 11 NPCs that unlike the cavalry hit extremely hard and are more numerous. Their power scales with the upgrade level of your troops. Units with no upgrade have much less armor and deal significantly less damage. Thus, it's recommended to summon the infantry only if you upgrade the troops first.
Comparison:

- Stormpike Commando (no upgrade):
 - Level: 56 -- 9986 HP - Damage: 335-432 - Armor: 2 699 - Resistance: 0

- Champion Commando (Champion upgrade):
 - Level: 61 - 11632 HP - Damage: 559-720 - Armor: 4 091 - Resistance: 5

 **How to summon?**

There are 3 steps your team must do in order to summon the infantry.

- 1. Complete ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Irondeep Supplies](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=6985) quest or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Coldtooth Supplies](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=6982) quest 4 times. [CUSTOM CONTENT]

- 2. Activate dialogue and receive special item.

- 3. Turn in the item to ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Warmaster Garrick](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13449) or to ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Field Marshal Teravaine](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13446).

Step 1:
First, you must accept the quest from ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Frostwolf Quartermaster](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=12097) or from ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Stormpike Quartermaster](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=12096). You have choice between going to the Coldooth Mine and Irondeep Mine - always select the Mine that is further away from your base. That's because completing "harder" quest once makes as much progress as completing easier one 4 times. It makes much difference if you want to save time. But if for some reason you wanted to farm supplies from the closer and safer Mine, you would have to complete the quest 16 times. That's a bit boring if you ask me!

[CUSTOM CONTENT] It's worth to note that these numbers are different from WoW Classic where 7 and 28 quests respectively are needed to summon the infantry.

Then, you must delve into the Mine and if it's not controlled by your team, you must kill enemy leader inside. Once it's done, you are able to grab supplies from the boxes. Go back to the Quartermaster once you grab all 10 supplies.

Step 2:
If you complete 4 turn ins, special dialogue will appear when you talk to the Quartermaster.
After clicking it, you receive ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Frostwolf Assault Orders](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17442) or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Stormpike Assault Orders](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17353). The item has 15 minutes duration so make sure not to hesitate and go to the next step.

Step 3:
After you receive the item, infatry's leader will spawn. You must bring him the orders you received from Quartermaster. You will find ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Warmaster Garrick](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13449) north-west of Captain Galvangar's building and south of Snowfall Graveyard and ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Field Marshal Teravaine](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13446) to the south of Stonehearth Bunker at the ballista. Complete the quest and infantry will spawn. Then, it will automatically move through the all enemy graveyards up to the last boss.

 **Tips**

- You can buff all of these units.

- Running across the map takes much time. To save it, use ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Frostwolf Insignia](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17690) or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Stormpike Insignia](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17691) to at least swiftly return to your base.

- Infantry (if upgraded) is the most powerful summonable force in Alterac Valley. It's shines as stalemate-breaker.

- Currently there is a bug on Turtle WoW that doesn't let you summon infantry more than once in the same match.

- When you fight infantry, it's good to separate the units and kite them to your NPCs so they can help you.

- Summoning can be synchronized with cavalry or elemental - combined power might be unstoppable.

Wing Commanders to do: image of 3 of them together

Also known as Aerial Assaults. Wing Commanders are special NPC located deep in enemy territory. When you talk with them, they start moving to your base. There are 3 Wing Commander for each side. If they successfully come back to your base without being killed, they will offer you special repeatable quest. Each Wing Commander offers other type of quest. The quest will require to turn in items dropped by enemy players. The quality of the item dropped by players is defined by their PvP rank.

You need to turn in following quantity of items in order to push this objective forward:

- 120 ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Stormpike Soldier's Flesh](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17326) or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Frostwolf Soldier's Medal](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17502)

- 60 ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Stormpike Lieutenant's Flesh](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17327) or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Frostwolf Lieutenant's Medal](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17503)

- 30 ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [Stormpike Commander's Flesh](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17328) or ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Frostwolf Commander's Medal](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17504)
WORK IN PROGRESS. Unfortunately this is the most unpopular objective on Turtle WoW - hardly ever completed by players. To be honest I don't know what these Wing Commanders do on this server after completing objective. So I decided not to copy-paste what other guides for WoW Classic state. I have seen this objective fulfilled only once on Turtle WoW. If you DO have knowledge, please contact me.

Ryson's All Seeing Eye [CUSTOM CONTENT] to do: Syndicate image, orb in troll's cave, turtle's AV map to note where syndicate hides and where is trolls cave

[CUSTOM CONTENT] Ryson's All Seeing Eye is side objective that was originally in Alterac Valley in patch 1.5 but was later removed and is unknown by most WoW Classic players. Turtle WoW restored this objective.

East of Field of Strife and behind Gnoll encampment there is a hidden cave in which Syndicate has a hideout. Their boss: [Syndicate Master Ryson](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13151) gives you a quest to recover [Master Ryson's All Seeing Eye](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17354) - powerful relic that was stolen by Winterax Trolls.

The item can be found inside Winterax Hold cave. Once you find the Eye, you must carry it back to the Master Ryson. The carrier of the eye, however, is cursed. You start to glow and your appearance will surely attracts other players' attention. Though you also get extra buff: with the Eye on you, you see invisible units from a distance. It's very useful buff if you want to detect enemy Rogues or Druids.

When you go back to Master Ryson and turn in the Eye, you will unlock new dialogue options.

The first one grants you 30 minutes buff that allows you to detect invisible units from a distance - without glow effect. This effect persists through death.

The second one is continuation of this objective. Master Ryson can give you a [Ryson's Beacon](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17362) that you can place in enemy base courtyard. Once placed there, it must be protected for one minute. When it's completed, Ryson's falcon spawns over enemy base and allows you to have view on enemy from your own base. This part of the objective is practically useless but it flavours how Syndicate can help you in fighting over Alterac Valley.

 **Tips**

- The quest can be completed once per AV match.

- If you carry the Eye and mount up, you drop the item - then it can be repicked by anyone.

- Sometimes it's not worth to complete the quest and keep the Eye for your team. For example to detect enemy stealthers inside your base.

- When you die carrying the Eye, the Eye is dropped and can be repicked by anyone.

- There is only one Eye.
