Korrak the Bloodrager [CUSTOM CONTENT] to do: korrak image

[CUSTOM CONTENT] Korrak the Bloodrager was originally added to the game in patch 1.5 but was later removed and is unknown by most WoW Classic players. Turtle WoW restored his presence though with a few modifications to the original.

[Korrak the Bloodrager](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=12159) is a powerful Troll that guards the Snowfall Graveyard and the bridge to Winterax Hold. He drops unique loot for example [[Mark of Deflection]](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17108). His loot table is also shared with other world bosses so technically Korrak can be treated as a world boss.

Loot, however, isn't the only reason to kill Korrak. This mighty Troll is the objective of the quests: ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [The Legend of Korrak](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=7181) and ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Korrak the Bloodrager](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13841). Blue items from these quests are one of the best items you can get in the game without raiding - and the quest can be completed at level 51!

[CUSTOM CONTENT] These quests also give you [[Winterax Ritual Dagger]](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=50743) that is completely custom item made by Turtle WoW team. Moreover, once the quest is completed, you get access to repeatable version of this quest that gives you only the dagger: ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/Tt49ZgY.gif) [The Return of Korrak](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=7381) and ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/uAbTCOR.gif) [Korrak the Everliving](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=7382).

These quests can be picked up from NPCs in your base in Alterac Valley: [Warmaster Laggrond](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13840) and [Lieutenant Haggerdin](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=13841). To complete the quest, your team must kill Korrak and loot his skull. However, only one person can loot the skull each match - the drop goes to random person who has quest active.

Let's delve into how [Winterax Ritual Dagger] works. The description is mysterious and doesn't tell us much about the item.

First of all, the item can be activated only in Alterac Valley. When you use it, one effect is certain: you will die. The other effects depend whether you have Korrak's debuff on you. The debuff is named [Bathed in Blood](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?spell=46437) and you have it applied if Korrak dies close to you. The debuff passively does nothing and lasts 1 hour but is required in order to activate other effects of using the dagger.

- If you use the dagger and you don't have debuff on you, you will die and nothing happens.

- If you use the dagger and you have debuff on you:
 - if there is no friendly player close to you, you die and everyone in your team is summoned to the location you used the dagger.

 - if there is at least one friendly player close to you, they all get bonus 30% damage dealt buff for one minute.

 **Tips**

- [Skull of Korrak](https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=18148) drops to only one person in one game.

- The dagger can summon whole team to your location. Rogues and Druids can stay in stealth to safely travel to enemy base and there summon their whole team. This way you can drastically shorten the length of the match and guarantee your team easy win.

- If you die, the debuff fades from you making the item useless in that match.

- You can stack the daggers in your inventory from multiple games. If you already have one dagger in your inventory before you kill the Korrak, you don't need to immediately return to your base to get next dagger - this can make your action quicker.

- Winterax Ritual Dagger, in good hands, can deeply influence the outcome of the game and even let weaker team win the match.

- Currently there is an exploit in the game that allows any ranged class [to solo kill Korrak using bad pathing under the bridge](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UjwCpH5npVg).

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/GPPbQms.png)

Shredder is a unit that can be summoned via one item obtained from specific quest in Alterac Valley. This item is called [Zinfizzlex's Portable Shredder Unit]
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/WzdqG9o.png)
<https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17384>. It allows you to summon and control a Shredder which is powerful elite with very high health pool. It causes you to control the unit but at any time you can break the control and order your Shredder to guard specific spot. Note that you can summon the Shredder only inside Alterac Valley.

Turtle Forum closes in October. It's a pity, some posts were very interesting and it's sad they probably won't be archived.

One of such posts (sorry for being not modest) was something that was regularly updated by me and that sit in a cozy corner of my hard drive and was to be released eventually. Unfortunately, this day has never came. I've planned to write full Alterac Valley guide adjusted to Turtle WoW version of the game. Turtle WoW closes soon so I release it in unfinished state. Who knows, nothing is lost in the Internet, maybe this knowledge will become useful for someone in the future. I wrote whole this guide about during Q3-Q4 of 2025 before I started creating my own AV on VMaNGOS. Last edit was made on 12th October 2025. This guide was abandoned for a while so I release it now.

The guide is in WIP state. Thus, sometimes the information isn't as precise as it could be and sometimes it even contains false information - Winterax Ritual Dagger actually had third effect that allowed to deal AoE damage, I still don't know when it activates though. Wing Commanders topic was a big mystery to me. While reading all AV guides including Wowhead one, I had impression that the people who wrote it didn't really know how exactly they worked. They just copy-pasted something that someone claimed on Nostalrius forum without verifying it.
By the way I replicated Wing Commanders behavior on VMaNGOS and I'm afraid even people who made it, didn't really know how exactly Wing Commanders work. This objective was simply very unlikely to experience during normal game in Vanilla and even now on WoW Classic it's almost impossible to organise AV match to test it.

Lastly, I want to thank whole Turtle team for bringing back undoubtedly the best iteration of Alterac Valley in the world and letting players experience it. No other private server, no Blizzard-Classic has ever done greater favour for our small AV community. You see, we had been waiting to experience legendary pre-nerfed Alterac Valley since patch 1.8 during late Vanilla that drastically changed the design of this battleground. Our community had no home to return to for more than 10 years. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

Honorable mention of AV legends: Jinro, Melg, Sotra and annonymous dev who gave us this pre-nerfed AV.
Here is the guide.







Alterac Valley Guide to Turtle WoW by Zvyrhol

- alliance
- horde


!!! DISCLAIMER !!!

This is the only relevant guide to Alterac Valley battleground on Turtle WoW. The server uses old map from Wow's patch 1.5 developed by Blizzard with all old features included that were removed later. Presented information and strategies might not be relevant on WoW Classic and other Vanilla private servers that rely on final patch 1.12.

Custom content or slightly modified things of Turtle WoW that were never present during OG Vanilla are marked next to chapters with [CUSTOM CONTENT] tag.




Introduction

Welcome to my guide to Alterac Valley! The guide concentrates all AV content in one place and serves purpose of AV encyclopedia. It also contains suggested and optimal strategy for both teams as well as tips from the guy who spent hundreds of hours on Turtle WoW's version of this battleground. Whether you are completely new player or OG Blizzard's fan that came here by accident through Google, you will find something useful here.



Lore background


Long ago, the warlock Gul'dan exiled a clan of orcs called the Frostwolves to a valley hidden deep in the heart of the Alterac Mountains. The Frostwolf Clan eked out a living until Thrall triumphantly united many of Azeroth’s orcs. The Frostwolves, however, chose to remain in the valley rather than joining Thrall in Orgrimmar – and their relative peace has since been challenged by the arrival of the dwarven Stormpike Expedition. The Stormpike Expedition’s desire to mine and plumb the underexplored caves for relics has invited conflict with the Frostwolf Clan, but opinions are divided on who struck first. Were the dwarves who arrived in the valley peaceful explorers who were massacred by the orcs, or did they plan to poach and conquer?


~ Blizzard Entertainment


How to enter Alterac Valley? [CUSTOM CONTENT]

On Turtle WoW you can access AV from any place in the world by clicking Battleground Finder icon (it's somewhere near the minimap by default). Level 51 is required to join.



How to win?

To win Alterac Valley battleground, your team must defeat enemy's faction boss: Vanndar Stormpike or Drek'Thar. Sounds like an easy job but it is not.





The boss sits in the building surrounded by his elite guard at the core of enemy base deep in enemy's territory. He has more than 100 000 HP and hits very hard.

The boss is guarded by Marshals/War Masters in his building. Practically, slaying boss without killing all of these guardians is impossible. So before you attack the boss, first you must lure out Marshals/War Masters and slay them.

But before you do it, you should first capture the graveyard at enemy's base - without respawn your team can't do much. The way to graveyard is filled with numerous NPCs so you won't have an easy job.

But it's not all. The base is also guarded by 2 Towers/Bunkers where the archers shoot anyone on a line of sight. Without these points burnt, the base will be hard to capture.

And before all of that, you must travel a long way to enemy's base without dying.


This guide will delve into all the details later.



REP & VENDORS:
*amazing pots*

*banner*

*mount*

*pre-raid bis items*


PVE OBJECTIVES

Armor Scraps to do: image of armor scraps icon, blacksmiths location

Armor Scraps are the quest items you can get from almost any enemy NPC in Alterac Valley. You can turn in large quantities of these to permanently upgrade your team's NPCs.

You turn them in to blacksmith NPC in your base (Murgot Deepforge in Alliance and Smith Regzar in Horde).

There are 4 levels of strength of your NPCs:
  • 1. Normal - game starts with this level of troops.
  • 2. Seasoned
  • 3. Veteran
  • 4. Champion
Each next level grants your NPCs more damage and health massively increasing your team's defense.

500 Armor Scraps are needed to upgrade troops to the next level - 1500 total. After turning in 500 Armor Scraps to the blacksmith, the new dialogue will appear. Click it so new stronger units will join the game.

After upgrading your troops to Champion ones, Armor Scraps become pointless because the Champion units stay in the match forever.

Good places to farm Armor Scraps are Coldtooth Mine and Irondeep Mine as well as surrounding of Captain Balinda and Captain Galvangar. Armor Scraps drop from Troggs, Kobolds and enemy NPCs.



Lokholar the Ice Lord and Ivus the Forest Lord to do: blood and crystal image, shaman/druid location, summon location




Lokholar the Ice Lord and Ivus the Forest Lord are probably the most iconic and powerful NPCs in the entire Alterac Valley. Each faction can summon their own mighty elemental that will lead their team to the victory.


How to summon?

Horde can collect Stormpike's Soldier Blood and Alliance can collect Storm Crystal from any enemy dead player or NPC. These items have 100% drop chance though only one random player nearby can loot these. If farm the items for yourself, it's recommended to loot enemy corpses away from your team mates.

Your team must bring 200x of these items to Primalist Thurloga in the cave in the Frostwolf Village or to Arch Druid Renferal who is located behind the Dun Baldar North Bunker.

You can ask these NPCs via dialogue to find out how many items are still needed to start the ritual of summoning. They won't directly tell you the number but below is the approximate formula:

First dialogue "still much work to do" tells you that your team has collected below 100 items, second one "I've made contact" informs you that your team has already turned in more than 100 but less than 150 items. Last dialogue "summon is near" informs you that there are less than 50 items needed to start the summon.

After turning in last item, the Shamans or Druids start moving to the place of summoning. Be ware. If they die to enemies during the escort, the summoning will fail. These locations are: small hill north of Galvangar's building or at the north-eastern edge of Field of Strife.

When Shamans or Druids are there, everyone in your team can click the circle to be part of the ritual of summoning. In order to summon the elemental, your team needs 10 clickers at the same time. When 10 people simultaneously click the circle, after a few seconds the Lokholar or Ivus appears and moves to the middle of the map.


The route

They stop in the Field of Strife for about 3 minutes.
They soon start moving into enemy's territory. Their next stop is Stormpike Graveyard or Frostwolf Village.
Next check-points are Aid Station or Relief Hut though usually enemy players kite them to the boss room so it rarely happens. Lastly they go to the Vanndar's or Drek'Thar's room.


Loot

When elemental dies, it drops some unique items. It's worth to note that Cold Forged Blade is the only item with this look in the entire game.



Tips
  • Elemental Lord is very good choice to break stalemate.
  • Good spots to farm Stormpike's Soldier Blood and Storm Crystals are Irondeep Mine and Coldtooth Mine supposing enemy team has captured these points. NPCs there have low HP and this area isn't crowded.
  • Once your team summons the elemental, you can buff them.
  • Entrance caves are good spots to kite elementals - your friendly NPCs will help you much.
  • Healing the elemental should be priority for every nearby player that has healing spells.
  • Hunters can kite the elementals. If your elemental is being kited by enemy Hunter, you should focus on the Hunter and stop him from ruining your team's effort.


Cavalry to do: cavalry banner in the title

Alterac Valley is the place where swift Frostwolves and mighty Alterac Rams dwell. These animals are used by Frostwolf Clan and Stormpike Guard as loyal mounts for their trained troops. Your team can tame these animals in order to summon the cavalry that will pierce through enemy defense.


How to summon?

In order to summon the cavalry, your team must meet 2 conditions:
  • Tame 25 Frostwolves or 25 Alterac Rams
  • Turn in 25 Alterac Ram Hides or 25 Frostwolf Hides
Part 1:
First, you must take the quest to tame Frostwolf or Alterac Ram. It can be picked up from Frostwolf Stable Master located in the stables east of Frostwolf Village or from Stormpike Stable Master who stays in the base of Dun Baldar.
You will receive the item that allows you to tame the animal. Use the item on the animal and after taming is complete, escort it back to the stables. Talk to NPC and turn in the quest.

Part 2:
Second, you must turn in 25 Alterac Ram Hides or 25 Frostwolf Hides to Frostwolf Wolf Rider Commander or to Stormpike Ram Rider Commander.
Unlike in the first part, you don't need to accept the quest to loot these items. You can loot all 25 items and then turn them in to that NPC.

Beware!
  • There is no way to find out exactly how many animals are still needed to be tamed. However, every 5 animals you tame, the animals appear in the stables. When stables are full - that means there are 5 more animals needed to be tamed. It's visual bug.
  • There is no way to find out exactly how many hides are still needed for your team to complete the objective. That's why it's recommended to turn in all 25 at once.
When both conditions are fulfilled, talk to the same Commander that gave you the quest for hides. Special dialogue will appear. Click it and observe how the cavalry charges and destroyes everything that stands in their way.


Tips
  • Riders move very fast and their route goes by all graveyards. Make sure to follow them and capture the graveyards along the way.
  • Although Riders don't as much damage as upgraded Ground Assaults, they stick together and are very tanky. If they all focus on one target, they can still one-shot an undergeared player.
  • The best strategy to fight cavalry is to slow and separate them.
  • Summoning cavalry is one of the easiest things low level players can do to influence the outcome of the game.
  • All Riders can be buffed.
  • It's possible to kill enemy's tamed Wolves or Rams that sit inside the stables to stop enemy from summoning the cavalry.


Infantry [CUSTOM CONTENT]



Infantry - also known as Ground Assaults - is the elite group of Reavers or Commandos that are the strongest soldiers of Frostwolf Clan or Stormpike Guard. They are possibly the strongest summonable units in the Alterac Valley.

The infantry consists of 11 NPCs that unlike the cavalry hit extremely hard and are more numerous. Their power scales with the upgrade level of your troops. Units with no upgrade have much less armor and deal significantly less damage. Thus, it's recommended to summon the infantry only if you upgrade the troops first.
Comparison:
  • Stormpike Commando (no upgrade):
    • Level: 56 -- 9986 HP - Damage: 335-432 - Armor: 2 699 - Resistance: 0
  • Champion Commando (Champion upgrade):
    • Level: 61 - 11632 HP - Damage: 559-720 - Armor: 4 091 - Resistance: 5

How to summon?

There are 3 steps your team must do in order to summon the infantry.
  • 1. Complete Irondeep Supplies quest or Coldtooth Supplies quest 4 times. [CUSTOM CONTENT]
  • 2. Activate dialogue and receive special item.
  • 3. Turn in the item to Warmaster Garrick or to Field Marshal Teravaine.


Step 1:
First, you must accept the quest from Frostwolf Quartermaster or from Stormpike Quartermaster. You have choice between going to the Coldooth Mine and Irondeep Mine - always select the Mine that is further away from your base. That's because completing "harder" quest once makes as much progress as completing easier one 4 times. It makes much difference if you want to save time. But if for some reason you wanted to farm supplies from the closer and safer Mine, you would have to complete the quest 16 times. That's a bit boring if you ask me!

[CUSTOM CONTENT] It's worth to note that these numbers are different from WoW Classic where 7 and 28 quests respectively are needed to summon the infantry.

Then, you must delve into the Mine and if it's not controlled by your team, you must kill enemy leader inside. Once it's done, you are able to grab supplies from the boxes. Go back to the Quartermaster once you grab all 10 supplies.

Step 2:
If you complete 4 turn ins, special dialogue will appear when you talk to the Quartermaster.
After clicking it, you receive Frostwolf Assault Orders or Stormpike Assault Orders. The item has 15 minutes duration so make sure not to hesitate and go to the next step.

Step 3:
After you receive the item, infatry's leader will spawn. You must bring him the orders you received from Quartermaster. You will find Warmaster Garrick north-west of Captain Galvangar's building and south of Snowfall Graveyard and Field Marshal Teravaine to the south of Stonehearth Bunker at the ballista. Complete the quest and infantry will spawn. Then, it will automatically move through the all enemy graveyards up to the last boss.


Tips
  • You can buff all of these units.
  • Running across the map takes much time. To save it, use Frostwolf Insignia or Stormpike Insignia to at least swiftly return to your base.
  • Infantry (if upgraded) is the most powerful summonable force in Alterac Valley. It's shines as stalemate-breaker.
  • Currently there is a bug on Turtle WoW that doesn't let you summon infantry more than once in the same match.
  • When you fight infantry, it's good to separate the units and kite them to your NPCs so they can help you.
  • Summoning can be synchronized with cavalry or elemental - combined power might be unstoppable.


Wing Commanders to do: image of 3 of them together

Also known as Aerial Assaults. Wing Commanders are special NPC located deep in enemy territory. When you talk with them, they start moving to your base. There are 3 Wing Commander for each side. If they successfully come back to your base without being killed, they will offer you special repeatable quest. Each Wing Commander offers other type of quest. The quest will require to turn in items dropped by enemy players. The quality of the item dropped by players is defined by their PvP rank.

You need to turn in following quantity of items in order to push this objective forward:
  • 120 Stormpike Soldier's Flesh or Frostwolf Soldier's Medal
  • 60 Stormpike Lieutenant's Flesh or Frostwolf Lieutenant's Medal
  • 30 Stormpike Commander's Flesh or Frostwolf Commander's Medal
WORK IN PROGRESS. Unfortunately this is the most unpopular objective on Turtle WoW - hardly ever completed by players. To be honest I don't know what these Wing Commanders do on this server after completing objective. So I decided not to copy-paste what other guides for WoW Classic state. I have seen this objective fulfilled only once on Turtle WoW. If you DO have knowledge, please contact me.



Ryson's All Seeing Eye [CUSTOM CONTENT] to do: Syndicate image, orb in troll's cave, turtle's AV map to note where syndicate hides and where is trolls cave

[CUSTOM CONTENT] Ryson's All Seeing Eye is side objective that was originally in Alterac Valley in patch 1.5 but was later removed and is unknown by most WoW Classic players. Turtle WoW restored this objective.

East of Field of Strife and behind Gnoll encampment there is a hidden cave in which Syndicate has a hideout. Their boss: Syndicate Master Ryson gives you a quest to recover Master Ryson's All Seeing Eye - powerful relic that was stolen by Winterax Trolls.

The item can be found inside Winterax Hold cave. Once you find the Eye, you must carry it back to the Master Ryson. The carrier of the eye, however, is cursed. You start to glow and your appearance will surely attracts other players' attention. Though you also get extra buff: with the Eye on you, you see invisible units from a distance. It's very useful buff if you want to detect enemy Rogues or Druids.


When you go back to Master Ryson and turn in the Eye, you will unlock new dialogue options.

The first one grants you 30 minutes buff that allows you to detect invisible units from a distance - without glow effect. This effect persists through death.

The second one is continuation of this objective. Master Ryson can give you a Ryson's Beacon that you can place in enemy base courtyard. Once placed there, it must be protected for one minute. When it's completed, Ryson's falcon spawns over enemy base and allows you to have view on enemy from your own base. This part of the objective is practically useless but it flavours how Syndicate can help you in fighting over Alterac Valley.


Tips
  • The quest can be completed once per AV match.
  • If you carry the Eye and mount up, you drop the item - then it can be repicked by anyone.
  • Sometimes it's not worth to complete the quest and keep the Eye for your team. For example to detect enemy stealthers inside your base.
  • When you die carrying the Eye, the Eye is dropped and can be repicked by anyone.
  • There is only one Eye.


Korrak the Bloodrager [CUSTOM CONTENT] to do: korrak image

[CUSTOM CONTENT] Korrak the Bloodrager was originally added to the game in patch 1.5 but was later removed and is unknown by most WoW Classic players. Turtle WoW restored his presence though with a few modifications to the original.

Korrak the Bloodrager is a powerful Troll that guards the Snowfall Graveyard and the bridge to Winterax Hold. He drops unique loot for example [Mark of Deflection]. His loot table is also shared with other world bosses so technically Korrak can be treated as a world boss.

Loot, however, isn't the only reason to kill Korrak. This mighty Troll is the objective of the quests: The Legend of Korrak and Korrak the Bloodrager. Blue items from these quests are one of the best items you can get in the game without raiding - and the quest can be completed at level 51!

[CUSTOM CONTENT] These quests also give you [Winterax Ritual Dagger] that is completely custom item made by Turtle WoW team. Moreover, once the quest is completed, you get access to repeatable version of this quest that gives you only the dagger: The Return of Korrak and Korrak the Everliving.

These quests can be picked up from NPCs in your base in Alterac Valley: Warmaster Laggrond and Lieutenant Haggerdin. To complete the quest, your team must kill Korrak and loot his skull. However, only one person can loot the skull each match - the drop goes to random person who has quest active.


Let's delve into how [Winterax Ritual Dagger] works. The description is mysterious and doesn't tell us much about the item.

First of all, the item can be activated only in Alterac Valley. When you use it, one effect is certain: you will die. The other effects depend whether you have Korrak's debuff on you. The debuff is named Bathed in Blood and you have it applied if Korrak dies close to you. The debuff passively does nothing and lasts 1 hour but is required in order to activate other effects of using the dagger.
  • If you use the dagger and you don't have debuff on you, you will die and nothing happens.
  • If you use the dagger and you have debuff on you:
    • if there is no friendly player close to you, you die and everyone in your team is summoned to the location you used the dagger.
    • if there is at least one friendly player close to you, they all get bonus 30% damage dealt buff for one minute.

Tips
  • Skull of Korrak drops to only one person in one game.
  • The dagger can summon whole team to your location. Rogues and Druids can stay in stealth to safely travel to enemy base and there summon their whole team. This way you can drastically shorten the length of the match and guarantee your team easy win.
  • If you die, the debuff fades from you making the item useless in that match.
  • You can stack the daggers in your inventory from multiple games. If you already have one dagger in your inventory before you kill the Korrak, you don't need to immediately return to your base to get next dagger - this can make your action quicker.
  • Winterax Ritual Dagger, in good hands, can deeply influence the outcome of the game and even let weaker team win the match.
  • Currently there is an exploit in the game that allows any ranged class to solo kill Korrak using bad pathing under the bridge.

*zinfizzlex & shredder*



Shredder is a unit that can be summoned via one item obtained from specific quest in Alterac Valley. This item is called [Zinfizzlex's Portable Shredder Unit]

https://database.turtle-wow.org/?item=17384. It allows you to summon and control a Shredder which is powerful elite with very high health pool. It causes you to control the unit but at any time you can break the control and order your Shredder to guard specific spot. Note that you can summon the Shredder only inside Alterac Valley.

author: Winrath
subject: Arena PvP is DEAD on Tel'Abim
content_md:
It's sad to see this but gradually we see that there is no incentive for people to do Arenas anymore.

People rather queue battleground for their honor instead of Arenas.

Arena PvP needs a serious revamp. My suggestions are:

 - Introduce  2v2 bracket
 - Introduce Rated Arenas
 - Update the Arena Gear (change the way the gear can be obtained)
 - Increase the arena honor gained substantially
 - Allow matchups between teams of the same faction
 - Spawn consumes on map to reveal invisibility to avoid griefers
 - Optimize the Queue so groups won't have to wait for solo queuers.

The introduction of rated arenas should be only for Tel'Abim, being a PvP server. This change will bring an influx of well needed players.

People that have the Arena gear on Tel'Abim took advantage of a bug when the server was launched and got their gear even before hitting 60. The fact that is almost impossible to get it now with the current system and queues on Tel'Abim makes the situation quite regrettable.

I know doing this comes with implications of balancing and gearing.
I know the team has already their plate full of TODO tasks.

BUT
Every single PvPer on the server would welcome these changes.
It will bring more diversity of things to do in the game.

Thank you

author: Thorngraze
subject: Increasing pvp participation and avoiding x-realm
content_md:
I am a Tel'Abim player, and this primarily concerns the situation on that realm.

I strongly oppose cross-realm PvP (and cross-realm features in general). I believe it weakens server community by matching you with players you never encounter outside battlegrounds. I like the fact that I'm participating in battlegrounds with the same people I run dungeons with or see idling in cities, as it enhances the world-building experience.

It still remains, there is a problem with PvP participation on Tel'Abim. While level 60 activity is decent for Warsong Gulch and Arathi Basin, there is an absence of matches for Arenas and Alterac Valley and participation at lower levels is practically non-existent. To help resolve this a really helpful feature would be displaying the number of queued players from both factions for each battleground.

This change would likely have a psychological effect, encouraging more players to queue when they see others waiting. This would particularly benefit lower-level battlegrounds and less popular options like AV and Arenas. Currently, I mainly queue for WSG, AB, and AV, but if I saw three others queued for Arena, I would queue knowing a match would start soon.

 **TLDR: Avoid cross-realm features! Instead display the number of players queueing to improve battleground participation.**

author: Gladeshadow
subject: Re: Increasing pvp participation and avoiding x-realm
content_md:
Have the devs given any indication of introducing cross realm play? To my knowledge, they have not. If anything, they've reiterated that they have no plans for it.

Tel'Abim's issue and it being a PvP realm has little to do with the battlegrounds but more to do with the players and the lack of **world** PvP structured scenarios. You go into battlegrounds and their intricacies, but the simple fact is that there is literally no reason to be on Tel'Abim for battlegrounds; just play on Nordanaar if those are desired. In fact, a bunch of people have already figured that out. Even the scenario you described of going to dungeons and idling in cities with the same people you PvP (battleground) with exists just as much on Nordanaar.

If you want to increase PvP participation, then you have to do what groups that advocate for it do. For example, guilds such as the Korkron Enforcers. And they do it *because they love pvp* rather than loving battlegrounds specifically. And press the devs to give an actual reason for Tel'Abim to exist.

I'm saying this as a fan of PvP realms. I started WoW some 20 years ago on a PvP realm and my only big experience with PvE has been on Nordanaar. Unfortunately, Blizzard gave next to no reason for world PvP in vanilla. The *only* world PvP that is structured in game that I can think of would be the towers in Eastern Plaguelands. So one scenario and extremely niche. If Turtle gave thought to adding features like this to pre-existing zones, for example Stonetalon Mountains, and made such features exclusive to the PvP realm, PvP participation might increase. And the scenario of world ganking, which is what we all know world PvP usually is, would be even more wasteful.

But if it's just battlegrounds, then Nordanaar exists to fulfill those desires.

author: Zvyrhol
subject: Ghost Queue Mafia EXPOSED
content_md:
[embed: https://www.youtube.com/embed/nDGOKXLkBb4]

This post relies on bug report submitted some time ago: <https://turtlecraft.gg/bug-report?id=9450>.
I would be grateful if you upvote this issue there.

Sometimes battlegrounds start with weird balance like 1 vs 15 in Arathi Basin or 1 vs 9 in Warsong Gulch.
Though it might be seemed as a bug, there is interesting theory that in fact games like these don't happen because of a bug but because of intentional activity of organised groups.

Background of the problem:

Warsong Gulch and Arathi Basin are specific battlegrounds because you can create a raid group and sign up everyone in this raid for one of these battlegrounds so everyone from your raid will join at the same time. In theory this mechanic might be the source of ghost queue bug and intentional abuse from some premade PvP groups to level PvP rank efficiently.

How to reproduce (as an organised PvP group):

- 1. Create Raid Group 1 that consist of real PvP premade of Faction X.

- 2. Create Raid Group 2 that consist of alts of the same PvP players from Raid Group 1 of Faction Y (on alt accounts).

- 3. When both Raid Groups are ready, the leaders of both groups join their group to selected battleground at the same time.

- 4a. With some luck, the server queue creates new battleground match with Raid Group 1 and Raid Group 2 as main participants.

- 5a. Everyone from Raid Group 1 enters the battleground while everyone from Raid Group 2 intentionaly doesn't enter.

- 6a. Raid Group 1 will have significant advantage in that match and will get free honor abusing the system.

- 4b. With no luck (for organised group), the Raid Group 2 won't face Raid Group 1 but some random players instead.

- 5b. The Raid Group 2 doesn't join the game and random players will have easy PvP game - that's the case in which most random people experienced this "ghost queue bug".

Facts that support this theory:

- This is possible in the game as long as PvP premade has lvl 60 alts of enemy faction on alt accounts.

- It's very unlikely that the server was coded that bad to allow 1 vs 15 situations.

- It's very unlikely for random people from one faction to mass decline - mathematically very unlikely.

- This method provides massive honor advantage for PvP rankers and makes their honor farming more efficient which is very important in the current PvP ranking system.

- From what I've seen, most of these 1 vs 10 screenshots were taken in Arathi Basin, some of them were taken in Warsong Gulch too. However, Alterac Valley that doesn't support joining as raid groups making this method impossible there. In fact this issue was never recorded there. There is no problem in Blood Ring because the game won't start if it isn't 3 vs 3. The issue was never recorded in Sunnyglade Valley.

This is only theory so the team should investigate the issue, maybe look at the logs to check if these groups really abused the queue system this way.
You might think that the best solution would be placing longer deserter debuff on characters that decline joining the battleground but it's bad solution - Raid Group of alts could join the game against Raid Group 1 and the result will be the same since their alts will be afk and the game would likely finish within 3 minutes if it's Arathi Basin.

The only solution would be monitoring such abusive activities through server logs and punish the alts that cause ghost games to start. Without the alts, organised PvP groups won't have easy honor farm making PvP ranking more fair for casual PvP enthusiasts.

Don't forget to upvote the issue here: <https://turtlecraft.gg/bug-report?id=9450>

author: Dracarusggotham
subject: PvP sets from later expansions
content_md:
I was thinking, a lot of people complain that the PvP sets are way inferior to the ones you get in Naxxramas and soon Karazhan, and that it's the main imbalance in PvP.

I was thinking that including sets from later expansions as PvP sets here would be a good idea, as it saves them design time, just dealing with the stat balance to match the Raid set it will counter.

It could be the Dungeon 3 set or the PvP sets released in TBC, the style doesn't deviate much and fits perfectly, maybe a retexture to vary the design a bit.

I think that would be a great way to start, no?

This also leaves them more time to design the PvE sets which I think the look is more important with the lore.

author: Zvyrhol
subject: P2W Battle Standards
content_md:
Dear Devs,

I understand that you don't pay much attention to PvP on this server.
However, there is one small issue that requires urgent fix because it makes the PvP "Pay To Win".

A few months ago Race Change Tokens returned to the donation shop.
There is one bug that allows you to buy both Battle Standards that can be used in battlegrounds simultaneously.
This bug is only accessible to people who pay their real money to the server.

This Battle Standard works like Shaman's totem: it has 1500 HP and it increases your party's total health by 15% for 2 minutes.
This item existed by default in Vanilla.
Actually, there were 2 items: one accessible to the Horde and other one accessible to the Alliance.
However, in Vanilla you couldn't change your faction by changing race because it's Turtle WoW custom feature.

With return of the Race Change Token in the shop, players can purchase for example Horde Battle Standard with their first Orc, then switch to the Dwarf and purchase Alliance Battle Standard.

Then, these players are able to place both of these Battle Standards in battlegrounds at the same time.
The bug isn't still well known, however, it has been reported already on a bug tracker.
Here you can find all the details: <https://turtlecraft.gg/bug-report?id=10869>

What deeply concerns me though is that the issue was reported 3 months ago.
I wouldn't be writing this post if you fixed that bug. It seems to be easy to fix.
I don't assume that you intentionally let this bug be to intentionally allow P2W on the server so the people interested in PvP spend extra $$$ on your server.
In contrast I assume you tend to ignore important PvP bugs without even understanding them.

By the way, it's not the only bug related with PvP that leaves its content broken.
There is one bugged quest in Alterac Valley that doesn't let you buff your team more than once per character (<https://turtlecraft.gg/bug-report?id=6475>). Bug is 1 year old and still not fixed.
A few days ago we finally got queue bug fixed after 2 years.
About 1 year ago there was new meta to play Alterac Valley discovered that relied on using backdoor that was accessible to only one faction - it was fixed after a few months of abusing instead of days.

What I mean is the PvP issues are being (if ever) fixed after unreasonably long amount of time.

Please fix Battle Standards bug as fast as possible. I think everyone doesn't want such P2W to be available on Turtle WoW.

author: Zvyrhol
subject: New AV meta discovered
content_md:
One week ago devs finally fixed one custom quest that is obtainable in Alterac Valley. Before the update, this quest actually didn't work properly: it could be completed only once.

- **Korrak the Everliving** and The **Return of Korrak** are now repeatable quests. However, the **Skull of Korrak** is no longer a party drop.

The quest can be taken from Warmaster Laggrond or Lieutenant Haggerdin in your faction's base in AV. Your objective is to kill Korrak the Bloodrager and loot his skull. However, skull can be picked up only by one random player near Korrak. If you are the only player with the quest, you will have 100% drop chance.
It's important to have debuff applied when Korrak dies near you. This debuff is essential to properly perform the ritual in the future. It has blood icon and 1 hour duration.
When you obtain the Skull of Korrak, go back to your base and turn it in to the quest giver. Then, you will receive [[Winterax Ritual Dagger]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=50743)

Winterax Ritual Dagger is the item you can click to perform the ritual. You must have the debuff on you - otherwise the ritual won't work. When you click it, it can do 2 things based on whether you have any friendly players nearby:

 1) if there is NO a friendly player close to you:
- You die. Everyone in your team in AV receives the summon to the place you are in.
 2) if there is a friendly player close to you:
- You die. Everyone close to you gets 30% damage buff and movement speed bonus for one minute.
This video is self-explanatory why I think this item becomes the new meta in AV.

[embed: https://www.youtube.com/embed/xqTsfb9fRIU]

As you can see the carrier of the Winterax Ritual Dagger can possibly summon everyone to the last graveyard and end the game in next 10 minutes.

EDIT - Patch 1.18.0

It seems the dagger was nerfed in patch 1.18 although it isn't noted anywhere in patch notes. Now to receive the summon, you must have "Bathed in Blood" debuff on you - the debuff you get when your character is close to Korrak's death. Practically, it means not everyone will receive the summon.

So in theory this meta can still be exploited but it requires much more team work. When the game starts, everyone from your team should go to Korrak instead of Stonehearth/Iceblood GY.  That is needed in order for your team to be summoned later. It's hard task because usually people in AV aren't well coordinated - everyone joins solo and some people don't even read chat.

subject: Re: New AV meta discovered

It seems the dagger was nerfed in patch 1.18 although it isn't noted anywhere in patch notes. Now to receive the summon, you must have "Bathed in Blood" debuff on you - the debuff you get when your character is close to Korrak's death. Practically, it means not everyone will receive the summon.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: CC Duration in PVP
content_md:
The pvp trinket being able to remove everything has had major impacts for classes that rely on their CC.

For instance, in a battle between mage & rogue, the mage now being able to get out of a kidney even with blink on CD makes kidney shot almost impossible to get value from.

Same with fears on shaman. Grounding and tremor already made fears rather weak / hard to apply with a shaman in combat. Having a second lifeline makes even deathcoil>kill totem>fear an unreliable/non option.

On the topic of deathcoil. That spell was never meant to be trinketable. Warlocks lack of personal defense is in parts due to deathcoils powerlevel.
By just changing the insignia you change all kinds of matchups majorly, as the class that has to apply the CC has a harder time.

PvP is in a unbalanced spot, and while the insignia itself is just a teeny tiny piece of the puzzle, it was adjusted without taking a look at each possible interaction. While everyone being able to get out of CC is nice, that also means everybody has go be able to fight a fair fight without relying on it. And in the case of Rogue or Hunter, these classes rely on CC more than a Shaman or Retpally. So buffing anti CC capabilities hurts them more

Long-lasting and even some fragile CC that is _also_ with a long duration have a mechanic called Heartbeat Resist, which thankfully at least appears to work here, if maybe a bit too unlucky when it comes to relying on it to occur exactly when you need it.

Aside from obvious suggestions like the Skull of Impending Doom and Free Action Potion, there's Lucidity Potion, pre-using Restorative Potion for a tick to Dispel a CC you expect to hit you soon that can be removed by it, various non-Engineering Consumables and even Engineering-made ones that do not actually require Engineering, there is also just Range "dancing" which indirectly mitigates not only CC but even DMG (VS Rogues outside of Blind, you can off-Range Gouge, Kidney, Dismantle if no Weapon Chain or Stronghold or Grips; VS Warrior you can avoid non-AoE Spells like Whirlwind such as MS, OP, etc., can deadzone for no Auto Attack or Intercept, and much more). Hell even in teamplay you can use Anti-Venoms on a friendly to remove Blinds and so on, Engineers can utilize Recombobulators on them to remove Poly _and_ heal (the heal still works even without a Poly on the recipient), and even solo as a desperation tactic or to stall, I pretty much don't even see anyone utilize Petrification Flasks despite their notoriety.

Some CC is actually already nerfed. For example, not that anybody plays Prot Warrior PvP, but Concussion Blow used to be a 5s Stun, but here it's 2s which is laughable and only serves to gimp Kidney and even the Warrior's own Intercept. For Arms, Improved Hamstring is gone, and Counterattack is not only terrible and not worth, but even its own Root is 3s rather than 5s.

Vanilla PvP was a big part of WoW from the start, but it was also quite flawed in some parts, yet still, a lot of aspects like each Class' CC and overall how one could be a counter to the other and that be countered by a different one entirely, how that also results in teamwork being all the more important to both combine old-fashioned XvX PvP design and the MMORPG aspect of many people teaming up and deciding to go against a different group (BGs etc., nobody really does WPvP Raids like Tarren Mill or Crossroads in Nordanaar though, and Cross-Faction has further hurt organic encounters). CC2's problem, however, has made stuff a lot burstier, and the PvP Trinket change has granted an extra escape with a shortened CD to everyone while CC-reliant Classes now have to deal with that fact. 3m CD removing nearly if not all CC compared to OG Vanilla's per-Class removes on 5m is a huge difference.

All in all I feel as though people want things to be like an awkward mix of WotLK burst but also have rapid-fire CC and CD reliance like in MoP, in an older iteration of the game that had both inherent old-fashioned design visions and its own flaws (intentional or otherwise), and this server's intent appears to be... at least... trying to... somewhat follow those principles (albeit CC2 and new gear/old gear changes have resulted in stupid outcomes by comparison).

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: Nerf Shamans and Warlock
content_md:
Shamans have counterplays and even some counters but a lot of them can be mitigated or fully negated - - like even Disarming Enhas immediately flops the moment you see "Immune". Also the fact that other Shamans even if they are Disarmed and pressured, can still hit you for big Earth Shock Crits or LBs/CLs like they're LARP-ing as Raiden or Thor so long as they have already applied Buffs on themselves, Debuffs on you, and Purged you naked save for literally your clothes off of you - - you can't do much against that other than Nature Resist/Absorb/Reflect and that is implying that doesn't get Purged just before anyway.

The PvP Trinket buffs have also allowed them to benefit from it just like any other Class now does, which actually can be negative when fighting against one as well, because that one important CC you might be banking on is very likely to be removed if it's not already going to be prevented or even removed by either FAP for 30s or LAP for 5s, or even LIP for 6s + full Physical Immunity.

... Meanwhile Warrior has become a bigger meme than it originally was, where it only really excels as a self-healing Fury-Prot Tank hoping that the mix of Blood Craze, Blood Drinker and Last Stand + Lifegiving + Consumables (implying no Purge on what can be removed) will _maybe_ let them bot against an opponent long enough to either outlast them or make them feel so bored that they give up anyway; otherwise Warriors have become bigger Execute spammers due to nonsensical Execute buffs making them dumb their own playstyle more than before the moment 20% HP hits. CC2 was clearly meant for endgame PvE only (and some Classes only became more OP and dumber to play), whereas in PvP... man has the imbalance become worse as a result.

Warlock with global easy empowered CoEx and more (on top of OG strong kit like Seduce, Fear spam to Immunity and unlucky with Heartbeat Resists, Inferno, Death Coil, etc.) as Shaman has more burst (hello giga-Windfury and random deleting Earth Shock Crit and even stronger kills with suicide-induced Lightning Shield) and control and even Shaman Tank becoming way more viable here, as most if not all Classes also have more burst that is actually behind the facade of more gear reliance than OG Vanilla... yeah that's not balanced, even for Vanilla. I'd say this goes beyond Shaman and Warlock but still on-topic, I'd say it's definitely a problem.

Meanwhile Warrior with no Improved Hamstring, Counterattack is not a good replacement, Hamstring CD (almost killing proc fishing) , Execute CD (needing a Fury Talent as Arms), overall non-gear-reliant Damage is weaker (why change Rend scaling or remove MS' bonus DMG just to give it a bit more % in Weapon DMG), Slam is like Cataclysm Slam only it takes a week even with movement casting and the Swing Timer continuation changes nothing when it comes to the fact that you must still use it after swinging (you can hardly use it after a CC like Intercept due to how long it takes with the little time you still have on top of needing to make sure you have just swung or stop your Attack)... but hey at least we get to spam more Executes and make them stronger than originally in Raids that are already being steamrolled - - that's great, right?

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: Nerf Shamans and Warlock
content_md:
In this server, arguably, it's Shaman.

Warrior's changes have mainly (in PvP) resulted in:
 - Arms spamming even more Execute than before (PvE Raid change since in PvP you either struggle to outlive or race others to 20% or simply kill them outright with Execute the same way as pre-CC2 meaning it's hardly even a noticeable change compared to the nerfs in other aspects);
 - Fury mainly being a tankier Spec if built into Blood Craze + Blood Drinker + Last Stand etc. (basically a self-sustaining Tank that needs less carry so this makes things redundant in this context as well);
 - Protection is... not PvP-viable anymore (Concussion Blow down from five seconds to TWO SECONDS ON ITS STUN - - WHY?!).

Shaman? Relatively _similar_ in the form of a mixed bag of changes (positive and negative both), but now Shaman Tank is more viable, which bleeds into being PvP-viable as well. Enhancement still rolls the casino and if it wins, it gets big numbers, you get a shortcut to a nearby Graveyard (which usually isn't nearby at all). If they have support from others, then that means more of their Mana is spent towards either DMG or CC, not Healing (how the hell would you spend extra unused Rage as a Warrior when you can't even use Hamstring more than once every six seconds).

Warrior feels like less of a reward to carry with support now, because they're just not as good. They're basically more of a Damage bot with the occasional Mortal Strike (if Arms), which is not so special anymore, when you have others now doing the same or at least similar, but with less effort and more failsaves.

This Is an absolutely needed change ( you cant fart on the 5hp totem and kill It like any Half decent player does btw)

Piercing Howl is 10yd -50% but for 6s and is a Physical Spell - - it can be Resisted and you can even be Silenced from using it (not that anyone would bother using a Silence on you unless he's playing 5D chess). Booming Voice here is altered to affect all Shout Spells including Howl, meaning up to 16yd (not even accounting for Leeway on top)... but it is in most cases redundant as you want to stay close and only dance relatively out of Range if VS Melee, plus you would need to sacrifice other (better) Talents to get that benefit, oftentimes being suboptimal. I have used Booming Voice but switched out of it due to needed Damage potential I had to give up for that. Not only that, but Howl is now... a crutch; due to how Hamstring is here, Howl is all the more important, which is a problem - - Hamstring is baseline, no Spec can alter it, Howl is a Talent.

What Booming Voice on Shouts is DEFINITELY good at... is anti-Stealth, extra Range on Intimidating Shout, and a niche potential for getting yourself and others into Combat with a wider Battle Shout if ANYONE is in Combat - - no Sap, as a result. But that is not enough, or rather, no - - that is not what is needed. We need to fight the new higher burst with burst of our own - - said burst coming from Execute spam in PvE, which does not apply in PvP. The rest of the kit is weakened. We can't have crutches. A crutch wouldn't be the answer nor should it be. We have lost sources of control (Hamstring/Improved Hamstring etc.) and even a bit of baseline survivability (base Shield Block is worse than Vanilla base Shield Block, making non-Shield builds less defensively capable). So we need more Damage. Bit of a smoothbrain method. But that's exactly what's happened anyway - - Class has been dumbed down, non-Execute performance is somewhat weaker on average all so that in PvE Execute just deals more Damage (because in PvP it just overkills with the buff here, and overkill is wasted Damage, so it's not really a usable buff).

As for Rage dump, we really don't.

First off, Hamstring is barely a filler anymore. You cannot refresh Snares or apply RNG Roots, nor can you try to fish for procs reliably. Slam is so slow that even talented it is not PvP-reliable for use (takes longer, cannot use it as often within an Intercept Stun compared to Vanilla, you can't avoid Melee attacks during a cast so you hurt your passive defenses). Sunder costs 5R less but that is inconsequential as in PvP you usually do not have the time to stack it and even if you did you would need control/survivability to make time (and we lost those), on top of needing more burst to fight against burst now, which means Sunder is not in support of that (not immediately). Pummel is... well, Pummel; you don't blow it on just anyone if there's a Caster nearby, and the most it can be useful for is getting a Crit off to apply Deep Wounds and if you have Hand of Justice that you proc it through Pummel (it will not proc Sword Specialization, whereas Hamstring can, same as Sunder and applying Rend both CANNOT, which is why Hamstring's nerf is so much bigger than originally perceived).

Then you have Whirlwind. Whirlwind is the same. Problem: Berserker Stance. Swapping Stances dumps Rage. You can keep up to 25R with 5/5 Stance Mastery in Tier 1 Arms. You still lose up to 75 each time. Another tidbit: +10% Damage INTAKE in Berserker Stance. Considering burst is higher here, you definitely don't want to stay in that Stance despite benefitting from +3% Crit. So you need to lose Rage, do Whirlwind, swap again, thus lose more Rage (unless VS a Rogue or Fear Class for Berserker Rage).

With the above last point, you can't even reliably use Heroic Strike or Cleave to consume your own next Auto Attack for more Damage as you will likely switch Stances for something thus lose Rage from that AND the Ability so you will need to remake that Rage thus HS/Cleave like that in an attempt to Rage-dump would actually screw you over. The ONLY time in this server you get to ACTUALLY do that is... Execute. Execute was already strong. The buff made it overkill in PvP in most cases, which is wasted Damage - - yes you can dump all the Rage but what's so useful about what is tantamount to being eye-candy considering OG Execute could already kill post-20% in PvP with ease and CC2 Execute does the same just with more Overkill Damage?

And just to get it out of the way in advance just in case: no, Counterattack is not good even as a Rage dump. It sucks. YOU CAN'T EVEN USE IT MOST OF THE TIME.

The problem with Shaman VS Warrior in a Group scenario where either is supported is the comparison of the Shaman as though you're expecting it to be a Warrior or to be played like one. First of all, no, secondly as pointed out multiple times the Warrior is not as flexible, is more braindead now, non-Execute Damage is worse while Execute Damage is redundant in PvP since it already used to kill just fine pre-CC2, so it's like... there's less in it when carrying the Warrior. The Shaman is a hybrid and is more flexible and can do more and at best during a carry they can be more reckless and try to pump more all the while they can have fallbacks due to what I just said while the Warrior DOESN'T (the Warrior CANNOT even try to save someone in the back lines by trying to get an Improved Hamstring off on an enemy, I WONDER WHY?).

Not that this is to say, "Don't support Warriors anymore", or, "Warrior sucks in group fights" - - no, of course not. Rather, it's not as good anymore... which doesn't even make sense, because you'd think, you'd assume, you'd feel it would be right, to instead be BETTER now, but it is NOT.

If you really ever did pvp in your Life that was a well known fact in the community and most wanted ( and After got) that change. Totems are clunky mechanic. This Is an absolutely needed change ( you cant fart on the 5hp totem and kill It like any Half decent player does btw)
Piercing Howl is 10yd -50% but for 6s and is a Physical Spell - - it can be Resisted and you can even be Silenced from using it (not that anyone would bother using a Silence on you unless he's playing 5D chess). Booming Voice here is altered to affect all Shout Spells including Howl, meaning up to 16yd (not even accounting for Leeway on top)... but it is in most cases redundant as you want to stay close and only dance relatively out of Range if VS Melee, plus you would need to sacrifice other (better) Talents to get that benefit, oftentimes being suboptimal. I have used Booming Voice but switched out of it due to needed Damage potential I had to give up for that. Not only that, but Howl is now... a crutch; due to how Hamstring is here, Howl is all the more important, which is a problem - - Hamstring is baseline, no Spec can alter it, Howl is a Talent.

What Booming Voice on Shouts is DEFINITELY good at... is anti-Stealth, extra Range on Intimidating Shout, and a niche potential for getting yourself and others into Combat with a wider Battle Shout if ANYONE is in Combat - - no Sap, as a result. But that is not enough, or rather, no - - that is not what is needed. We need to fight the new higher burst with burst of our own - - said burst coming from Execute spam in PvE, which does not apply in PvP. The rest of the kit is weakened. We can't have crutches. A crutch wouldn't be the answer nor should it be. We have lost sources of control (Hamstring/Improved Hamstring etc.) and even a bit of baseline survivability (base Shield Block is worse than Vanilla base Shield Block, making non-Shield builds less defensively capable). So we need more Damage. Bit of a smoothbrain method. But that's exactly what's happened anyway - - Class has been dumbed down, non-Execute performance is somewhat weaker on average all so that in PvE Execute just deals more Damage (because in PvP it just overkills with the buff here, and overkill is wasted Damage, so it's not really a usable buff).

As for Rage dump, we really don't.

First off, Hamstring is barely a filler anymore. You cannot refresh Snares or apply RNG Roots, nor can you try to fish for procs reliably. Slam is so slow that even talented it is not PvP-reliable for use (takes longer, cannot use it as often within an Intercept Stun compared to Vanilla, you can't avoid Melee attacks during a cast so you hurt your passive defenses). Sunder costs 5R less but that is inconsequential as in PvP you usually do not have the time to stack it and even if you did you would need control/survivability to make time (and we lost those), on top of needing more burst to fight against burst now, which means Sunder is not in support of that (not immediately). Pummel is... well, Pummel; you don't blow it on just anyone if there's a Caster nearby, and the most it can be useful for is getting a Crit off to apply Deep Wounds and if you have Hand of Justice that you proc it through Pummel (it will not proc Sword Specialization, whereas Hamstring can, same as Sunder and applying Rend both CANNOT, which is why Hamstring's nerf is so much bigger than originally perceived).

Then you have Whirlwind. Whirlwind is the same. Problem: Berserker Stance. Swapping Stances dumps Rage. You can keep up to 25R with 5/5 Stance Mastery in Tier 1 Arms. You still lose up to 75 each time. Another tidbit: +10% Damage INTAKE in Berserker Stance. Considering burst is higher here, you definitely don't want to stay in that Stance despite benefitting from +3% Crit. So you need to lose Rage, do Whirlwind, swap again, thus lose more Rage (unless VS a Rogue or Fear Class for Berserker Rage).

With the above last point, you can't even reliably use Heroic Strike or Cleave to consume your own next Auto Attack for more Damage as you will likely switch Stances for something thus lose Rage from that AND the Ability so you will need to remake that Rage thus HS/Cleave like that in an attempt to Rage-dump would actually screw you over. The ONLY time in this server you get to ACTUALLY do that is... Execute. Execute was already strong. The buff made it overkill in PvP in most cases, which is wasted Damage - - yes you can dump all the Rage but what's so useful about what is tantamount to being eye-candy considering OG Execute could already kill post-20% in PvP with ease and CC2 Execute does the same just with more Overkill Damage?

And just to get it out of the way in advance just in case: no, Counterattack is not good even as a Rage dump. It sucks. YOU CAN'T EVEN USE IT MOST OF THE TIME.

The problem with Shaman VS Warrior in a Group scenario where either is supported is the comparison of the Shaman as though you're expecting it to be a Warrior or to be played like one. First of all, no, secondly as pointed out multiple times the Warrior is not as flexible, is more braindead now, non-Execute Damage is worse while Execute Damage is redundant in PvP since it already used to kill just fine pre-CC2, so it's like... there's less in it when carrying the Warrior. The Shaman is a hybrid and is more flexible and can do more and at best during a carry they can be more reckless and try to pump more all the while they can have fallbacks due to what I just said while the Warrior DOESN'T (the Warrior CANNOT even try to save someone in the back lines by trying to get an Improved Hamstring off on an enemy, I WONDER WHY?).

Not that this is to say, "Don't support Warriors anymore", or, "Warrior sucks in group fights" - - no, of course not. Rather, it's not as good anymore... which doesn't even make sense, because you'd think, you'd assume, you'd feel it would be right, to instead be BETTER now, but it is NOT.

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: Nerf Shamans and Warlock
content_md:
They would need to see the value in it. I don't think they do. The community from my own experience is also at times unwelcoming.

RP-PvE is their main appeal. Lots of changes have been made to that end. Some of them have hurt PvP. Even what has been reverted or further changed for the sake of balance, was more for PvE equality and rarely for that of PvP (saying this so that nobody assumes none ever were for PvP's sake -- just, not enough).

Lunatic can also not be used as a point. See, for example, Nordanaar; L1s are so inflated that they can just fight L20s. Problem: not enough L20s who are PvP-marked. Also, people are generally anti-PvP, anti-War-Mode, take offense to PvP, see someone twinking and think they're a loser (true if he's a lowbie-camping bully, sure). Due to this limited activity... Lunatics stay in Starting Areas. That is where people can take War Mode. Then you have for example, Human players doing that, entering the Kobold mine within Northshire, and bam -- dead to a Level 1 Rogue Lunatic. Hence WM's notoriety of being a "noob trap". They're just camping there. That's... it, whenever it's not BGs -- which are not quite active, as this is very niche of a Challenge, so it just leads to... more camping.

Also, just... why... why does Lunatic even exist? What was the point of it? People really spent time and effort on this... instead of actual PvP design -- be it pre-60 or 60 or let alone endgame 60 PvP -- the actual foci? Really...?

This is part of why R14 is less rewarding and desirable here and PvE instead is all the moreso? Like why grind towards R14 with the ongoing over-competitive Chinese-esque Honor farming (despite recent changes to combat abuse on a massive scale that was being done), when you can just get Naxxramas gear -- considering even, say, Warrior Damage Dealers get their own separate T3 Set, which my goodness is it strong. Only the R14 Weapons MIGHT still be good (hello Kara40), but then that makes them the tip of the iceberg and just not as rewarding for the whole grind -- especially considering that by then, on the flipside, you might get TUB, Ashkandi, KR, UC, CAB, etc. (and this is just comparing Two-Handed Swords alone -- not even mentioning MoM, EoI, etc.).

This place needs actual designer persons interested in PvP, Class balance, and knowledge in PvP on the side of both Equipment for PvP, and Class performance in PvP. I feel that there might actually be none -- from my own uneducated perspective. Even if there are... I have no idea what the hell they're doing (they themselves probably don't know).
content_html:
They would need to see the value in it. I don't think they do. The community from my own experience is also at times unwelcoming.

RP-PvE is their main appeal. Lots of changes have been made to that end. Some of them have hurt PvP. Even what has been reverted or further changed for the sake of balance, was more for PvE equality and rarely for that of PvP (saying this so that nobody assumes none ever were for PvP's sake -- just, not enough).

Lunatic can also not be used as a point. See, for example, Nordanaar; L1s are so inflated that they can just fight L20s. Problem: not enough L20s who are PvP-marked. Also, people are generally anti-PvP, anti-War-Mode, take offense to PvP, see someone twinking and think they're a loser (true if he's a lowbie-camping bully, sure). Due to this limited activity... Lunatics stay in Starting Areas. That is where people can take War Mode. Then you have for example, Human players doing that, entering the Kobold mine within Northshire, and bam -- dead to a Level 1 Rogue Lunatic. Hence WM's notoriety of being a "noob trap". They're just camping there. That's... it, whenever it's not BGs -- which are not quite active, as this is very niche of a Challenge, so it just leads to... more camping.

Also, just... why... why does Lunatic even exist? What was the point of it? People really spent time and effort on this... instead of actual PvP design -- be it pre-60 or 60 or let alone endgame 60 PvP -- the actual foci? Really...?

This is part of why R14 is less rewarding and desirable here and PvE instead is all the moreso? Like why grind towards R14 with the ongoing over-competitive Chinese-esque Honor farming (despite recent changes to combat abuse on a massive scale that was being done), when you can just get Naxxramas gear -- considering even, say, Warrior Damage Dealers get their own separate T3 Set, which my goodness is it strong. Only the R14 Weapons MIGHT still be good (hello Kara40), but then that makes them the tip of the iceberg and just not as rewarding for the whole grind -- especially considering that by then, on the flipside, you might get TUB, Ashkandi, KR, UC, CAB, etc. (and this is just comparing Two-Handed Swords alone -- not even mentioning MoM, EoI, etc.).

This place needs actual designer persons interested in PvP, Class balance, and knowledge in PvP on the side of both Equipment for PvP, and Class performance in PvP. I feel that there might actually be none -- from my own uneducated perspective. Even if there are... I have no idea what the hell they're doing (they themselves probably don't know).

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: Perfectly solve the PVP power creep caused by equipment.
content_md:
Current state is that PvE is easier to stomp, making PvE gear easier to obtain.

In PvP, at least on Nordanaar, there is a serious problem with Honor grind competition -- which actually used to be even worse due to targeted abuse and exploiting of the BG queue system, but even after some alterations, it still stands quite strong there. This causes other people who don't already belong to this higher end of the division -- spending countless hours like this is a job -- to just breathe dust. The sole reason this is even a problem at all (why should it be when of course people who put effort into this would deserve it, right?) is actually pretty simple: it does not in fact take skill to grind towards R14. Just a lot of time. A lot of... time being bored.

Furthermore, PvP gear is lagging behind PvE gear, and coupled with the above, makes PvP gear less worthwhile. This includes even custom PvP Equipment, the likes of anti-Crit-Damage Items and so on -- their Stats are found lacking for the most part, with the -%CDMG being the main takeaway. What if this Damage is not a Crit? Why sacrifice your own Stats for this one gimmick? This is insufficient as a makeshift Resilience "Stat" in this server, at least for the time being.

And to give the worst discrepancy: old PvE gear changes and new PvE additions (varied Tier Sets per Spec or at least Role at worst) are so goddamn strong, that it's simply better for PvP.

On top of it all, this is especially true for a select few Classes and even some Specs in particular: an immediate example being Warrior. You just get PvE. You go in there and mop up. That's it. If you want PvP dominance, you basically do PvE.

That is not proper.

author: Hexagun81
subject: Re: New to turtlewow, how is PvP?
content_md:
I play a 60 warrior, rank 7, with some raid gear and I would describe PVP (specifically BGs) as astonishingly bad for everyone but more especially melee classes. I'm not sure why I keep playing. It's not that I suck or that's it's too hard. I'm doing well. It's just disgusting that all classes spend most of their time slowed down, immobilized or stunned, and usually go from full health to zero in that state, within seconds.

It's quite obvious that crits and CC are out of control. It's pathetic. Without ~50+ hours of BG experience, good gear and frequent use of consumables/trinkets, you will MELT.

I'm pretty sure that an incredible amount of newbies that tried BGs were so disgusted by it that they never tried again. NEVER.

I see players go from full HP to zero in TWO SECONDS if not one second in every single BG I play. 30 seconds later I see their face and the same thing happens again even if the player is careful. ONE second after the first stun, he's dead. Some random dude 30 yards away pressed 3 buttons, dealt 4k damage, laughed. For the 10000th time, always in the same order.

No good gear = one of the most stupid and unfair multiplayer combat I have witnessed in 30 years of gaming.

Like i said, I'm not even complaining. I'm doing fine with the skill/gear I currently have. It's just insanely unforgiving for beginners.

I like hardship, adversity. Don't enter the world of 5+ PVP encounters if you don't like hardship.

author: Triunfax
subject: Re: New to turtlewow, how is PvP?
content_md:
This is hands down the most miserable PvP experience I’ve ever had—absolutely unbalanced and infuriating to the point where you’ll desperately wish Blizzard would step in and fix it. It’s even worse than SoD. If PvP is your focus, do yourself a favor and only roll Paladin, Shaman, or Warrior. Don’t get me wrong—you’ll still suffer and have a terrible time, but at least with these classes, you might snag a few kills in the brief 3-second window before getting obliterated so hard it sends you flying out of your chair.

TurtleWoW overhauled every class with new abilities, rotations, talents, and flashy upgrades, but somehow, it never occurred to them that these changes would turn PvP into a split-second burst fest. They gave everyone insane damage but did nothing to improve survivability, so now combat is over in a blink. It’s honestly disappointing, considering all the effort they put into the expansion, but it’s clear PvE is their only priority. So if you’re hoping for a good PvP experience… well, don’t.

Which is why multiple times already have I made the point that CC2 here has resulted in imbalance that's worse even by Vanilla's own ancient standards.

Also, the Shamans in question being in Naxxramas gear makes perfect sense. You and at least one other person here have already pointed out why, but, still, let's humor the idea anyway, for those who still don't get it.

See, Naxxramas Sets in this server have multiple variations per Class now, unlike how they were in Vanilla -- Warrior T3, for example, is Tank, but here, it has a Damage Dealer version as well. And it is busted. LOOK AT HOW MUCH AGILITY AND CRIT THEY GET. JESUS. I've complained that overall non-Execute Damage feels lower here due to CC2 and more after it, on top of loss of some CC and a bit of survivability, making them dumber and not as good UNTIL Execute, at which point BOOM, back to being amazing -- because Execute here got a buff it DIDN'T NEED. However... every point I've made can be IGNORED... the moment the Warrior gets T3 DpS. Why? Because LOOK AT THE STATS. My arguments about Class braindeath and weaker pre-Execute DMG DO NOT MATTER, because the gear CARRIES until the problems DO NOT MATTER. Basically it looks like they are NOT THERE. Remove the Naxx gear, and they ARE THERE. Basically, good game, more gear carry than original Vanilla, pretty much hide new glaring flaws behind inflated Stats.

Shaman, in this case, is pretty much the same; originally for Restoration, there is now also one for Enhancement, and one for Elemental.

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: nerf shamans
content_md:
> **Kroxoman wrote: Fri Mar 28, 2025 7:24 am**
> So everyone should be playing warlocks mages and shamans and fuck warriors we will do raids and so on without them thats your point ? Why the hell is there that class if it is not meant to be played when it gets destroyed in PVP.

Aye, when other Classes are better, it discourages the people playing the ones that at least _feel_ are not -- and not to mention, are not fun.

For instance, I've seen too much of the same stuff being regurgitated by tons of people, and it's all gotten samey and droning.

I can keep getting better, amass more gear, but that won't change that it's how the scene is.

I constantly bump into Arcane and Frost Mages exercizing their absurd power, but never Fire ones -- why is that? Well, because Fire just isn't as good. Instead, I just keep seeing the same ones who press two to three buttons and call it a day after melting you.

And to dispel bias, I have the same gripe with Warrior; Protection is no longer PvP-viable, because its kit got gutted for the scene. You will never see a Protection Warrior. The Spec simply got killed off when it comes to PvP.

Arms also has... pretty much one build. Arms with sub-Prot Talents just isn't good when you remember that Hamstring is still nerfed and you more or less need Piercing Howl. You can get Improved Intervene from Protection, but Intervene shares its Cooldown with Intercept, and you ditch Piercing Howl and _more_ just to get that -- which, that effect that it gives you can pretty much get almost fully the same way by using Free Action, Living Action, and even Limited Invulnerability (circumstances matter here). That style is basically more demanding of someone carrying you just to make it work. So, I wouldn't even count that as a build to invest in when it's guaranteed to only really work with a carry, and even then, with how things are designed and "balanced" now, it's just redundant -- you'd still just prefer to go the classic Arms sub-Fury way.

Ironically, Fury is the only Spec that sees some diversity in PvP. You have your classic Dual Wield DD build, you have Fury-Prot Tank (disgusting self-healing from Blood Drinker), and even Two-Handed Fury DD (Flurry on 2H goes "brrr").

Shaman pops Chain Lightning and wipes a group of people like a Dungeon Boss. Or Earth Shock for a Crit that is basically unreactable to, unless you predict it, to... what, exactly -- pop a Protection Potion that will immediately get removed (NOT EVEN BY PURGE BUT BY DAMAGE?!), or Sheen of Zanza to hopefully reflect it back? How is that consistent counterplay? How is that skill? It's just Consumables to try and have an answer to a broken Class and gear design mix.

This also only gets worse in group settings -- like Battlegrounds. Imagine MORE THAN ONE Shaman like that. And since this is in Vanilla spirit, only the Horde has Shamans. The Alliance... does not have an equivalent to this (what do you expect Paladins to do?). So, not only is the 1v1 experience dull for the duelist sweatlords such as myself, but even brawls are just utterly screwed here.

This is not to say, "give Alliance Shamans", but to stress that once you remove Cross-Faction and pit one against the other, you stack Shamans and just watch carnage.

You can say "just get Warlocks" but hey, THEY can have Warlocks TOO.

There is just no balance, AND there is no response to Shamans' power here compared to Vanilla, in Alliance VS Horde matchups.

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: nerf shamans
content_md:
The only fun I can see a Warrior having fun in Alterac Valley on Turtle WoW is by making a spiritual equivalent of an AoE Arms PvP Spec. But again, it needs specific gear to make it work.

Full Enrage (no Reckless Execute). Get Tier 2 Warrior Damage Dealer -- the 8P Set Bonus adds +2 to your Whirlwind Target limit (it now hits up to six, rather than four).

Sweeping Strikes. Charge in. Whirlwind. You hit up to six people with WW alone. Sweep copies five of those hits immediately (5 from WW or 4 from WW + one from Auto).

That's how I see it. However, it's T2, not T3. And eight pieces, not some neat hybrid. So your Stats will be lower by comparison.

I don't know otherwise. This is hard to salvage. It's in contrast to Shaman. Even T3 DD for Warriors is not as good (Set Bonuses are mostly for consistency/PvE).

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: nerf shamans
content_md:
> **Ataika wrote: Fri Mar 28, 2025 6:23 pm**
> Hamstring buff does not help against high enemy burst people complain about

It does against people constantly getting away from you (especially everyone who is ranged that never melees you), so, indirectly, it does. You get to try to stop it more frequently, or respond with your own at the same time.

As for literal rebalancing, some Class Abilities and Talents need to be reworked -- especially those that exhibit broken behavior both in PvE and in PvP; so that nobody (PvE nerds) complains.

Past that, further tweaking via a mix of anti-Player DMG and anti-Player Crit DMG gear (makeshift Resilience), together with PvP-only modifiers that have no effect on anything PvE (like the reduction to Healing Done in PvP Instances like Battlegrounds and Arenas (WotLK patch 3.3.2 change as an example to give). The main detail with this is finding good values for these things.
