author: Atreidon
subject: Re: hitchance melee
content_md:
Unless your target wears gear with +defense (which noone does in meaningful quantities) 5% hit is all you need.

If you are dual wielding you will still miss plenty of swings past this point due to dualwields massive hit penalty, but its generally not worth overcapping hit. As after 5% all your abilites are hitting.

Normally it doesnt matter, but check if you actually have 300 weaponskill trained on your weapon of choice. But that should only affect pve hitchance. Worth investigating tho if nothing else helps.

Other than that, its worth noting that hitcapped does mean your attacks cant miss, but your oponent atill can parry, dodge and block them. Since those are separate mechanics

content_md:
If I recall correctly, some time ago one dev uncovered that the team has in plans to introduce "rated arena" system to Turtle WoW. The topic wasn't much uncovered but it's self-explanatory - the system will evaluate everyone's arena rating based on win/lose ratio in Blood Ring.

It might sound amazing for everyone. I have seen a few forum posts about PvP that asked for this change. What can go wrong then? Although it's generally desired change, people expect too much from this concept and I will explain why rated arena is overhyped.

I think there is nothing wrong with adding arena rating to the game. However, some people believe rated arena equals to matchmaking that selects players based on their arena rating. In other words, bad players would face bad players and good ones would face stronger enemies. While it's technically possible to introduce such matchmaking along with rated arena, this idea has one issue. This system actually shrinks the Blood Ring playerbase. Why does it matter?

Currently in Blood Ring matchmaking is absolutely random. Your gear doesn't matter, you face random players who also queued. This isn't fair but at least playerbase isn't fragmented.

I'm not sure how lv 60 Blood Ring scene looks like now but one month ago on Nordanaar it was nearly dead apart from BR days. You could have game after game only on BR day (if you were lucky) and usually there were only 0-2 arenas active simultaneously.
On the other hand, on non-BR days arena was completely dead like Sunnyglade Valley. You could be in queue for a few hours and not join any Blood Ring.

People think this kind of matchmaking makes sense because Blizzard has already implemented it on retail (and wherever else). But people can't see the difference between Blizzard servers and Turtle WoW. They can't see Blizzard has like 100x more players who play arena, moreover, players connect from several servers because cross-server battlegrounds are standard there.
People think this matchmaking would work here too because it works on Blizzard's servers completely ignoring Turtle WoW's reality. The worst thing is that it takes 1 second to type "/who Blood" to be enlightened how small arena community is on this server.

If the matchmaking was changed to select only players with similar arena rating, let's be honest, Blood Ring would be even more dead than now. Players with low rating couldn't participate in the same games with better players. I'm not sure how many "layers" of that matchmaking would be needed on Turtle WoW but mathematically let's say at least 2. That means the playerbase would be splitted at least by half. The threshold will be too high resulting in never-popping games.

This is why rated matchmaking will likely never be implemented on Turtle WoW. Devs wouldn't want to kill their own child.

Quality is far too low for Ranked Arena to be a thing here. Lots of PvP adjustments need to occur - - from the Ring itself, to Classes, to Equipment. Too soon (Executus).

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Grounding totem gcd nerf
content_md:
Ah yes the stockholm syndrome of pvp players
Everything is broken in pvp, but we cant be fixing the thing that is broken about my class because everyone elses is also broken. Keeping everything in an eternal gridlock.

"Just destroy Grounding with a non impactful spell"
Dealing with grounding in any way costs you resources. Fireblast is on a 1s gcd. Rank 1 frobo/scorch/searing pain/moonfire etc all are on a 1.5 sek gcd.
So even if you place your grounding totem horribly obvious. It costs an opposing caster at least 1 gcd to deal with.
Anyone with half a brain drops it halfway into an important enemy cast. Forcing them to cancel whatever they do, deal with it and restart the cast, getting closer to 2-3 sec time investment to deal with the consequences.

"Just whack it in melee"
Ah yes, my caster will no doubt stand in melee range to the totem when its being placed and i am a hybrid so my weaponswing is actually ready.

Even if your enemy outplays your grounding usage, you not having a gcd used for it means the shaman get ahead in the exchage.
PvP is meant to be punishing and outplaying your oponents mistakes. Badly timed groundings is such a mistake. Yet the shaman isnt punished for it, as he still gets free value from it if the spell isnt having any gcd

And why are you taking paladin as an example why grounding needs to be strong? That class doesnt give a rats ass about it even being up

author: ChecksumNomad
subject: Re: Grounding totem gcd nerf
content_md:
Honestly, I see valid points from both sides here. I’ve played shaman in PvP quite a bit, and yeah — losing the instant reaction with Grounding definitely hurts. It’s not some spammy defensive; you need to read your opponent well for it to work.

But I also get why it was changed — in classic-style PvP where a few spells can decide a fight, absorbing a key cast for free with no GCD is a big deal.

Maybe instead of full GCD, something like a short internal CD or just slightly longer cooldown on Grounding would’ve been a better compromise. That way it keeps the skill-based nature but doesn’t feel “free value” every 15 sec.

Give people free, competitive level gear that can only be used in pvp instances. Its the only way to close the gear gap without making people’s work feel invalidated, and without segmenting the player base.

Alternate option: scale the item level of all gear up to match that of the highest in the battleground. Means your choice of gearing still matters, but an MC epic will be scaled up to a nax epic if theres a nax geared player in the bg, while a person wearing blues will only have a blue at nax ilvl, so they will still be weaker

author: Dasmius
subject: Re: PvP is about to die please do something
content_md:
My suggestion is to make stats static when you enter PvP.
Unfortunately, there is no balance between the gear itemization process and the power gap between players. Think about it: In 2 years with T5 T6 or whatever, a solo tank will completely defeat a raid of players because he is the only one who has the gear, which the rest will take months or years to obtain, so it is better to give up on PvP because no one will like to create a character to play PvP in a game that will never be able to kill anyone because they will be entering years later.
Now, if you lock a predefined stat when entering PvP combat, you(Devs i mean) can have better control of the balance between classes, and in only one part of the content will be affected, without worrying about ruining Raids or dungeons, and even World PVP (which in my opinion is the best part of pvp content) will become very fun.
The best PvP player is the one who plays the game better, and not the one who managed to obtain the most best items (by playing or in who knows what other ways, huh).

author: Rhope79
subject: Re: PvP is about to die please do something
content_md:
-To the people saying 'let it die'.

Warcraft started with Orcs and Humans.

 -To the people saying make things scale

This removes player agency and makes the player feel at the whim of the gamemasters/devs.
This defeats the point of playing an RPG.  You rise in a difficult world thanks to your efforts (and the world has to appreciate your slow rise.)

 -To the people saying add resilience

Resilience made healers overpowered and made games that were meant to have an exhaustion win condition (1-2m fight) into stalemates that were endless.

 -The core of the problem.-

People are more interested in hitting than being hit so players chase damage based gear and the developers of old realized this and made gear for them to chase.

Then everything became more and more oneshot meta.

Also PvP gear being comparable to Dungeon 1 set (the original blue) which has been outdated for 2 decades and often having less stamina than greens 10-15 levels lower than them.

Aside for the 2 piece set bonus on the Epic PvP set, every piece of gear has lackluster stamina compared to the number of dps stats on other pieces of gear.

 -Heres an extreme recommendation but a worthy experiment.

Let people get DPS gear from PvE and Stamina gear from PvP.

So if we're looking at an item like Savage Gladiator Chain Chestpiece
+13 Str
+14 Agi
+13 Stamina
+2 Crit

Have it's PvP equivalent be
+13 Stamina
+14 Stamina
+13 Strength
+20 Stamina

Alot of Stamina, right?
Looks like a ridiculous amount right?
Surprise its the reverse of equally defensive stats.

Also rework the PvP system so there is no decay and every 1k honor you get counts so you can rank up without having to dedicate 10s of hours per week to do so.

Add higher ilevels of PvP gear so they arent outpaced by t2.5.

Add a crafted starter pvp set,
one blue that is cheap and requires alot of easy mats per peice (20-60)
(thorium, Rugged leather, Runecloth)
and one epic that requires a few expensive mats per piece (2-6)
(mooncloth, arcanite, enchanted leather)

The blue set will have item level of Dungeon two quest set

Epic will have item level of MC epics.

The Ranking system rewards will be(with each set having stamina reworked stats):
 1- Tabard and Insignia
 2-4 First Blue PvP set
 5-7 Epic PvP set
 7-10 Epic PvP set II (on par with AQ gear)
 11-13 Epic PvP set III (on par with Naxx gear)
 14-16 Epic PvP set IV (on par with Kara gear)

The next time a dungeon is released, release a new number of 3 higher additional ranks to climb for PvPers.

Have weapons be available at the lower ranks of a PvP tier bc people will almost always go for PvE weapons for damage specialization and will be less valuable.

Also PvPers will wear PvE and PvP gear combinations because pure PvP gear will be too slow paced for some people, whereas others will enjoy that they can outlast a stunlock or a mage's kiting cooldowns.

Im open to arguements where the PvP gear also has anti CC and interrupt properties as CC can be out of hand in WoW and nobody wants to not be able to play their class.

Rogues/Mages who are CC reliant already do enough damage that with this change they wont be able to global and CC 95% of players 100-0, but will still do decisive damage.

+The only problem+ is an yes new players will enter and have to fight very formidable opponents.  However with things like PvP version SGC having tanky stats and T4 hitting hard but being glassy you will almost never win those fights but you will be able to live noticeably longer(even in the Blue PvP Crafted set) which opens up the skillwindow so a trash player wont win 80% of matches based on a 1-5 second burst damage window.

Im estimating 8k health pools on the low PvP gear side and 16k on the high.  So these people spamming out 2-3k crits who only have 2-4k health will start to feel counterpunches and their own mortality.

author: Nkarie
subject: CROSS-REALM BG's/Arena
content_md:
Greetings!
While talking to many PvP players on both realms (Nordanaar and Tel'Abim), I’ve noticed that the biggest issue in PvP is the poor battleground queueing and near-zero Arena activity. At level 60 on Nordanaar, we get about 10–15 BG regs per day, while on Tel'Abim, it’s even worse—less than 10. The Blood Ring Arena on Nordanaar (level 60) doesn’t reg at all.

Because of this, I’d like to ask our beloved Turtle WoW developers to consider implementing cross-realm BG queueing for both realms. Similar systems already exist on other private servers like Warmane, Sirus, WoWCircle, etc.

Personally, I originally planned to play on the PvP realm, but when I compared the populations—7k on Nordanaar vs. 700 on Tel'Abim—the choice became obvious, and I went with PvE. However, if cross-realm BGs were realisating, I would’ve definitely chosen the PvP server despite the population. I’m sure this change would increase the PvP realm’s population and improve BG quality on the PvE realm.

What do you guys think? Share your opinions!
Best regards.

subject: Revert buff costs for PvP

Everytime you are now fighting people with 6k+ health even without flasks because buffs are so cheap to cast that they can be placed on every player every time. For PvE I see no problems with the reduced costs as it just allows everyone to get ready faster.

author: Forumdweller
subject: Some suggestions for Warlock as a Warlock main
content_md:
I'll preface this by saying that I want everyone to feel like the game is as fair as possible. I play many classes and have done so across many private servers and my classic wow career. That being said I know it's not possible to please everyone and that it's probably a good thing that you can't. Please refrain from being toxic in this discussion and come up with legitimate counter arguments/praises and explain your reasoning. I want the game to be fair, just like you. But we all have our own individual experiences and perspectives. All the changes I suggest don't have to come together in a package, one or two ideas can be implemented and the others can be discarded, keep that in mind.

First off I think curse of exhaustion is WAY too strong as it currently stands. Specifically for destruction. Perma control & enormous burst damage is not a good combination to have from a pvp perspective. It's better for affliction since they lack burst damage and have to wait for their dots to ramp up or pray for nightfall procs.

I don't think curse of exhaustion for destruction is necessarily a bad thing, but 50% baseline for 3 points that early in the affliction tree is insane. To put it into perspective you can literally curse someone on a 100% mount and they'll never catch up to you even as you're running (this actually looks bugged TBH. something is off with how movement speed is calculated in regards to curse of exhaustion and mounted targets)

I suggest reigning it down to like 20% and bring amplify curse back (maybe make amplify a deeper talent that wont let you take it with conflag?). That way we can double it to 40% but ONLY ONCE on a long CD (2-3min). It's a very good counter to a rogue after they pop sprint or vanish for example but can't permanently be exploited to keep a warrior at 36 yards while hardcasting soulfire or shadow bolt.

The next suggestion is for aftermath. If this talent is incorporated you may choose to discard curse of exhaustion completely. With max points, shadowburn and conflagrate has a 100% chance to daze the target. This would be fair because shadowburn is a low range ability with a mid-long CD, and conflag can only be applied after casting Immolate (i think someone said that conflag can now be casted without immo? that should definitely be reverted.. imo).

Non soul link Warlocks have always lacked defensive options against melee classes. It would be nice if demon armor gave slightly more defense but that would depend on if we actually had a way to get away from them excluding a 3 min CD in the form of death coil. And I know there's a talent in demo now to increase the effect of Demon Armor but it's hilariously negligble and will never be worth taking it over grim reach, nightfall, or fel concentration. Basically off the table.

Fear should be completely reworked. This spell is a god damn nightmare for every party involved. It's practically only castable against other casters. You can't fear most targets because of the short range (which is fine). It's basically our only defensive but it's unusable 90% of the time because it takes 6 seconds to cast it against melees or classes that can hit you quickly (including hunter). But if you do cast it there's a good chance the target runs around uselessly for a minute. Fear is especially useless in uncoordinated and coordinated group PvP alike, where you manage to fear someone but it breaks instantly because they got hit by someone elses direct damage, which is basically a death sentence to the warlock and it's completely out of their control. Or it breaks from the first tick of your corruption which can also happen more often than you think.

I have a few suggestions for how fear could instead function.

The first is to leave fear as is. Since fear is already very good against casters we leave it. HOWEVER we modify howl of terror instead. Howl of Terror now comes with a baseline baked into the ability (or a point early in a talent tree) which prevents casting from being interrupted by damage. This would make it a silly choice to cast against casters (unless they're really cocky and come up to your face) but gains a viability against melee while maintaining a long CD and a longer cast time than fear (howl of terror is already a 2 second cast). As of right now it's unusable without a pre-emptive lip which is quite toxic.

This gets abit complicated now but what if fear applied a debuff that prevented it from breaking immediately from direct damage for 2 seconds (excluding shadowburn and nightfall procs to prevent exploiting). However after the two seconds it has a high chance to break from ANY damage. Think of it like a pseudo-disorient (not a stun) that can also be used as the infamous method to control one target while you deal with another. This could even be a talent that can be gathered in the destruction tree or applied to a destruction set bonus/pvp gloves.

The last option and probably most OP is to simply change the current warlock pvp glove bonus from searing pain to compatibility with fear instead. I.e 70% chance to resist interruption from damaging attacks while casting fear.

Let us cast fear (unless we're kicked) it's our signature spell!!

Finally I think the Insignia changes should really be looked at. Imo they should retain their class specific features but they could definitely do with a relooking at. Imo the purpose of pvp insignias should be to help alleviate class counters. A warlock insignia should remove stuns (since we already suffer greatly from CC especially against melees who are naturally ingrained with many stuns) while a mage shouldn't remove stuns because they counter practically every class that can use them by simply blinking or popping ice block.

A non PvP suggestion: bring back curse of doom for demonology. I'm gonna be honest I don't know much about the new raiding specs for lock but deep affliction is bis now right? It would cool to make demo an alternative like in WoTLK. curse of doom can only be used against non players and ticks for large damage every 10 seconds for 30 seconds.

I'll preface this by saying that I want everyone to feel like the game is as fair as possible. I play many classes and have done so across many private servers and my classic wow career. That being said I know it's not possible to please everyone and that it's probably a good thing that you can't. Please refrain from being toxic in this discussion and come up with legitimate counter arguments/praises and explain your reasoning. I want the game to be fair, just like you. But we all have our own individual experiences and perspectives. All the changes I suggest don't have to come together in a package, one or two ideas can be implemented and the others can be discarded, keep that in mind.

First off I think curse of exhaustion is WAY too strong as it currently stands. Specifically for destruction. Perma control & enormous burst damage is not a good combination to have from a pvp perspective. It's better for affliction since they lack burst damage and have to wait for their dots to ramp up or pray for nightfall procs.

I don't think curse of exhaustion for destruction is necessarily a bad thing, but 50% baseline for 3 points that early in the affliction tree is insane. To put it into perspective you can literally curse someone on a 100% mount and they'll never catch up to you even as you're running (this actually looks bugged TBH. something is off with how movement speed is calculated in regards to curse of exhaustion and mounted targets)

I suggest reigning it down to like 20% and bring amplify curse back (maybe make amplify a deeper talent that wont let you take it with conflag?). That way we can double it to 40% but ONLY ONCE on a long CD (2-3min). It's a very good counter to a rogue after they pop sprint or vanish for example but can't permanently be exploited to keep a warrior at 36 yards while hardcasting soulfire or shadow bolt.

The next suggestion is for aftermath. If this talent is incorporated you may choose to discard curse of exhaustion completely. With max points, shadowburn and conflagrate has a 100% chance to daze the target. This would be fair because shadowburn is a low range ability with a mid-long CD, and conflag can only be applied after casting Immolate (i think someone said that conflag can now be casted without immo? that should definitely be reverted.. imo).

Non soul link Warlocks have always lacked defensive options against melee classes. It would be nice if demon armor gave slightly more defense but that would depend on if we actually had a way to get away from them excluding a 3 min CD in the form of death coil. And I know there's a talent in demo now to increase the effect of Demon Armor but it's hilariously negligble and will never be worth taking it over grim reach, nightfall, or fel concentration. Basically off the table.

Fear should be completely reworked. This spell is a god damn nightmare for every party involved. It's practically only castable against other casters. You can't fear most targets because of the short range (which is fine). It's basically our only defensive but it's unusable 90% of the time because it takes 6 seconds to cast it against melees or classes that can hit you quickly (including hunter). But if you do cast it there's a good chance the target runs around uselessly for a minute. Fear is especially useless in uncoordinated and coordinated group PvP alike, where you manage to fear someone but it breaks instantly because they got hit by someone elses direct damage, which is basically a death sentence to the warlock and it's completely out of their control. Or it breaks from the first tick of your corruption which can also happen more often than you think.

I have a few suggestions for how fear could instead function.

The first is to leave fear as is. Since fear is already very good against casters we leave it. HOWEVER we modify howl of terror instead. Howl of Terror now comes with a baseline baked into the ability (or a point early in a talent tree) which prevents casting from being interrupted by damage. This would make it a silly choice to cast against casters (unless they're really cocky and come up to your face) but gains a viability against melee while maintaining a long CD and a longer cast time than fear (howl of terror is already a 2 second cast). As of right now it's unusable without a pre-emptive lip which is quite toxic.

This gets abit complicated now but what if fear applied a debuff that prevented it from breaking immediately from direct damage for 2 seconds (excluding shadowburn and nightfall procs to prevent exploiting). However after the two seconds it has a high chance to break from ANY damage. Think of it like a pseudo-disorient (not a stun) that can also be used as the infamous method to control one target while you deal with another. This could even be a talent that can be gathered in the destruction tree or applied to a destruction set bonus/pvp gloves.

The last option and probably most OP is to simply change the current warlock pvp glove bonus from searing pain to compatibility with fear instead. I.e 70% chance to resist interruption from damaging attacks while casting fear.

Let us cast fear (unless we're kicked) it's our signature spell!!

Finally I think the Insignia changes should really be looked at. Imo they should retain their class specific features but they could definitely do with a relooking at. Imo the purpose of pvp insignias should be to help alleviate class counters. A warlock insignia should remove stuns (since we already suffer greatly from CC especially against melees who are naturally ingrained with many stuns) while a mage shouldn't remove stuns because they counter practically every class that can use them by simply blinking or popping ice block.

A non PvP suggestion: bring back curse of doom for demonology. I'm gonna be honest I don't know much about the new raiding specs for lock but deep affliction is bis now right? It would cool to make demo an alternative like in WoTLK. curse of doom can only be used against non players and ticks for large damage every 10 seconds for 30 seconds.
topic_title: Some suggestions for Warlock as a Warlock main

author: Forumdweller
subject: Re: Some suggestions for Warlock as a Warlock main
content_md:
I'll do a small Q&A here because I feel like people are gonna keep making the same misrepresentation of these changes.

 **Doesn't the change with 2 second grace window make fear even more op?**

No. In many ways it becomes weaker overall, but it becomes more usable for skilled players who know how to fake cast their abilities or juke spells. This is because fear would now break from ANY damage after the 2 seconds debuff, meaning it can no longer function as a mini 20 second stun which don't break even as dots are ticking. It encourages warlocks to not keep you CC'd permanently while dealing damage or putting up their dots willy nilly. It's more rewarding now but is less toxic for the people who rightfully complain about how OP fear can be (remember I said this would be a destruction talent or set piece so affliction warlocks can still play the game)

The point is to make it so that it doesn't make it break immediately when you're fearing someone in pvp which can either happen when you're 1v1'ing from the first tick of your corruption - if it ticks within the 2 second 'grace' window - (this happens more often than you might think) or because someone else is slamming them. It's basically a death sentence most of the time and it's completely out of your control. To make it even more clear what I'm trying to convey here, the disorient effect only lasts as long as the 2 second debuff fear would now apply and breaks from MOST, if not all direct damage from the warlock but will NOT break from dots or other players for 2 seconds. The best thing the warlock would be able to do in this window is either run, drain life (2 free ticks), or cast a free searing pain (1.5s cast) without fear breaking.

 **What about the change to the pvp glove bonus with fear adding a chance to resist interruption from taking damage while casting fear?**

As for the change with replacing the pvp glove bonus of searing pain to functionality with fear, fear is exactly the same... now you can just cast it versus the classes that keep you 'soft-stunned' permanently. To put that into perspective, fear can take upwards of 6 seconds to cast vs warriors or rogues. It's so absurd that a skilled player wont even bother kicking fear because they know you wont even manage to even get it off. How is this fair?

Psychic scream is a instant cast aoe CC. What do you think is better. Fear or psychic scream? Priests can also heal themselves. I think we'll be fine with these changes.

i'm level 30 and been playing turtlewow for little under a couple weeks and my experience of warmode at least in the starting alliance zones up until has just been getting 1 tapped by passing-by level 60s or getting ganked by twinks with fully enchanted gear.

i don't think i've accidentally bumped into a levelling horde who also has warmode turned on yet, and i've played almost 80 hours so far.

on paper warmode was probably created to incentivise people doing world pvp because the risk of being killed was worth the exp boost. but in practice the only people that have it activated are people actively looking to PVP others but not while levelling, just instead they want to use it to gank lowbies who took warmode to get extra exp.

i still use it because im used to playing on PVP worlds and getting ganked so why not get the free extra %20 experience? i've been ganked maybe 10-15 times between level 1 to level 30, so i don't think it's that bad of a risk to take at least early on.

i'll probably change my opinion once i get to mid-level contested zones where horde are more common - and if i keep getting killed over and over and over en masse i'll probably just turn it off to save myself the headache but i don't think it's bad at all so far.

Ultimately, the problem is the existence of PvE realms.

Ganking has never been so bad as to justify negating the WPvP aspect entirely when it could have been suspended with things like a "potion of neutrality" or dampened with bounties on gankers (the more grey-level players you kill, the more real-time data is fed about your character to the opposite faction*) or whatever.

The absence of any real danger in a video game, which is meant to be the overcoming of danger and hardship, is antithetical to the nature of the hero's journey.

 *ie:
For any given period of 12 hours, let's call it Dishonorable kill (killing a grey or green-leveled player):
 1 DK: zone warning
 3 DK: zone warning with name
 5 DK: zone warning with name, lvl, class
 8 DK: zone warning with name, lvl, class, weapon used (indicates general level of gearing)
 12 DK: Zone tracker, global warning.
 16 DK: Zone tracker, global warning, bounty bag on death.
 20 DK: Global tracker, global warning, bounty bag on death, NPC cavalry squadrons deployed (occasional groups of same-level elite knights(EK-A)/sentinels(KA-A)/wolfriders(KA-H)/deathguards(EK-H), depending on area, appear and give chase, equipped with knockback ranged weapons (like Goblin bruisers in BB, to prevent evade trickery).
 30 DK: Gryphon riders / bat riders harass from the air (slow movement, prevent stealth, decrease healing).

Grand Theft Warcraft.

author: Based_Chadman
subject: Regardling Resilience
content_md:
I would like to make a case against pvp gear, especially with unique stats.

Part of the enjoyment of casual pvp in vanilla WoW is the ability to cross over from pve to pvp content - to take your hard-earned gear and go fight other people with it. If you introduce pvp gear, the casual playerbase will dwindle, and world pvp participation will also drop due to the disinterest in farming multiple sets for both types of content.

Instead, to deal with high burst, why not consider something like a blanket %dmg decrease in pvp combat to see how that works out over adding resilience? Thank you.

PVP gearing

The elephant in the room when it comes to pvp is gear disparity - a hot topic as postnaxx content rolls out. My solution? Make battlegrounds restricted by item level.

How Would It Work?
If a player’s item level exceeds the battleground cap, they cannot queue. If they swap to higher itemlevel gear while inside, they are kicked with a deserter debuff.

For example, if the item level cap is 78, there are two primary ways to calculate this restriction, each with pros and cons:

1. absolute ilvl cap (78 × 15 = 1170 total item level)
✔ simple and clear
✖ doesn’t properly account for weapons, disadvantaging players with dual-wield/mainhand-offhand/shield setups

2. average ilvl cap (total item level divided by used slots ≤ 78)
✔ accounts for weapon differences fairly
✖ creates an awkward meta where players might intentionally leave certain slots empty to lower their average item level

the best approach: a hybrid system

To balance both issues, the best solution would be an absolute item level cap, but with weapons contributing as an average rather than a hard limit. This avoids the weapon disadvantage of the first system while preventing the empty-slot meta of the second.

(Additionally, this would require a UI update in the character tab, clearly displaying absolute item level to help players track their eligibility.)

Why this is the longterm solution?

Instead of constantly buffing pvp gear every time a new raid is released - a system that is not sustainable - or doing nothing at all, which would cause pvp gear to gradually become irrelevant as pve content progresses, this approach removes the need for artificial stat inflation.
- no need for new pvp exclusive stats like resilience
- pvp gear (including reputation rewards etc) can instead be designed to offer better stats relative to their item level
- rank 12-14 gear could receive minor stat buffs, but the main balancing factor would be item level itself

The ripple effect

This system wouldn’t just balance battlegrounds - it would revitalize other aspects of the game:
- players would need to optimize gear within a set limit, making quest rewards, crafted gear, and reputation items more relevant
- consequently rural areas and trade would become richer, as players seek out diverse gearing options
- higher item level pieces would still be valuable, but players could balance them out with lower ilvl gear, creating more diverse builds rather than just stacking raid bis

This way everyone can easily attain blue resi gear by simply farming honor points in bg's.

Which would basically be the pvp equivalent of farming dungeons.
And with rated arena's people that want to seriously get into pvp can attain their purple resi set thats equivalent to currently the highest raids Ilvl, bring back to old rules like 1800mmr for weap 2.2 mmr for shoulders.

Bring back arena teams (where back then you had to make an arena team and then invite someone into it before you could queue for arena's) but make your MMR be bound to you the individual and not the team (to stop people from disbanding and remaking a team after end of the week arena reward) that way your MMR always stays the same no matter which team you join.

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: Regardling Resilience
content_md:
I am fine with PvE players bringing raid gear into PvP. They earned it and that is fine. The problem is that PvP needs easily accessible PvP gear to counterbalance it.

I would not even mind starting PvP gear being 30 to 40 percent weaker if it was easy to get. That way, raid-geared players would still have an edge, but skilled PvP players could still make plays and win fights. Right now, you are fighting backpedaling raid bosses casting Lightning Bolt or Frostbolt and two-shotting you.

The result is clear:

 * PvE geared players demolish new players
 * The team with the most raid gear usually wins
 * New PvP players are discouraged and often stop trying

This is not fun for anyone. I do not enjoy one-shotting green geared players, and I do not enjoy being one-shot by Naxx veterans either. My friends who have never PvPed before were shocked at how fast they died and did not queue again.

Whether it is resilience or another approach, we need easily attainable PvP gear so fights are about skill and decision making, not just who has the most gear. Some will say “I farmed scripted NPCs for epics so I deserve to destroy players without resistance,” but that mindset is gatekeeping and bad for the game.

Making PvP accessible means more people queue, more people have fun, and the whole game benefits. That is what we all want.

subject: Assign a dedicated developer to revive PvP
content_md:

Someone who would monitor and adjust class balance, propose PvP sets and items, optimize gearing, honor, tokens, ranking systems, and more?

Currently, PvP is dead if we look at the number of players participating compared to the total player base. This doesn't have to be the case. There are hundreds of players willing to engage in PvP, but not in its current form, with all the burst damage, difficult gearing, and faction imbalances.

We would love to see a comeback of the PvP era. Many players, myself and my friends included, play the game mainly because we enjoy PvP.

Even just acknowledging these issues and communicating that the dev team is actively working on them would go a long way.

author: Whoopie
subject: Re: Assign a dedicated developer to revive PvP
content_md:
You should be interested in PvP if you’re making PvP changes. As it turns out, people who are really good at PvP have a better understanding of PvP.

Regarding the car reference - no, you don't have to be a racer to make cars, but I bet a racer would make a better car than a plumber would.

I also don't understand the references to vanilla and its imbalances that many people bring up. We're on a Classic Plus-type realm, whose whole purpose is to build on vanilla and fix the problems the original game had.

And I don't agree that separating PvP balance brought us to this problem. This problem emerged because of a lack of concern for PvP. I understand the game is mostly made by and for PvE enthusiasts, but PvP is still a part of the whole, and we should strive to find ways to improve it.

Whether it’s through a dedicated developer whose whole purpose is to find ways to improve this aspect of the game (by communicating with top PvPers, taking inspiration from other iterations of the game, etc.) or by the core team dedicating some insights themselves - although if they're not actively playing PvP, they might lack an understanding of the problems.

Back to the analogies: if you ask a team of plumbers to fix your car, you might not be driving anytime soon.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Assign a dedicated developer to revive PvP
content_md:
If the goal is to make pvp an environment where skill at the matchup being played is the deciding factor, the influences from sources outside of that interaction have on its outcome need to be minimized. Be it engineering you farmed nodes for, raidgear you spent months comlecting, consumables you bought with gold or even gear you earned from fighting other players

And to drive my point home, plenty of the self proclaimed "good" pvp players make full use of some or all of the above to minimize the actual skill required to win.

And similrly how a couple years ago counterstrike pros were absolutely loosing it when other "easier" weapons than the ak-47 were buffed, or how competetive starcraft maps just have to be at least so big that stimmed marines cant walk base to base and kill you before your sunkens can finish, you can expect someone with tens of thousands of honorable kills to hold calcified believes for pvp.
For instance, druid is the undisputed king of wsg flag running. Every single wsg team in classic line environments in competetove settings bring a druid as their fc.
Now i ask all of the oh so skilled pvpers, is this bad gamedesign or just a fact of pvp. (Wether or not i think druid fc is problematic is btw completely irrelevant here. It goes to show how experience  in pvp alone is not nearly enough of a qualifying factor for shaping pvp)

To stick with my car analogy, even tho a racecar driver might help tell you what needs to be improved, the actual work will still have to be done by a mechanic and an engineer

As for separating pve and pvp, it doesnt really make sense for the simple fact that every single item ever created has to be doublechecked for pvp. At which point you might as well include them for the design process to begin with

I love low-level PvP, and it should be what it is: low-level PvP.

author: Imonobor
subject: Re: PVP is BROKEN Lv 19 with over 2200 HP !?!?!
content_md:
I agree that enchants should be ilvl-restricted, but unfortunately it's probably not happening for two reasons:

 -Items that already have high-level enchants applied to them would have to be removed manually, which is a huge undertaking. You would basically have to un-enchant almost every item on every twink character. It's likely possible to automate this.

 -How would current twinks be compensated for their lost enchants? Imagine dishing out several thousand gold to set up your twink, and logging in the next day to find all your enchants gone. That would be really shitty, and would cause a huge backlash and wave of whining.

If TWoW implemented enchanting vellums that could store enchants in consumable item form, they could possibly just add those to the twink's inventory when removing it from their items, so they could re-sell it on AH and recoup some of the cost. But enchanting vellums are probably not happening either.

An alternative would be to just add the current AH value of all mats used in the enchants to the twink's gold total, but that has its own problems - like ever-changing AH prices, and enchants that can't be valued accurately like the Naxx enchants.

It's not impossible to see this implemented at some point, but I don't see it happening any time soon.

If, however, it were to happen, I would love to try out twinking. The upfront cost of endgame enchants has always put me off from trying it. I imagine more people are in the same camp, so it could revitalize the twinking scene with new blood.

author: Xudo
subject: Vanilla was bursty by design
content_md:
Lot of people complain about CC2 and its "burst" meta. But lets be honest, burst was good even before CC2. PoM-Pyro mages, enh shamans, ele shamans, shockadins, seduction-soulfire warlocks. CC2 just added burst to more classes/specs.
Some also might notice that resilence in later patches made heals stronger and fights longer.

Here is my point: vanilla pvp was bursty by design

Imagine wow without bursts.
In this game, group pvp will look like DPS race. Your team inflict damage, enemy team outheal this damage. If damage > heals, then your team wins.

You might say "but we can CC healer". Right, but all CC can be dispelled in one way or another. What would healer do in the next second after releasing from CC? Right - he will heal.
If enemy team can CC, then your team can CC too. Damage dealers can be CCed and their target can be outhealed during that short period of inactivity.
If played right, your team can outheal any inflicted damage taken. See "turtling" in WSG base. At some gear level, team can just stay near graveyard and fight endlessly.

Vanilla devs came to conclusion like "to prevent long boring fights with DPS race, we allow some classes to inflict heavy damage in short timeframes".
As a result, in Vanilla your class had burst or some pressure against healing: Mortal Strike, Viper Sting, Wound Poisons.

If you look at pure pvp games, you might notice that there is few ways to restore health, but there are always some way to nuke enemy player.
Team Fortress - you need to exit "front line", travel to specific point and pickup health. Skilled engineer can make turtling at some points of the map. But there are classes with huge burst like Sniper or Soldier.
DotA - healing fountains are present in base so you need to exit "front line" and travel back in order to heal. Very few classes can heal others in combat.
Mortal Combat - no heals at all.
For Honor - you can heal at some points of the map. Though, fights here are bursty like in Mortal combat. You can't heal full during fight.
Counter Strike - headshots say "hello".
Hell, even chess are "bursty". If one figure attacks other, defender can't survive at all. It just dies and get removed from table.

So in conclusion, bursty pvp is a norm. It is design proven by multiple other games.

author: Dannyp92
subject: Re: Vanilla was bursty by design
content_md:
The intro is almost a false equivalence. Just because Vanilla had burst doesn't mean it's fine for Turtle to be even more bursty. Nuance matters. The extent, accessibility, and frequency of burst is clearly much higher in Turtle now, due to CC2, new gear, and general power creep.

Besides, even though Vanilla was bursty, it almost always had trade-offs. Sure, you could kill someone with 2x Pyroblasts, but you were limited to a certain spec and setup, could only do it every 3 minutes, and you weren't always able to pull it off. Yes, Shamans/Paladins could one-shot you if the stars aligned, but otherwise their damage was fairly low and they were susceptible to getting shut down. Etc. etc.

Furthermore, I believe the old PvP-sets had especially high Stamina on them to counter burstiness, but as far as I know the new endgame gear in Turtle will have power that far outpaces that Stamina.

I'm also not convinced the PvP trinket change was a net positive. The original design leaned more into a rock-paper-scissors meta, where you couldn't trinket everything. That gave us better tools to shut down burst through strategic CC; now it's harder to do so.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Vanilla was bursty by design
content_md:
Even with some classes burst windows getting intentionally or unintentionally nerfed (spellbatching for frostmage and elemental shaman crits being removed, reckoning reverted, Raptorstrike Critchance significantly lowered)

The massive influx of gear and class changes for higher average DPS have substantially changed the pvp landscape. What used to be freak oneshits like tripple crit windfury of shaman or reckoning bombs that required long time in combat to stack up has traded places with on demand burst.

Shamans have a over 60% chance to see their windfury in the first 3 seconds of combat. Arcane mages have a spell that hits substantially harder than Pyro (thanks to 220% crit multiplier and spell windfury for up to 185% normal damage) on a 2.5 second casttime that can even be shortened substantially due to their haste interaction.
(Yes its possible for that single spell if stars align to do 5-6k burst damage)
Paladins next to remaining similarly unkillable as they were boast holy strike which hits about as hard as holy shock used to. With a third of its cooldown. While SoR scales 2-3x as well with spellpower as it did back in the day.

There are choice examples of classes whose burst got worse, but the general trend is very clearly up. And while classic wows pvp was always bursty, it was never that intense. And the trend only is getting worse as more Kara gear with high offense and low stamina makes its way around.

And there is one giant problem with oneshot pvp. It is not fun to be on the receiving end of it repeatedly. And with all the powercreep what used to be a rare occurance has become ever more commonplace. If i wanna have engage times of 2-3 seconds id play a shooter where im back in action 20 secs after i died. In wow that process of rezzing buffing and riding back to the front takes minutes.

content_md:
Do you even pvp??? i can post my armories, i think i know what happens around here. Even enha shamans dont run out of mana unless you mana drain them. They can sit there and cast good 6 healing waves back to back . But running up next to a shaman with 20 yard mana drain is extremely dangerous you are ASKING to get WF'd in 1 hit. Only safe way to do it is while they are feared and even then you are better off just casting shadowbolts.

i have 70k hks on my horde one and close to 30k on alli(r11 and 13 respectively) i think i know what goes around me. After about 3k hks you get the feel of the class what it can do and what it cant.

Do you know whats 800 sp with TOEP popped? 371 corruption, 156 siphon,123 agony followed up by 850 sburn(thats only 650 dmg every THREE seconds--lesser healing wave is 1.5s cast and is 1k healed before any spellpower. So in those 3 seconds your dots need to tick shamans can pull off TWO lesser healing waves negating all your damage). guess what, its not enough. The shamans sit there on 1 spot and heal right through the damage. Sure if you latch on to them with dark harvest and u dont get ES'd they MIGHT die since it speeds up your dots (why do we need ANOTEHR channel spell again?) but most of the time they just LOS, heal up and get back into the fight.  WITH TONGUES. Yes, you can put agony plus tongues now. Too bad, their health is so high and healing is so heavy they heal through.

Do you know how long it takes for a pet to destroy a ground totem unless its an imp? warlock pets dont have any movement speed increase and shamans drop all totems automatically so the pet will also be slowed by earthbind.

Good 5-10 seconds sometimes i mash petattack macro and tap my foot while it slow as molasses crawls to the totem but by then it already came off cd(12 seconds) so shaman is ready to drop another one.

Sure man ill dot them up and sic a pet on them and interrupt but it just dies in 1 hit from WF and you are back to square one, out of mana, out of pet while shaman is at full hp.
Ground totems are immune to dots, so i have to waste my shadowburn(15s cd) but its also very close range. which again, is very dangerous. Wands are just exempt i wont even go there completely useless charge-up time of 2 seconds you might as well cast a shadowbolt at it. 30 yard range is also too dangerous thats into frostshock/earthshock category

Do i usually top kills? sure. multidotting and tongues/exhaustion isnt hard. But go on, show us how it is done, you should be geared up in no time in bwl-aq gear on nord its basically free. Show us how it is done.

Well lets compare what Shamans can do on TWoW vs Paladins since those are the exclusive classes:

Shaman offense:
Purge
Damage (caster or melee)

Shaman CC:
Frost shock (soft cc)
Earth shock (interrupt)
Earthbind totem(easily killed totem and soft cc)

Shaman CC removal:
Grounding totem (good for 1 damage spell cast and will absorb for anyone targeted in your party not just the shaman)
Tremor (unreliable and easily killed totem only works on fears and sleep)
Cleanse Poison
Cleanse Disease (never used in PvP)

Shaman defensives:
Heal

Pally offense:
Damage (holy damage cannot be mitigated)
Hard CCs

Paladin CC:
HoJ (Hard CC stun)
Repentance (Hard CC incap)

Paladin CC removal:
Cleanse (removes 3 debuffs with 1 cast including magic)
Freedom (complete removal of all slow debuffs and immunity)

Paladin defensives:
Eye for an Eye talent (returns 30% crit spell damage back to the caster)
LoH
Bubble (total immunity can still heal or attack)
Hand of Protection (complete removal of all physical debuffs incl Sap and immunity to physical attacks for the pally or an ally)
Heal

Shamans have 1 defensive ability, to heal themselves. Where as paladins have multiple defensive abilities for both them and their allies including the ability to go completely invulnerable and still take actions. They can also use a Hard CC to stop the person attacking/moving (or if stunned take any actions at all) and go on the offensive or defensive via the baseline abilities given to them which don't require a talent (consecration, holy strike, crusader strike). Where as the new shaman ability is not baseline and requires a talent.

Paladins need some of their defensive capabilities locked behind talents (bubble holy spec capstone) since they have been given so much baseline now.

author: Skullcat
subject: Re: Paladin Retune When??
content_md:
This thread is indeed very much anti-paladin sentiment in a lot of official capacity. To paint the image correctly:

> Paladins are the least mobile melee of all melees. Warriors have charge. Feral druids are simply faster in cat-form. The Rogue has a sprint. Survival Hunters have Aspect of Cheetah. Shaman that's smart enough can Spirit-wolf (it takes only 3 seconds.)
 -> Paladin struggles with catching runners. Warriors have charge, and hamstring. Feral Druid can entangle, or keep on their target. (30% movement speed in cat form is really hard to shake off.)  Shamans have Earthbind totems. Rogue generally never need to catch runners (because at that point runners are already dead.)

---
> Paladins have zero ranged capacity outside of Engineering. Warriors can use ranged weapons. Rogues can use ranged weapons. Shamans can cast spells afar. Druids can cast spells afar. This means that Paladins are mostly forced to engage enemies in close-quarter combat at all times.
 -> As such. Paladins will be best performing fighting enemies **indoors with wall for LoS.**

---
> Paladins have a lot of survival kits. But that is to compensate for their glaring PVP weaknesses. Once the distance is made, the Paladin will never win that PVP fight and their only solution is to *leave.* A Paladin that cannot make the chase will either have to leave, or lose.
 -> Hand of Freedom, and Hand of Justice will not help the Paladins with chase almost all of the time. If they are not bursting the damage immediately, the target survives. That said target can flee, and survive the encounter with a Paladin. It's not the end of the world.

---
Their only saving grace is that Paladins' strong points are simply the ability to stun an enemy on-demand (But on a 60 second CD). Stasis themselves into invulnerable stasis (on a 5 minute CD.). Recharge all of their health affected by healing reduction at cost of all their mana (On a whole hour CD). And 10-seconds of movement-impairing immunity on a 20 second cooldown.

But Paladins, once cannot reach their target, have already lost.

Paladins may be terrifying. But they are slow. They are dependent on Engineering. They need speed boosts to reach you. Once you're able to outpace the paladin at that point. You've effectively won. *Paladins* just can't do anything about it.

author: Skullcat
subject: Re: Paladin Retune When??
content_md:
> **Laysson wrote: Fri May 09, 2025 4:25 pm**
> - Add a CD to Cleanse like 6 or even 8 sec. : spammable 1 button to dispel 3 effects (that ruins all classes except Warrior) is just too much, but make it guaranteed to dispel
>  - As a compensation, give them some mobility, like Long Arm of the Law from Cata
>
>  - Increase Freedom CD
>
>  - Eye for an Eye to 15% : 30% passive damage is just absurd

Hand of Freedom retrieving an increased cooldown will be extremely brutal for Paladins. Considering they are dependent on not getting slowed. The moment the Paladin receives a hamstring, Piercing Howl, concussive shot, Stonebind totem'd, Frostbolted, Frost Nova'd, Cone of Cold, Entangling rooted, Curse of Exhaustion, Mind Flay (This is a channel), and even Rogue's Crippling Poison (This can be cleansed.)

They are going to struggle catching up.

In addition, Shamans, Warlock's Felhunter and Priests can **purge** Hand of Freedom.

Paladin is perhaps the only class that doesn't have much crowd-control outside of repentance (Which is a heavy RET investment) and Hammer of Justice. And then there's the Seal of Justice. Seal of Justice is a Proc% to stun a target for 2 seconds. So not only do you have two on-demands stun, you also have a gambling seal. And *nobody*  of reasonable sort wants to bet on possibilities during a PVP confrontation. Hence **Engineering**.

---
Adding CD to Cleanse is like a redundancy;

The Paladin has to expend 8% of his mana to cleanse the debuff. And everytime you keep reapplying that debuff. The paladin has to cleanse again. And again. If you cast debuff on him and they cleansed 10 times. That means 80% of their mana are pretty much gone.

Whereas if you just add a cooldown. You're achieving pretty much the same result.

Also you forgot to add the fact that Warlock's curses cannot be cleansed. It's a curse, not magic.

---
Eye for Eye is more or less to give pity to Paladins who struggle catching mages and warlocks. Since mages can kite Paladins easily if they're not stupid. And Warlock has fears and Curse of Exhaustion (And w/ Felhunter, can purge Hand of Freedom to re-apply Curse of Exhaustion). Well -

It's a pity talent basically. "Oh you're getting critted by a caster that you can't catch? Well here. If they crit you, they take 15%-30% damage backlash."

This Paladin is a Holy Paladin. A Shockadin build in process. At that level, they have access to Holy Shock. The hunter opens engagement with a very well-placed usage of an ice trap. You can tell this Hunter is very good at engaging multiple open-world PvP. In addition, Paladin switches to healing to keep Hunter alive from the Shaman's last resort.

Notice that I said last resort?

This video is grossly egregious yet deceptive.

During the video, you can see the Shaman and Druid pursuing two runaways. Attempting to finish them off. When you see their mana, they were very close to OOMing. As such, it's not surprising that a level 51 hunter and paladin were able to defeat two level 60s that weren't at their best. On top of that, they were caught off-guard by sudden introduction of the Hunter and Paladin.

While you wont always be the one getting the kill you will still be extremely annoying debuffing everyone, tongues on healers/casters plus agony or COE, dots flying everywhere and once you have all 3 dots on someone and you apply dark harvest the damage is up there. Now affliction still blows to tackle a priest 1v1,but u can COE+apply all dots and hit that drain mana button with your felhunter on him. its a slow battle but you will probably win--you may have to coil him and healthstone since disc priests hurt but if you can keep him feared and drain his mana while he is feared you can win vs shadow and disc

author: Rhope79
subject: Re: New players have no chance in PvP
content_md:
Veteran geared players should have an advantage.

The problem is obtaining inferior ilvl PvP gear with a pitful amount of stamina is very time consuming.

The offensive stats are far more plentiful on gear in numeric value and also when you consider that they have synergy.

So a piece with 10 agi and 10 str actually is worth more than just 20 offensive stat points because of that.

Stamina is the only real defensive stat, armor is good against rogue,war,hunter and nobody else and spell resistence is very costly per stat value to obtain and even more niche.

Having entry level blue and epic crafter PvP sets that have equal amounts of defensive stats (really mostly just stamina) to the offensive stats and then from ranking have PvP sets that go up all the way to ilevel Kara gear would fix alot of the problems.

Also having the pvp pieces have some CC reduction properties may not be a bad idea as well.

One shots or 5-10 second fights should only occur when someone is vastly outgeared or someone wins the lottery in luck for the fight, and fights that have endless CC isnt interesting for the person being stuck in sheep for a minute

>  So there is no evidence that adding resilience here would make pvp better. It might turn out it will become even worse

Good points, but id hardly consider cata to be "the most balanced". In my book thats wrath, and both wrath and tbc didnt have all of that homogenization going on, and resilience worked well in those expansions to lessen the impact of overbloated damage.

My own points against resilience here, is that it really kills the gearing versatility of vanilla and segragates the two gamemodes, limits you with what you can wear etc, which is why if it is to be implemented, it should be implemented for all pieces of gear, with pve gear having lower values and pvp more of it.

Another minus to resilience, is that it never feels good seeing one of your abilities do 2k dmg to a mob, and then deal 1k to a player. These kinds of damage discrepancies just dont feel good, as you cant properly gauge how much damage you'd actually be able to do without proper knowledge and experience. For me this isnt a problem, but I know its a problem for some.

Then theres the issue of healing. Healing might become too overpowered. How do you address this? Lowering healing output on targets with higher values of a stat might work but it feels weird losing power this way as well, and has never been done in WoW, as its certainly open to weird unforseen exploits. At the very least hybrid classes will become unkillable gods if they don't have severe mana issues as counterbalance.

Imo the correct course of action is adding more stamina, armour and resists to most pieces of raid and pvp gear. It fits the vanilla aesthetic more, but it would also warrant PvE readjustments, which might be far too time consuming and nearly impossible without a large playtest. How are the devs supposed to organize 40 players to readjust raid damage intake with all those buffed stats?

For a similar reason simply scaling down damage is going to be tricky. How would it affect raiding if suddenly DPS drops down by 20%? Content becomes much harder. It wont be an issue for early tier raids, but naxx could become very difficult (might be a good thing).

Ascension tackled this problem by first having global dmg reduction, ontop of every spell having its own pvp modifier. Both of these lead to huge problems and created a ridiculous shitstorm. Spells would be forgotten to be updated, scaling would break etc.

Resilience isnt a pretty solution, but theres a reason blizzard took that route - it was an easy and cost effective solution that actually fixed the problem, at the expense of creating a diffent problem.

Currently its better to have at least some solution rather than nothing, so picking the lesser evil is preferable. PvP is disgustingly bad, its hardly a "classic" experience in that regard, and its putting off a sizable junk of the playerbase. A large crowd of the classic fanbase gear up so they can PvP as an endgoal. When PvP becomes a 2shot fiesta with next to no counterplay, gear is irrelevant in equal matchups, and playing is pointless if you dont have the gear to match up. You'd get more balanced and fun fights if everyone was buttnaked instead.

author: Talon2e
subject: Re: Cataclysm resilience is the easiest fix to PvP
content_md: I honestly think the best solution for PvP is going to be some form of damage mitigation stat.  You can call it resilience or whatever you want but something that just does player takes X% less damage from other players.  Then you add another tier to PvP gear to be on par with Naxx and Kara 40.  This set will have say 10% over all damage less than the current best tier of PvE gear but would have say 15% more stam making it good gear but not ideal gear for PvE.  Last thing you do is open up PvP gearing so its more accessible.  Remove the ladder aspect to ranks and instead make them flat honor bench marks.  Rank 1 say is 25K honor and then go from there.  That way everyone can eventually rank up and have access to full PvP gear.  I'd probably shuffle current tiers around so current rank 14 gear is down around rank 10 and the new set caps out at rank 14.  Going forward any more raid progression gets an equal set of PvP gear and you can either make new ranks or you can push the existing sets down in rank.

PvP is disgustingly bad, its hardly a "classic" experience in that regard, and its putting off a sizable junk of the playerbase. A large crowd of the classic fanbase gear up so they can PvP as an endgoal. When PvP becomes a 2shot fiesta with next to no counterplay, gear is irrelevant in equal matchups, and playing is pointless if you dont have the gear to match up. You'd get more balanced and fun fights if everyone was buttnaked instead.

I completely agree with your points. I have been struggling in BG's for 2 months and anyone that CC2 has done anything but ruin pvp is completely wrong. Either your play a Burst damage class or you lose, which bodes very poorly because I keep on trying to make demonology warlock work. And news flash, it is near impossible with the silly amounts of burst damage coming from Shaman,Disc Priest, Rogue, Feral/Balance Druid, Mage, Warrior. Yes, I listed just about every class.

I agree that you identified the problem. Some combination of reworked talents + overly powerful gear has made pvp a burst fiesta. Coincidentally, Retail wow had this very same problem. Which is why I laugh at every forum post where someone defends this crap storm by saying "go to retail". Guess what, Turtle wow has made the exact same mistake as retail- so we are already on a reimagined retail. Put simply, not enough thought was put into the implications of CC2 on all aspects of the game.

More problematically, not enough thought is being put into the solution to the problem that they created. The current suggestion is just not good, unless there are far more nuanced conditions that they have not revealed. Turtle attempted to be a special snowflake and just created the same problems in its own special way. Sadly, resilience or some form of it is the easiest path forward. It will be much easier and straight forward to introduce gear that negates damage than try to retune every raid, dungeon and mob based on new damage ranges and buff interactions.

Lastly, resilience wasn't even a bad stat in classic wow. Yes, it meant having two separate gearing paths, which was huge problem in retail because of the unforgiving nature of ranking and time sink that was raiding. However, turtle has already announced their intention to revamp pvp gearing to make it a smoother curve. If they already have plans to revamp/add gear it seems that the simplest solution is to add resilience to the gear that they already plan on adding than go through all of the trouble of retuning every aspect of the pve environment.

These kinds of damage discrepancies just dont feel good, as you cant properly gauge how much damage you'd actually be able to do without proper knowledge and experience. At the very least hybrid classes will become unkillable gods if they don't have severe mana issues as counterbalance.

Imo the correct course of action is adding more stamina, armour and resists to most pieces of raid and pvp gear. It fits the vanilla aesthetic more, but it would also warrant PvE readjustments, which might be far too time consuming and nearly impossible without a large playtest. How are the devs supposed to organize 40 players to readjust raid damage intake with all those buffed stats?

Ascension tackled this problem by first having global dmg reduction, ontop of every spell having its own pvp modifier. Both of these lead to huge problems and created a ridiculous shitstorm. Spells would be forgotten to be updated, scaling would break etc.

You'd get more balanced and fun fights if everyone was buttnaked instead.

Either your play a Burst damage class or you lose, which bodes very poorly because I keep on trying to make demonology warlock work. And news flash, it is near impossible with the silly amounts of burst damage coming from Shaman,Disc Priest, Rogue, Feral/Balance Druid, Mage, Warrior. Yes, I listed just about every class.

I agree that you identified the problem. Some combination of reworked talents + overly powerful gear has made pvp a burst fiesta. Coincidentally, Retail wow had this very same problem. Which is why I laugh at every forum post where someone defends this crap storm by saying "go to retail". Guess what, Turtle wow has made the exact same mistake as retail- so we are already on a reimagined retail. Put simply, not enough thought was put into the implications of CC2 on all aspects of the game.

More problematically, not enough thought is being put into the solution to the problem that they created. The current suggestion is just not good, unless there are far more nuanced conditions that they have not revealed. Turtle attempted to be a special snowflake and just created the same problems in its own special way. Sadly, resilience or some form of it is the easiest path forward. It will be much easier and straight forward to introduce gear that negates damage than try to retune every raid, dungeon and mob based on new damage ranges and buff interactions.

Lastly, resilience wasn't even a bad stat in classic wow. Yes, it meant having two separate gearing paths, which was huge problem in retail because of the unforgiving nature of ranking and time sink that was raiding. However, turtle has already announced their intention to revamp pvp gearing to make it a smoother curve. If they already have plans to revamp/add gear it seems that the simplest solution is to add resilience to the gear that they already plan on adding than go through all of the trouble of retuning every aspect of the pve environment.

It's all because of number of players in factions imbalance. There are many more players in Alliance than in Horde. Many players tend to farm AV when they hit level 60 to get rep for mount and other pre-bis items.
What really happened and is the reason why Alliance performs so weak is that AV connects 2 types of players: these who farm their rep and ranked PvPers. They decide not to sign up for AV ever again because they know most of their team mates will be brainless. They go for AB or WSG instead. This disproportion creates opportunity for Horde because they can easilly win AV game without much effort. Thus, more and more Horde's PvP rankers decide to play AV more often for fast honor.

author: toloth9
subject: Idea for dealing with spike damage in PvP
content_md:
I am not sure if this has been suggested or not, but why not have a stat that works like a Brewmaster tank. For example.

Grit: X% of the damage a player takes in PvP gets taken over Y seconds as a damage over time.

Make the damage you do take from the DoT portion a little more than the damage you would have taken, so that players can choose how they want to build their characters. It also changes the PvP meta a little because certain classes will be better or worse or change their spec depending on how much Grit they decide to stack.

For example: Warrior has 15% grit, so he takes 15% less spike damage, that's the upside. The down side is he takes 5% more damage over the 10 seconds the damage is distributed too (so 15% + 5% more damage). Thus the warrior is taking  a little more damage overall, but its less spikey.

Another warrior Might decide he wants 5% grit. He takes more spike damage than the first warrior, but because he chose less grit, the DoT he takes is only the 5% damage he took.(so 5% + 0% more damage)

Warrior 3 has 25% grit, its almost impossible to spike him down with damage, but the the damage over 10 seconds is say 40% , a 15% increase in the damage done overtime. (25% + 15% more damage). This means the warrior is going to take much more damage, but he can hang on longer to secure a kill, or run a flag.

This creates a situation where players can build around the choice of spike damage vs overall damage, and no playstyle suffers more than another.

If players can add grit to any item like they would and enchant, they can choose how much grit they want. The length of the dot effect can be changed to balance, the amount of damage reduction and the amount of damage you take for the reduction can also be balanced as needed, all without affecting PvE or creating the need for 2 gear sets like resilience did. (assuming you can have it stack with existing enchants.) Turn in a warsong gulch mark, and get an enchant for 1 item that say adds 5% Grit.

A few things to consider:

There would need to be no way to negate the damage, for example it would need to damage pallies through bubbles, otherwise all pallies would just use a bubble to negate the large Grit damage DoT.

Depending on how powerful being a healing class is against this damage, an MS style anit heal effect may need to be part of the DoT Debuff. (ie. heals are 10% less effective when you have it, etc).

Just thought I would throw the idea out.

I'm not sure what the mage was doing considering he could've just shimmied forward, nova'd the thing and shuffled away, but, sure, warlock is just OP and no skill issue is involved here.

The fifth fight also involved an infernal and, and sixth clip was him attacking someone who wasn't paying attention to him at all that either couldn't or didn't feel like kiting the thing. Also a resto sham presumably, so you'd kinda be silly to expect them to win that fight anyways.

Seventh fight was an immense skill and gear issue on the mage's part. Starting with icicles is silly because it chunks 30% of your (I think base?) HP upon taking any damage.

Eighth also involved attacking someone who was already occupied, so, yeah, kinda self explanatory.

Ninth was just slaughtering a poor warrior on their mount who would've been fucked either way. You saw all the people tailing behind, I hope.

Numero eleven was- LMAO WHY ARE YOU ATTACKING THE PALADIN THERE'S A HALF HEALTH SQUISHY CLOTHY RIGHT THERE TO DUMP YOUR LOAD ON DUMBASS

Anyways yeah that warrior may as well have not been a factor in the fight. Rushed in, swung at a plate wearer while the felguard was twirling right on top of him with no rage to spend, had no support, and the mage was already getting cooked anyways.

Twelve is just a poor lower geared player trying to swim away with a felguard on their ass and probably having no way to retaliate. Might as well have been a mercy kill.

author: Halfgeek9
subject: Re: Shadow Priest vs Warlock
content_md:
If you ask Spriests, they will say Warlocks far better. More mobile, can kite endlessly with CoEX, can shut down casters with Curse of Tongues, has a pet that can dispel magic on you, while you're stunned or CC by magic like Paladin hammers, and Warlocks can get Ruin for huge crits to instant gib people.

If you ask Warlocks, they will whine that Spriests are better Affliction locks, with more defensive tools, a better dispel, and can always pop out to heal.

IMO, having played both, and main Warlock since 2003, Spriest is a one trick pony. A Warlock has multiple good specs, and hence, playstyles. Spriest gets old & boring real fast.

Plus, Turtle nerfed spriest with VE. While Warlocks got buffed with CoEX, and 2 curses active on one target. ie. Agony damages while you can Shadow, Tongue, CoEX.

Edit: To add, Turtle nerfed Spriest further with Blackout 3s stun -> 2s. It's even more difficult to peel melee on top of you, and Warriors in Turtle gain rage hitting Shields absorbs. But Priest have a viable Smite build when you get ultra geared, just lacking huge fat crits since spell crit only 1.5x not 2x like other casters.

author: Blitzunddonner
subject: Premades ruin Battlegrounds
content_md:
I was wondering if this is acknowledged and whether there is anything planned to regulate this. Its literally unplayable for hours on end to que with randoms vs decked out premades.
Tbh I can't really think of something that would fix this for sure but I think its worth thinking about.

There's going to be 3 or 4 specs that are absolutely monstrous in pvp dominating every single fight, the rest are going to be mid or even worse off than what we currently have.

Take feral for instance. Already extremely tanky but pumps out huge crits as cat and stops you from even casting your spells. So now we can't even burst them down which was previously your only way do deal with them as a caster cause not only do they do absurb damage but now they can tank all your damage without even shifting to bear. They're already as good as immune to CC excluding stuns. Plus they are now going to have an easier time escaping because there are exactly 0 limitations on their ability to freely maneuver and it'll be harder to finish them off before they escape.

feral here isnt geared at all and isnt even opening me as a feral usually would which leaves you at half hp before u even get out of pounce

[embed: https://www.youtube.com/embed/cZ143gK8lKY]

Specs like destruction are extremely reliant on their burst and is practically our only way to win fights. Resilience doesn't help us in the slightest vs melee classes cause we can't cast spells in the first place due to spell knockback. Now our suffering is simply prolonged and melee classes yet again get to feel good about themselves hitting a defenseless child.

![Image](https://gyazo.com/b7786fa2737444d281ca99c4e8c777b1.png)

Vs rogues? Yeah resilience is really going to help us out when the problem isn't surviving but being stunned for eternity while we can't do anything. Warrior intercepts you and coil is now even less useful because they're taking reduced damage from you so you just stand there.. being more useless than usual? In vanilla as a non SL lock once a melee is already hitting you it's game over because you can't cast spells and one swing does half your HP. You can't get away again like a mage can (which is gonna dominate warrior even more now because warr can't get a lucky kill when they do connect XDDD)

There's going to be new class changes to compensate for this which brings us back to the question. Why add global resilience in the first place? A better move would be to give each spec their own values which isn't perfect either but is certainly one step towards fairness.

Idk, I think you've just successfully doubled down on turning pvp into a consume/trinket fest. Only way to survive ferals now is popping lips.

On an off note, cat should now be affected by all forms of CC including seduction.

TL:DR resilience changes are going to accomplish absolutely nothing except making 1sided matchups even more 1sided.

Pets are also going to need some sort of hp & resilience buffs to compensate

author: Grinspoon
subject: Re: Ranks won't go up
content_md:
I'd recommend to look into how the vanilla ranking works. it's a bit of a mess. tldr is that there's a decay that grows with the rank and that means you can't slowly chip away at the next rank. your characters are essentially just making as many honor points as are decaying so it would be best to focus on only one of them at a time.

keep in mind though that to move further up in ranks the amount of honor needed will drastically increase.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Ranks won't go up
content_md:
The way it works is turtle wow still has the "decay" of the ranking points in, but you cant drop further than to 0% od a rank. (Aka you stay rank 9) But in order to ever moveup a rank, you need to overcome the rank decay that you have at rank 9 before you make progress.

You need about 100'000-150'000 honor to even move it up at this point. (But ofc you want more so it moves up quicker)

Twows ranking system allows you to take breaks every rank but is every bit as brutal as it always was to actually climb each individual rank.

author: Membrane
subject: Re: Ranks won't go up
content_md:
It's not about how much honor your make, it's about how much honor you make compared to everyone else that week. If you're farming honor and your rank is not progressing, it means everyone else around you is farming more honor.

From your post, I gather you're trying to rank up multiple chars at the same time. At rank 9-14 you're not going to be able to do this, the people around you will be getting in excess of 300,000 honor per week.

Download the addon HonorSpyTurtle and you'll see your standing along with everyone elses.

<https://github.com/gwetchen/HonorSpyTurtle>

This is not a TWoW thing, this is how it was in Vanilla WoW back in 2005 / 2006. However TWoW has reduced the burden slightly as you cannot go down in rank here, in 2005 if you had a few days / week off, you would lose your rank.

Patch 1.18 has announced some PVP changes, specifically something to help the Rank 14 grind a little less painful, what that turns out to be though currently remains a mystery.
