author: Ellifta
subject: Analysis on why Alliance loses 90% of the time.
content_md:
It wouldn’t be a hot take to say Horde wins the majority of BG matches on this server. When playing on WSG day followed by AB day, as a holy paladin in Kara40 gear I won 7 matches out of 52 I played. Everyone’s welcome to say that I must be really bad at the game and it must be me causing all that, and I’ll gladly take the blame. I got 217k honor last week and that put me at standing 38 for Alliance, which might be interesting for Horde players who are trying to rank up to see how wildly different honor to standing ratio is for the other side.

People tend to open threads in this forum when they notice one specific problem that leads to massive Horde winrates, and are quickly shut down by whataboutism (Example: I got one shot by shaman/ But what about druid T3.5 gear???) and people who don’t know how to refute points or argue. It doesn’t help that Alliance players open these threads without an intention to argue with, but to vent their frustrations, so I decided to make a neutral toned and objective analysis as to why Alliance is losing so often in BGs, from the perspective of a healer in BGs who only plays soloque.

 **1- Paladin vs Shaman Core Design**
The biggest reason I can think of is how bad the average paladin player is and how shaman counters paladins on top of that. For starters, purely from a design perspective a shaman counters a paladin. Purgeable seals and purgeable buffs including freedom give shaman a massive edge over paladin who can’t afford to auto attack shaman’s totems with a slow two handed weapon. Secondly, the counter to a shaman are kicks and silences. Paladins have stuns, but the average paladin player is really bad and only uses HoJ as an opener to start doing their PvE rotation on the shaman while the shaman will just facetank the initial 6 seconds and then wreck the paladin. Because the majority of Alliance plays paladin, on the bigger picture you’re looking at shamans hardcasting a lot of the time because paladins don’t have kicks and that’s what people are playing. It’s actually harmful that people are playing paladin so much, the situation wouldn’t be as bad if Alliance had more casters and rogues. In terms of bursty DPS niche, both elemental and enhancement are far more bursty than AP or SP ret.

 **2- 17 Enhancement Build**
The elephant in the room is the uncounterable 17 enhancement and rest on elemental shaman build which is what a pre-CC2 shockadin could dream of being. This specific build gives shamans massive armour from their gear and their shield and dodge while they’re still able to do 3.5k in one global with guaranteed crits. Anyone with a shield is simply less prone to being critically struck, these shamans are still able to heal decently because they have SP gear. So you end up with a build that is really tanky, has a shield, deals massive ranged damage and can heal. Alliance has no counterpart or counterplay to this other than watching their mortal strikes hit for 450. I know people like to complain about getting one shot by soulfires and whatnot, but to me this is the only objectively overpowered spec in PvP right now. Holy paladin would be a good second contestor, but purely because no one plays healer on Alliance side this goes unnoticed. Holy paladin is incredibly tanky and has insane single target healing, but because it lacks any offensive abilities at all unlike 17 enhancement build, people don’t play it. This build alone accounts for the vast majority of Alliance players quitting BGs due to how annoying it is, which leads us to my second point.

 **3- Gear and Player Discrepancy**
Since Alliance loses the majority of the battles, people who PvP on Alliance side do it mostly to rank up to their desired rank and stop playing. They aren't exactly enjoying the game, but grinding their teeth until a desired rank. They don’t stick around and are quickly replaced by people in greens. I’ve seen people as low as 2.3k HP with kings on Alliance side, people with empty ring slots, people with missing helmet and shoulders, people in level 40 spirit AH gear… In any match, a sizable portion of Alliance players will be walking health packs for Horde players. This wouldn’t be so bad if 50% of Alliance weren’t retribution paladins. A less geared healer is infinitely more useful than a less geared melee DPS. A less geared caster is infinitely more useful than a less geared melee DPS. But as everyone probably notices, Alliance only plays ret paladin. Since good players don’t really stick around, you’ll be stuck healing these people who will just quit after getting one tapped. It’s bizarre to me that as a class that can do 2.7k heals every 1.5 second, I can’t keep some of these people alive against one shaman.

 **4- Melee vs Caster Damage**
Post CC2, it’s safe to say that a lot of casters got quite bursty while melee classes except enhancement shaman and melee hunter didn’t receive any buffs to compensate. When we look at it from the bigger perspective again, Alliance has a lot of melee players in the form of retribution paladins while Horde has a lot of caster players in the form of elemental shamans. Melee works great against clothies, when I equip my Kara40 weapon on my retribution spec (I very rarely play this) I can one-shot low geared horde casters and do serious damage to even high geared casters. However, the fundamental problem is never the priests, warlocks or mages. It’s always this particular 17 enhancement build which reduces my crusader strike damage to 550 on a non-crit and 1000 on a crit. Suddenly as a melee DPS I’m against a caster that deals me 700 in return from their shield against my 550, then deals 3.5k damage to me. I’m literally killing myself playing melee against this particular build, the water shield or whatever it is will wear me down from my own auto attacks. Caster DPS ignores all armour at the cost of being soakable by potions, but guess what, shamans can purge your nature protection potions. In the end, you are in an extremely unfavorable matchup against a shaman as melee, which sadly the majority of Alliance is.

 **What is the Solution?**

There’s unfortunately no short term solution to this extreme discrepancy. I don’t think the recently announced flat damage reduction or healing reduction will solve any of these issues. Things need to be done for the currently low-geared Alliance players to rank up and enjoy the game so hopefully there’s an equally skilled and geared playerbase on both sides in the future. Several things come to mind

 **B) Make Paladin seals undispellable - No brainer, the equivalent of this would be paladin cleaving all shaman totems every GCD.**

 **Unfortunately while I’m fairly confident on things I’ve said until this point, I’m not about the following.**

 **C) Give paladins a seal that ignores armour but deals X% less damage.**
A seal that can ignore armour by turning all damage dealt to holy damage but reducing overall DPS would work and give the equivalent of enhancement shaman capabilities to retribution paladin. Competitive, serious games do not represent the majority of the gameplay and in those situations bans and restrictions can be manually placed. It wouldn’t be a hot take to say Horde wins the majority of BG matches on this server. When playing on WSG day followed by AB day, as a holy paladin in Kara40 gear I won 7 matches out of 52 I played. Everyone’s welcome to say that I must be really bad at the game and it must be me causing all that, and I’ll gladly take the blame. I got 217k honor last week and that put me at standing 38 for Alliance, which might be interesting for Horde players who are trying to rank up to see how wildly different honor to standing ratio is for the other side.

People tend to open threads in this forum when they notice one specific problem that leads to massive Horde winrates, and are quickly shut down by whataboutism (Example: I got one shot by shaman/ But what about druid T3.5 gear???) and people who don’t know how to refute points or argue. It doesn’t help that Alliance players open these threads without an intention to argue with, but to vent their frustrations, so I decided to make a neutral toned and objective analysis as to why Alliance is losing so often in BGs, from the perspective of a healer in BGs who only plays soloque.

1- Paladin vs Shaman Core Design
The biggest reason I can think of is how bad the average paladin player is and how shaman counters paladins on top of that. For starters, purely from a design perspective a shaman counters a paladin. Purgeable seals and purgeable buffs including freedom give shaman a massive edge over paladin who can’t afford to auto attack shaman’s totems with a slow two handed weapon. Secondly, the counter to a shaman are kicks and silences. Paladins have stuns, but the average paladin player is really bad and only uses HoJ as an opener to start doing their PvE rotation on the shaman while the shaman will just facetank the initial 6 seconds and then wreck the paladin. Because the majority of Alliance plays paladin, on the bigger picture you’re looking at shamans hardcasting a lot of the time because paladins don’t have kicks and that’s what people are playing. It’s actually harmful that people are playing paladin so much, the situation wouldn’t be as bad if Alliance had more casters and rogues. In terms of bursty DPS niche, both elemental and enhancement are far more bursty than AP or SP ret.

2- 17 Enhancement Build
The elephant in the room is the uncounterable 17 enhancement and rest on elemental shaman build which is what a pre-CC2 shockadin could dream of being. This specific build gives shamans massive armour from their gear and their shield and dodge while they’re still able to do 3.5k in one global with guaranteed crits. Anyone with a shield is simply less prone to being critically struck, these shamans are still able to heal decently because they have SP gear. So you end up with a build that is really tanky, has a shield, deals massive ranged damage and can heal. Alliance has no counterpart or counterplay to this other than watching their mortal strikes hit for 450. I know people like to complain about getting one shot by soulfires and whatnot, but to me this is the only objectively overpowered spec in PvP right now. Holy paladin would be a good second contestor, but purely because no one plays healer on Alliance side this goes unnoticed. Holy paladin is incredibly tanky and has insane single target healing, but because it lacks any offensive abilities at all unlike 17 enhancement build, people don’t play it. This build alone accounts for the vast majority of Alliance players quitting BGs due to how annoying it is, which leads us to my second point.

3- Gear and Player Discrepancy
Since Alliance loses the majority of the battles, people who PvP on Alliance side do it mostly to rank up to their desired rank and stop playing. They aren't exactly enjoying the game, but grinding their teeth until a desired rank. They don’t stick around and are quickly replaced by people in greens. I’ve seen people as low as 2.3k HP with kings on Alliance side, people with empty ring slots, people with missing helmet and shoulders, people in level 40 spirit AH gear… In any match, a sizable portion of Alliance players will be walking health packs for Horde players. This wouldn’t be so bad if 50% of Alliance weren’t retribution paladins. A less geared healer is infinitely more useful than a less geared melee DPS. A less geared caster is infinitely more useful than a less geared melee DPS. But as everyone probably notices, Alliance only plays ret paladin. Since good players don’t really stick around, you’ll be stuck healing these people who will just quit after getting one tapped. It’s bizarre to me that as a class that can do 2.7k heals every 1.5 second, I can’t keep some of these people alive against one shaman.

4- Melee vs Caster Damage
Post CC2, it’s safe to say that a lot of casters got quite bursty while melee classes except enhancement shaman and melee hunter didn’t receive any buffs to compensate. When we look at it from the bigger perspective again, Alliance has a lot of melee players in the form of retribution paladins while Horde has a lot of caster players in the form of elemental shamans. Melee works great against clothies, when I equip my Kara40 weapon on my retribution spec (I very rarely play this) I can one-shot low geared horde casters and do serious damage to even high geared casters. However, the fundamental problem is never the priests, warlocks or mages. It’s always this particular 17 enhancement build which reduces my crusader strike damage to 550 on a non-crit and 1000 on a crit. Suddenly as a melee DPS I’m against a caster that deals me 700 in return from their shield against my 550, then deals 3.5k damage to me. I’m literally killing myself playing melee against this particular build, the water shield or whatever it is will wear me down from my own auto attacks. Caster DPS ignores all armour at the cost of being soakable by potions, but guess what, shamans can purge your nature protection potions. In the end, you are in an extremely unfavorable matchup against a shaman as melee, which sadly the majority of Alliance is.

What is the Solution?

There’s unfortunately no short term solution to this extreme discrepancy. I don’t think the recently announced flat damage reduction or healing reduction will solve any of these issues. Things need to be done for the currently low-geared Alliance players to rank up and enjoy the game so hopefully there’s an equally skilled and geared playerbase on both sides in the future. Several things come to mind

A) Nerf the 17 enhancement build - This is a no brainer, it’s equally cancerous as shockadin. No caster should be able to do 3.5k damage in one global and have 6k armour + dodge + shield. Moving these talents past the 20 point in enhancement tree can fix this problem to a degree. Shamans will quickly point out to a similar build Paladins can use by taking points in holy and prot tree, but this build has nowhere the same offensive abilities as an elemental shaman does. All you’re doing is trading healing for 10% DR, which can be desired or not, this doesn’t give you any offensive abilities.

B) Make Paladin seals undispellable - No brainer, the equivalent of this would be paladin cleaving all shaman totems every GCD.

Unfortunately while I’m fairly confident on things I’ve said until this point, I’m not about the following.

C) Give paladins a seal that ignores armour but deals X% less damage.
A seal that can ignore armour by turning all damage dealt to holy damage but reducing overall DPS would work and give the equivalent of enhancement shaman capabilities to retribution paladin. To ensure this doesn’t disrupt PvE balance, make it so that the X number is high enough that SoC or SoR deal more in their corresponding gear against targets with 2k or less armour. Ideally this seal should deal more damage to targets above a certain armor threshold but less against targets with less armour such as casters compared to SoR or SoC.

D) Buff direct combat abilities of warriors, feral druid and rogues so that people are less likely to flock on Paladin or Shaman classes.
I think people play paladin because playing warrior is kind of a suicide and other classes don’t seem interesting enough. Instead of tinkering with paladin or shaman, perhaps buffing others to make them interesting could be a choice, but this has the obvious problem of powercreep.

Competitive, serious games do not represent the majority of the gameplay and in those situations bans and restrictions can be manually placed. A) Nerf the 17 enhancement build - This is a no brainer, it’s equally cancerous as shockadin. No caster should be able to do 3.5k damage in one global and have 6k armour + dodge + shield. The problem is that we have too many ret paladins on alliance side, which blocks potential classes like warlocks or rogues getting in the same match who could kick shamans or counter them to a degree. At this point this is a population and percentages problem. Alliance player rolls ret paladin, loses horribly, either grits his teeth until desired rank and quits, or just quits on spot while Horde player enjoys the game so he keeps playing even after he got his gear or rank, leading to very unbalanced sides. This is also why Tel'Abim could be more balanced. Shamans being OP is one problem, Alliance having less geared and skilled playerbase is partially caused by that and other factors like racials, but in the end we have very unbalanced faction playerbase that require dev intervention in some way at this point.
I agree with most of what has been said, however, I've seen most alliance players pvp in numbers out in the open world, or simply mess with low levels, because they plainly suck at pvp.

author: Voodoochile
subject: Re: Analysis on why Alliance loses 90% of the time.
content_md:
This is a fantastic post. I have been working on a Shaman Rework proposal for a couple months and I've been having troubles getting opinions on Shaman in pvp as a whole, but especially regarding the enhance tree, that doesnt feel overtly biased.

CC2 has a lot of issues that I still believe make it an objectively worse class balance state, but I think worst among them were the powercreep inherent in the changes as well as those classes who did not get new bells and whistles. Because while Ele Shaman are a large point for why pvp is so skewed right now, keep in mind that Ele Shaman burst is down from what it was before CC2. But because Enhancement got alot of love from CC2, the balance of Ele was fucked because suddenly they were able to get the improved tank talents on top of the new raid tier increasing the base stats that those tallents were scaling off of. It is all just a poor amount of forethought for the powercreep in the changes they forced forth despite the community backlash.

That being said, this post has been valuable to me as I can now see some points I can improve upon for my Rework idea. Originally I didnt want to touch the enhance tree because it had gotten a good amount right with making enhance feel like a satisfying class to play and I took the tank talents at face value because Shaman tank needs those talents for raid tabking.

But seeing how it affects pvp, I can comfortably say we can afford to move them or their effects deeper into the tree so it cannot be abused by the other specs. Because as it is, and as it was in Vanilla, Shaman tanking was perfectly viable for dungeons, and often better than warrior tanking. So a shaman in the early game while leveling doesnt truly need these survivability talents as they are right now in the 20-30 range where the problematic talents reside.

No. Just find a way to express your skill that doesn't involve looking for places to stand that you hope people won't know how to get to. Alternatively, there are other servers.
Skill in literally all aspects is literally about finding or doing things that newer players don't know how to do. Not just in regards to safespotting, but in how and when you press your keys, your movement, etc.
Knowledgeable, skilled players shouldn't be punished for putting in the effort of knowing the game better than newer players. New players should be encouraged to learn the game so they can actually compete with the guy who's been playing for years and knows all of the nooks and crannies.

Safespotting should only be punishable when it's clearly an unintended area that you shouldn't be able to go to (using class abilities, trinkets or items to reach a cliff or a platform other people can't). People have been jumping on the logs, top of tunnel, and the various buildings in WSG for 20 years and the only barrier to entry in this regard is knowledge or bad spatial awareness, not game mechanics.

It's the flag carrier's JOB to keep the flag away from the other team.

author: pillowed
subject: A Demonology warlock fix is desperately needed
content_md:
The spec that is supposedly the defensive warlock spec is simply impotent. There is no other way to describe it.

Problem 1:
Fear and Howl of Terror are both near un-castable when being attacked by anyone with a twig with greater than 2.5 attack speed. The primary two defensives that a warlock possess are just unreliable. This problem is exacerbated if you are an alliance warlock that basically has to cast 3 fears for one to have desired effect because of trinkets and racials. This is even more ridiculous when you look at the fact that warriors and priests have a more reliable fear than the class known for fear. With the amount of damage most melees are putting out, 1.5 second cast time on a spell that you will probably need to land 3 times is simply too long. In any scenario where you would want to cast "Howl of Terror", a cast time of 2 seconds may as well be a 30 second cast time. And "Death Coil" is simply on too long of a cool down to only affect 1 player.

Problem 2:
The "Fel Domination"/"Master Summoner" combination needs to net to an instant cast summons. The main reason for this spell is to on-demand summon a voidwalker to sacrifice for an emergency shield. The current values resulting in a 1.5 second highly interruptible cast time, that can also be stunned resulting in the loss of the "Fel Domination" buff, means that the emergency void sac is essentially unusable. The same situation applies as above, 1.5 seconds is too long of a cast for a defensive that... well that leads to.....

Problem 3:
The voidwalker sacrifice absorbs far too little damage. If, and it is a big if, you do somehow get a sacrifice off, if you didn't already have a voidwalker summoned, you are rewarded with a shield that absorbs about 1.1 second worth of damage with the absurd amount of damage classes are outputting now. The shield is simply too weak to provide any meaningful or significant relief, especially given that it took you 8-10 seconds and 3000 hitpoints to execute if you are being attacked. Warlocks simply do not have enough mobility to have a shield that does absolutely nothing of significant value. Fear and shields are our only defensive and both are essentially worthless. Especially when you see priests running around with on demand bubbles, and instant cast aoe fears. Mages with blink and a complete10 second immunity that removes all debuffs. Shamans..... well lets not even bring up the absurdity of a class that can burst for 5k+, tank 3 or 4 people while healing themselves through it, and insta-gib people.

Problem 4:
The design of the warlock pets, lesser and greater demons, is just not well thought out. I don't think I'm alone in saying that it would be better to have a permanent pet somewhere between the current lesser and greater demons than to be completely feeble except for every 5 or 15 minutes. Especially when as soon as you throw out a greater demon it becomes a bat signal for everyone to either burn the greater demon down or simply burn the immobile warlock down. It was a good idea to try something new but the power gap between the two is way too large. Valiant effort on reimagining demonology("soul link") warlocks but this is simply terrible in practice. Waiting 5 minutes for a pet to be insta-deleted, banished, or being swarmed as soon as you summon it is just not a good practical choice if you intend to have class balance. Either add more impactful damage modifiers for the lesser demons deep in the demonology tree or reduce the damage output of the infernal or felguard and make one of them a permanent pet for soul link warlocks. Before you say it.... Unleashed Potential is simply bad for pvp. Fishing for crits is not a reliable strategy as a demonology warlock because to get unleashed potential you simply don't have enough points to dump into improved searing pain, the best option to fish for crits when fully talented, to get to the full 10 percent increased crit chance on searing pain. Not to mention, it effects spell damage and as an alliance warlock the preferred pet, the fellhunter, gains absolutely zero benefit from that talent.

author: Allwynd01
subject: Re: There is no more enjoying the game
content_md:
> **ForumGentleman wrote: Mon Jul 07, 2025 8:18 am**
> To be fair, I know many ppl in nordannar that like PVP and would have preferred a PvP server back when they created their characters but they are too much invested right now to reroll in TA
>
>  It doesn't mean 90% ppl on turtle prefer having a PVE server as ppl absurdly claim

I've been on this server since October 2018 and I've seen it when it had 150 players and what people cared about and now that it has 8000+ players and what it's about.

It started as a niche slow server with PvE and RP as the main focus, the XP rate was x0.5 and the point was to relax and do all content and interact with other people, even from the beginning you could join forces with the opposite faction. As the server grew, more people of all walks of life started playing and eventually caused the increase of toxicity. I'm not trying to make a correlation between toxicity in PvP, because it would be illogical and subjective.

Yes, you are right that some people wanted PvP when it was only PvE so that's how Warmode came to be. But even that didn't become very popular. I still stand behind what I said that the population on the PvP server is a testament to how many people are interested and serious about PvP and it's also a gauge how important it should be for the developers to focus on it and pour resources into it.

If people started on the PvE server when it was the only one, but now want to play on the PvP server, but are hesitant, because they're already invested and don't want to start over, this is just an excuse. If they wanted to be on the PvP server so badly, they would have moved long ago. But they don't, either because the population there is so low that they see no point, or because they actually don't want to be on a PvP server that much.

Let's imagine a hypothetical scenario where both servers get merged and it becomes one PvP server - what will happen is that more than 90% of the population will leave and will also be extremely unhappy with the change. This will only make it universally evident that PvP is not popular for the core Turtle WoW community.

It may seem that I don't like or care about the PvP server, but that's not true, I just don't like PvP and am more or less content with the state of the PvE server. I don't want the PvP server to go away, I just want people to stop drawing attention to it, because there is no point. First, it's a waste of internet space and second, there is no potential for it so talking about how it can be better is pointless, because there is not enough community interest in it. People creating thousands of threads about how to enrich the PvP server won't do anything if most people don't care about it. It will only show brand new players on the server that the PvP server is in a bad spot and actually deter them from playing there, effectively ensuring it stays in a bad spot that is potentially getting worse as time goes on. These people need to accept that the PvP server will not have 1000 or 2000 active players and it won't become more alive and either enjoy it for what it currently is and be thankful that it even exists or just give up and return to the PvE server, sure, they won't have open world PvP, but at least they will be able to do instanced PvP and not wait too long or be forced to play with the same few people who want to do it. Sometimes people just need to accept reality and stop with the wishful thinking that them writing letters to Santa will amount to anything, because Santa doesn't exist.

As the server grew, more people of all walks of life started playing and eventually caused the increase of toxicity. I'm not trying to make a correlation between toxicity in PvP, because it would be illogical and subjective.

Yes, you are right that some people wanted PvP when it was only PvE so that's how Warmode came to be. But even that didn't become very popular. I still stand behind what I said that the population on the PvP server is a testament to how many people are interested and serious about PvP and it's also a gauge how important it should be for the developers to focus on it and pour resources into it.

If people started on the PvE server when it was the only one, but now want to play on the PvP server, but are hesitant, because they're already invested and don't want to start over, this is just an excuse. If they wanted to be on the PvP server so badly, they would have moved long ago. But they don't, either because the population there is so low that they see no point, or because they actually don't want to be on a PvP server that much.

Let's imagine a hypothetical scenario where both servers get merged and it becomes one PvP server - what will happen is that more than 90% of the population will leave and will also be extremely unhappy with the change. This will only make it universally evident that PvP is not popular for the core Turtle WoW community.

It may seem that I don't like or care about the PvP server, but that's not true, I just don't like PvP and am more or less content with the state of the PvE server. I don't want the PvP server to go away, I just want people to stop drawing attention to it, because there is no point. First, it's a waste of internet space and second, there is no potential for it so talking about how it can be better is pointless, because there is not enough community interest in it. People creating thousands of threads about how to enrich the PvP server won't do anything if most people don't care about it. It will only show brand new players on the server that the PvP server is in a bad spot and actually deter them from playing there, effectively ensuring it stays in a bad spot that is potentially getting worse as time goes on. These people need to accept that the PvP server will not have 1000 or 2000 active players and it won't become more alive and either enjoy it for what it currently is and be thankful that it even exists or just give up and return to the PvE server, sure, they won't have open world PvP, but at least they will be able to do instanced PvP and not wait too long or be forced to play with the same few people who want to do it. Sometimes people just need to accept reality and stop with the wishful thinking that them writing letters to Santa will amount to anything, because Santa doesn't exist.
I agree on one main thing: pvp forum posts should be more positive. People babbling "thiS iS UtER trash Servor" with zero solutions are honestly just trolling at this point

Personally; I still have way more fun than on SOD - and I think cc2 patch is still mostly positive overall (as in, there are more fun specs to spec in PVP than before). Some stuff should be tweaked for sure

TA already has 1-2k active players. It is Monday now and we had almost 2k so it is FAR from being dead and it is constantly growing

Last point: I dont agree that devshould chose between pve and pvp. A cleverly designed talent will make a class shine in both PVE and PVP

As for content other than class design, I am confident even PVE purists wouldnt say no to a new BG or World pvp quests

author: Thaladar
subject: Fear Classes & Faction Balance
content_md:
I’ve been playing Alliance priest on Turtle WoW for a while now, and I’ve also played both Vanilla and TBC on retail from way before. I’ve reached a point where I really want to open up a proper discussion about fear-based classes and how the Horde racial Will of the Forsaken (WOTF) interacts with them.

 **Core issue**

If you're a priest, warlock, or even a warrior relying on fear, playing against Undead Horde players just feels off. Your primary control ability is often rendered useless on a huge portion of the enemy faction. Fear, Mind Control, Howl of Terror, Seduction, Psychic Scream, they’re all shut down instantly by one racial.

WOTF is not just strong. It’s everywhere. In most BGs, it feels like half or more of the Horde team are Undead. The odds that your fear will be ignored are incredibly high. Even Undead hunters now get WOTF, which is worrisome considering they’re already hard to pin down.

 **Racial comparison**

I understand there are strong racials on Alliance too, like Stoneform and Escape Artist. But there’s a key difference:

- **Stoneform**
breaks Blind and bleeds, but rogues still have tools like Vanish, Gouge, and Kidney. You counter one ability, not their entire kit.

 **Edit 250915:** Stoneform no longer removes blind.*

- **Escape Artist**
is great against snares, but mages have more than just Frost Nova. They have Blink, Polymorph, roots, slows, and kiting tools.

WOTF, on the other hand, deletes the central mechanic of fear classes. It’s not situational. It’s a hard, reactive counter with no cost or downside.

 **Fear Ward is baseline**

Previously, Fear Ward was one of the few tools Alliance priests had to counter WOTF and give their team a shot. Now that it’s baseline, even Undead priests have it. That means a class that already has WOTF now also gets to shut down your fears on others too.

A fear break, a fear immunity, and the ability to deny your fears, that is too much on one character.

 **Perspective from the other side**

What makes this feel worse is knowing that Horde fear-based classes get to use their abilities normally. If you’re an Undead warlock or priest, you don’t have to worry about your fear being broken by a racial every other fight. As an Alliance player, I often don’t even cast Psychic Scream unless I’ve already seen the racial used or know it’s on cooldown.

Every once in a while, I face a Troll or Orc rogue and they actually stay feared. It’s such a strange feeling because it reminds me how these abilities are supposed to work. But those cases are rare.

 **Proposed solutions**

I’m not asking for a nerf out of frustration. I genuinely think there are ways to keep the spirit of WOTF without making fear classes feel worthless:

- **Make WOTF proactive**

Instead of breaking fear, it could give a 5 second immunity to fear, sleep, and charm effects. This would require skillful timing and couldn’t be used as a panic button.

- **Introduce counters or vulnerabilities**

If Undead are going to keep this strength, there should be a meaningful tradeoff. They could be vulnerable to spells like Turn Undead, Shackle Undead, and Exorcism. This wouldn’t break PvP, but would add a layer of counterplay and decision-making, Undead players would have to weigh the benefits and risks before using WOTF.

It would also enhance faction flavor, adding a unique dynamic to facing Undead opponents. Paladins would gain a situational tool that feels thematic and rewarding, not something they can spam. And priests would finally have a reason to use Shackle Undead in PvP.

Of course, this wouldn’t override other CC. Polymorph, stuns, slows, and normal mechanics would still apply. This is about making Undead a little more interactive, not introducing more immunities.

- **Change WOTF to a flat duration reduction**

Similar to the Orc racial, reduce the duration of fear/sleep/charm effects by a certain percentage rather than fully breaking and blocking them.

 **Final thoughts**

Racial flavor is one of the best parts of the game. I love that my priest can shoot a bow and actually deal good damage and that a crit can proc an instant Smite. I love that Starshards got a damage boost and now feels like a real, meaningful spell. These are great examples of how racial identity and class synergy can feel rewarding without being broken.

A lot of people talk about skill, and I think most of us genuinely enjoy pulling off clutch, well-timed plays. I doubt most Undead players feel “skilled” when pressing one button to negate a core mechanic of another class. If anything, introducing counterplay or requiring proactive timing (like the 5 second immunity idea) would actually increase the skill ceiling.

These changes would let us talk about outplaying, not just out-racing. And that benefits everyone.

Would love to hear other players’ thoughts, especially if you’ve played both factions and seen this from both sides.

 **Update after more playtime**

Since posting this, I have also realized that Feral Druids with Berserk are too strong in the same way. They already deal incredible damage and when you fear, they use Berserk, you use Chastise, they trinket and you die.

If Berserk did not remove fear, Druids would actually have to make a choice. Either stay feared or break it and risk being crowd controlled by something else. Right now there is no choice at all, just an instant reset.

What makes it worse is that Feral has no trouble closing the gap on targets, unlike classes that rely on uptime management. From a PvE perspective I can understand why fear removal exists. Warriors have it too. But Warriors are not a hybrid class with stealth and off healing. And in PvE you are expected to bring teammates who handle those mechanics such as Priest Fear Ward and Tremor Totems.

 5 seconds is too short duration in my opinion.

Yeah, I see your concerns about Paladins potentially becoming overpowered against Undead players. If there were actual ways to play around it in PvP, I’d be all for keeping it as-is, but at the moment, there really aren’t.

Again, there are plenty of good racials, including all of the ones you listed.

For instance, yes stoneform is amazing against feral druids, but it would be a stretch to say that it breaks the class. A feral druid against a dwarf priest will still win almost all of the time since they also got a new fear immunity imbedded into their talent tree. However, none of these can be compared to WOTF when it comes to completely rendering certain class CCs useless.

A priest has a 30s cooldown on their fear, and when you have a melee on you this long, you will not be lasting enough. Sure, we have chastise, but that is a global CD and it buys temporary respite. But since we have no means of escaping we are super prone to getting slowed and pinned right after. A horde priest, however, gets the luxury of having their fear actually last 5+ seconds, which is a huge time window since:

 * Your dots get to tick
 * You get to use 3-5 spells where you can damage and heal
 * You get the opportunity to make significant distance between you and your opponent

However, an Alliance priest does not get to enjoy the above luxuries and it's basically an opportunity cost that is incredibly high currently. A racial shouldn't have the power to deny other players this amount of play.

content_md:
Well, I've used to play a lot of pvp as a dwarf shadow priest before patch 1.17.2. However I've never felt like I'm disadvantage against a undead, it was just about timing. Now, talking about racial skills, I see the fear ward change to not be a racial skill more like focused on pve. But I can understand your complaint.

Let's take a look to possible solutions.

 1. Turning undeads as actual undeads (your suggestion):
If it's forever then an absolute no. May make to overpowered alliance priest or pallys (way more that they actually are) when fighting undead players. If it effect lasts for the duration of will of the forsaken would be more acceptable, however, it's still ridiculous that a cc breaking ability could make you vulnerable to a more powerful cc.

content_html:
WOTF, on the other hand, deletes the central mechanic of fear classes. It’s not situational. It’s a hard, reactive counter with no cost or downside.

Fear Ward is baseline

Previously, Fear Ward was one of the few tools Alliance priests had to counter WOTF and give their team a shot. Now that it’s baseline, even Undead priests have it. That means a class that already has WOTF now also gets to shut down your fears on others too.

A fear break, a fear immunity, and the ability to deny your fears, that is too much on one character.

Perspective from the other side

What makes this feel worse is knowing that Horde fear-based classes get to use their abilities normally. If you’re an Undead warlock or priest, you don’t have to worry about your fear being broken by a racial every other fight. As an Alliance player, I often don’t even cast Psychic Scream unless I’ve already seen the racial used or know it’s on cooldown.

Every once in a while, I face a Troll or Orc rogue and they actually stay feared. It’s such a strange feeling because it reminds me how these abilities are supposed to work. But those cases are rare.

Proposed solutions

I’m not asking for a nerf out of frustration. I genuinely think there are ways to keep the spirit of WOTF without making fear classes feel worthless:

  • Make WOTF proactive

Instead of breaking fear, it could give a 5 second immunity to fear, sleep, and charm effects. This would require skillful timing and couldn’t be used as a panic button.

  • Introduce counters or vulnerabilities

If Undead are going to keep this strength, there should be a meaningful tradeoff. They could be vulnerable to spells like Turn Undead, Shackle Undead, and Exorcism. This wouldn’t break PvP, but would add a layer of counterplay and decision-making, Undead players would have to weigh the benefits and risks before using WOTF.

It would also enhance faction flavor, adding a unique dynamic to facing Undead opponents. Paladins would gain a situational tool that feels thematic and rewarding, not something they can spam. And priests would finally have a reason to use Shackle Undead in PvP.

Of course, this wouldn’t override other CC. Polymorph, stuns, slows, and normal mechanics would still apply. This is about making Undead a little more interactive, not introducing more immunities.

  • Change WOTF to a flat duration reduction

Similar to the Orc racial, reduce the duration of fear/sleep/charm effects by a certain percentage rather than fully breaking and blocking them.

Final thoughts

Racial flavor is one of the best parts of the game. I love that my priest can shoot a bow and actually deal good damage and that a crit can proc an instant Smite. I love that Starshards got a damage boost and now feels like a real, meaningful spell. These are great examples of how racial identity and class synergy can feel rewarding without being broken.
I agree with nerfing WOTF, currently is easily the most powerful racial ability in the game, and no racial should be this powerfull in the first place, and plus with the Horde having Fear Ward too makes the thing even worse, is must be a trade off using it, similar to Blood Fury for example, which reduces the healing received while under the effect, for WOTF, players could take extra damage, or do reduced damage, or slower attack and casting speeds for example, while under the effect, that would put a cost or a risk for the benefit of the removing the fear effect.

Another option, as you suggested, is make the use proactive, removing the the fear/sleep breaking effect just making you immune if a fear/sleep spell is cast on you while already under the WOTF effect.
Totally agree. I don't understand why SMeld was nerfed either. I would love to gain insights on how the devs reason around their racial changes since this is just too much.
For Shadowmeld, i think they should make usable in combat like was in WotLK, that's a nice buff and would make the skill useful in both PVP and PVE, it would work similar to Hunter's Feign Death.

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: Fear Classes & Faction Balance
content_md:
**Update after more playtime**

Since posting this, I have also realized that Feral Druids with Berserk are too strong in the same way. They already deal incredible damage and when you fear, they use Berserk, you use Chastise, they trinket and you die.

If Berserk did not remove fear, Druids would actually have to make a choice. Either stay feared or break it and risk being crowd controlled by something else. Right now there is no choice at all, just an instant reset.

What makes it worse is that Feral has no trouble closing the gap on targets, unlike classes that rely on uptime management. From a PvE perspective I can understand why fear removal exists. Warriors have it too. But Warriors are not a hybrid class with stealth and off healing. And in PvE you are expected to bring teammates who handle those mechanics such as Priest Fear Ward and Tremor Totems.

Having a racial that outright deletes an entire school of CC is incredibly bad for Alliance. Here are just a few scenarios where WOTF directly alters game outcomes:

 * Fearbombing ressing players in AV or AB to stop a cap → countered instantly by WOTF, giving Horde more opportunities to secure or deny flags

 * Getting opened on by an Undead Rogue as an Alliance Priest → WOTF prevents your only peel, often a guaranteed loss without immediate support

 * Mind controlling players off LM or AV bridges → broken instantly by WOTF, saving key players who would otherwise be out of the fight

 * Defending nodes or towers → Fear chains to delay or scatter attackers are negated, making Horde pushes more reliable

 * WSG flag room defense → AoE Fear to peel FC escorts becomes irrelevant, allowing clean exits

 * Chokepoint fights like tunnel or bridge → Horde Undead can just run through Fear, while Alliance gets feared back

 * Emergency healer peels → Priests using Fear as a last resort lose one of their only defensive options outside of Chastise

And on the whole skill issue thing, that is just a lazy fallacy. Skill does not make a racial that deletes a core CC mechanic disappear. Players adapt to plenty of CC like stuns, poly and traps without free immunities. WOTF is a get out of jail free card every two minutes and pretending that has no balance impact is ignoring reality.

It needs to be brought up to par with existing talents that do not break the game this badly for the opposing faction.

I do want CC in the game. The issue is that Fear is broken, it's the outlier of all the CCs.
Disorients keep you in place and only last a few seconds, Blind lasts longer but breaks on damage.
Incapacitates keep you in place and break on damage.
Polymorph keeps you in place, heals you and breaks on damage.
Stuns keep you in place, only last 5-6 seconds depending on class.
Fear will run you in a random direction, for a random distance, lasts ~ seconds and can be chained. Can break on damage but is extremely unreliable.
Fear is the most unpredictable CC. When a rogue stuns you, you know precisely how long it will last. With Fear it's completely random when it will break as you're getting chunked for 5k damage.

Other CCs also have consumables to counter them such as FAP. Fear has no such consume, as Horde you either rely on your trinket, tremor totem (which is extremely easy to counter), Fear Ward or WotF. Some classes don't have the option of picking WotF.

WotF counter-balances the incredible potency of Fear. It seems to me like you're the one who doesn't want to deal with it and learning how to play your class effectively. I'd rather see the pvp trinket reverted to its vanilla state than any other change.

Stuns keep you in place, only last 5-6 seconds depending on class.
Fear will run you in a random direction, for a random distance, lasts ~ seconds and can be chained. Can break on damage but is extremely unreliable.
Fear is the most unpredictable CC. When a rogue stuns you, you know precisely how long it will last. With Fear it's completely random when it will break as you're getting chunked for 5k damage.

Other CCs also have consumables to counter them such as FAP. Fear has no such consume, as Horde you either rely on your trinket, tremor totem (which is extremely easy to counter), Fear Ward or WotF. Some classes don't have the option of picking WotF.

WotF counter-balances the incredible potency of Fear. It seems to me like you're the one who doesn't want to deal with it and learning how to play your class effectively. I'd rather see the pvp trinket reverted to its vanilla state than any other change.

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: Fear Classes & Faction Balance
content_md:
A lot of good points have been raised in this discussion, like how WOTF staying as is might mean Priest Fear should become a Horror effect, how Shamans already bring plenty of anti-CC tools, and how cross-faction BGs will only spread that imbalance to both sides. People are also suggesting tuning WOTF to something like a passive resist instead of full immunity. I really like seeing these ideas being discussed because it shows the issue is bigger than just ‘get better’

WOTF is game breaking because it deletes an entire CC school on demand and denies crucial clutch moments. As a Priest, I have zero counterplay. Tremor can be killed, Fear Ward can be purged or dispelled, but this racial cannot be stopped. It provides an incredible and unfair advantage to Horde players. Alliance has nothing even close. Imagine if Escape Artist not only instantly removed every root, snare and immobilize effect but also granted five seconds of full immunity to them. People would riot because it would make entire specs redundant, which is exactly what WOTF does to fear-based classes. In world PvP, whenever I see an Undead player with equal or better gear, I simply do not engage. It is an impossible fight, and no other racial in the game forces you to completely avoid fighting someone like this. That is horrible design for PvP.

I get why people roll Undead. Some like the aesthetics, others knowingly choose an incredibly overpowered edge because it reduces difficulty. Of course they lobby against any change. If that is their mindset, let them leave. Skillful, fair PvP has never been their intention anyway. If WOTF remains as it is, then Priest Fear should become a Horror effect that cannot be broken. And honestly, any nerf should probably come with a free race change for Undead players to quell the rage. But right now this ability is broken, unfair and it needs to be tuned.

subject: Re: Fear Classes & Faction Balance
content_md:
Tauren racial isn't insane. It resets your swing timer, gets pushed back and shares Diminishing returns with other stuns for your classes. So using the warrior for the example. If he stomps and it goes off without an issue, the swing timer on his 2-handers is actually longer than the stun he just did and if you have another stun it now lasts half as long.

THEN you compare the 1% Dodge which is very good and gets better the more dodge you stack and the 1% run speed which makes you the fastest race in the game able to flee or chase down any other race more effectively to the Taurens 5% health which scales linearly.

And for your ambush examples: Guarding Flags in battlegrounds is a great example, setting up an ambush in world PvP as well. And if you are moving from site to site, you aren't guarding your point, you are patrolling. I remember on retail shadow meld was used extensively in the BGs I played.

And cross faction BGs, I can see it now, Paladins everywhere and undead to fill in the gaps while the Night Elves fall in somewhere behind them while the goblins cry in the corner.

author: Larohir
subject: Re: Fear Classes & Faction Balance
content_md:
Racials are in a much better place than they were at launch—Classic racials were a mess.

That said:

Will of the Forsaken is too powerful, and combined with the 2% damage passive (PvE), Undead are now top-tier in both PvP and PvE.

Orc Hardiness should probably be reduced to 10% stun resist. Even then, Orcs remain very strong.

Tauren War Stomp shouldn’t reset the swing timer, but otherwise, Tauren racials are very solid.

Trolls are in a great spot.

Goblins need a rework.

Humans, Night Elves, and Gnomes are well-balanced now after recent buffs.

Dwarves will see a nerf to Stoneform in the upcoming patch, and their passive racial is quite weak. They deserve some dicent and permenant pasive.

Blood Elves suffer from low base Agility, which diminishes the value of their 2% Agility bonus. For Hunters and Rogues, Night Elves are likely better. Consider increasing it to 3% or adding 2% Intellect alongside the Agility bonus.

author: Vrag
subject: Re: Fear Classes & Faction Balance
content_md:
I disagree with this and after reading your post I see zero reason for nerfing WOTF.

"They break my fear" Then CC them again in 3 seconds or chastise them immediately after?
This ability counters enemy priest, warlock, I mean that's how they are as a race. This is immunity to charm, fear and sleep. Undead is vulnerable to all other types. If mage frost nova freezes the undead, that ability won't work.

Gnome has Escape Artist - "Escape the effects of any immobilization or movement speed reduction effect" Should we nerf this because he can escape every immobilization and movement speed reduction? I am a hunter, gnome breaks my concussive shot stun and runs away. Should we nerf this?

You as a priest have psychic scream, mind control, chastise, shackle undead. Feel free to correct me here but this seems like its plenty of CC. You can chastise directly after undead uses will of the forsaken and shackle him.

Warlock has seduction, if you can't kill his succubus, or stun it and in that time kill warlock then you are probably dead. Undead has a slight advantage here, he can break this once. But after 3 seconds he is no longer on the high ground. This demands you control the succubus or kill it and kill a warlock that put dots on you that keep on ticking. You have to act fast. That's a tough situation for many classes but I still don't think we should nerf succubus nor the will of the forsaken because it gives you slight advantage for like 3 seconds.

That's the point of races. Each one has an advantage in something and you choose them accordingly.

author: Odomiah
subject: The best battleground I ever had in my life (10-19)
content_md:
[embed: https://s9e.github.io/iframe/2/imgur.min.html#a/EocTUJ3]

What you see above is utter domination by horde.
What you see above is complete obliteration of your opponent.

 *But what happens when your opponent just won't quit?*

This battleground lasted 1h and 36minutes. I carried the flag for over 1h at least.
This entire time my patience was tested to the fullest.
Countless of runs, countless of calculations of where to go, what cooldowns they have so I can escape...
It was mental breakdown at some points.

We had a fight versus party of geared horde 19s. 3 shamans and 2 priests.
 99% of people would give up after 10 deaths and pointless tries to outdamage the healing potential of their 19s.
But I kept flag.
I kept flag and "cowardly" ran away every time they tried to catch me.
I used all knowledge of map layout I had. Used every single tiny bit of shortcut I can to make the gap between me and a chaser.

No offense to horde, but with three shamans you should seriously do better with totem positioning. I used their lack of battle IQ to fullest and stalled until my warrior guildmate eventually grabs a kill or two.
We even had 2 man down at some point as ppl simply had to leave. Battleground was over 1h at that point.

Still I ran...

They cought me 2 times. But as scoreboard says, I managed to get them two times too. Both crucial times! Got our flags back with, eventual, capping follow up.

Our 15lvl rogue played perfect counterplay when they got me second time! Separated himself from group, went straight to retake their flag. They managed to get him killed but I was fast enough to forsee it and spring my way to him while he dropped the flag. I took it from him and made his effort count!
I will never forget that moment, Barbetruc!

Also our lv15mage Atmena did amazing job with "sheep" spell. Countless times he prevented them from using either heals or fears against us.

Their kill counts are huge but our willpower was bigger.
It would take me 3 pages to write you all epic scenarios that we had in this Warsong Gulch battle, but biggest one happened in our minds!

I want to pay homage to all my comrades in this battleground for not giving up after this slaughter they did to us!
I want to congratulate them for sticking with me on it and carefully playing out plans and actions.
(keep in mind, we did it via bg chat, not discord)

We killed them few times, but all those times were when we planned it and wanted it!

Last fight happened when they lost it in their heads. They went full in our graveyard. But their mistake was that they went in 2 by two... 2 priests... 2 shamans.
Still you'd think they'd have a bigger chance, but people underestimate me. I have 850 hp but my damage compensates for it. Glown's few heals were just enough to give me edge over their entire roster. They made mistake to focus me, while mage was there just conveniently sheep-ing them.
They started going out of mana, heals were fewer on the horizon and they eventually started dying 1 by 1.

We killed them all and left their flag carrier last. Eventually I killed him too, got flag back and used my sprint only to meet their shaman Ypernyteatr running towards our flag. When he saw me, he placed totem to slow me down but my jump was bigger than the gap between  us and I capped final flag.

I don't know how they feel after such a loss.
But we, as total underdogs... we felt amazing!

This bracket surely has something others don't.

Welcome to 10-19 Warsong Gulch.
Antler Song awaits you!

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Think Resto druid is the weakest spec/class pvp
content_md:
Pvp at the moment is extremely bursty and thats definitely having a negative impact on all healers powerlevel.

And while i do think you have a point with barkskins cast time reduction, you reveal that you might have quite a bit to improve about your own gameplay by even mentioning treeform.

Pvp is a lot different from pve. If you just stand there "like a tree" you will of course get jumped. Healing in the current burst meta is not like healing in a pve mmo, the pure dmg output of enemies you wont overcome. But its healing like in a moba, where your heals can buy your allies enough time to hopefully unleash their own burst. So abilities like prowl are a godsend to ensure its your team getting junped, not you. And with a quick regrowth + swiftmend from an unexpected angle, you can save the burst target while giving the enemy not much time to counteract.

Also switching to bearform for that sweet sweet bonus health is vital if you see dangerous casts come your way. You wanna run something like this ans avoid people jumping you in the first place by being difficault to get a hold of

[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/druid?po ... DAIAFAAAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/druid?points=BgQDAAAAAAAAAAAoaABAAAAAAAAAAotAANDAIAFAAAA=)

Tree form massively gets in the way of your best survivavl options in pvp.

author: Thaladar
subject: Woven Wrong: Spirit Cloth Gear in PvP
content_md:
I’ll never forget the moment I lived a Rogue opener with 80 HP left. One more tick of poison and I was dead, but I had just enough stamina to survive, fear the Rogue (thank god he wasn’t Undead), and heal myself + my teammate.

And when you’re farming PvP gear, you need survivability now. You're stepping into BGs half-naked, getting stunlocked by Rogues and nuked by Mages. Every point of Stamina helps you stay in the fight long enough to contribute. Spirit does absolutely nothing in that grind.

 1/ PvP cloth gear needs a rethink. Why? Because Spirit is eating up stat budget where we desperately need Stamina or utility stats like Spell Power or Resilience (a lot of discussions on this atm)

 2/ As a Priest, I’m going OOM anyway in most fights. Spirit regen doesn’t matter when I’m chain casting and trying to stay alive. It’s even worse when you’re still gearing up, every missing point of Stam hits hard.

 3/ Spirit makes more sense in PvE, where you get time to regen. But in PvP, it’s dead weight. It’s time to stop letting PvE stats dilute PvP performance.

 4/ If PvP gear is meant for PvP, then let’s make it work for PvP. Drop Spirit from cloth sets and give us stats that matter in actual combat.

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: Why XFaction  bgs
content_md:
Saying X-Faction isn’t about classes ignores the elephant in the room: racials and faction skew. Paladins and Shamans are not symmetrical, and Alliance doesn’t have anything like WOTF or Tremor Totem.

The whole point of competitive PvP is the pursuit of improvement, testing yourself against equals, not picking the path of least resistance. Many roll Horde precisely because they don’t have to deal with WOTF or oppressive Shaman utility. That’s not about ‘skill,’ that’s about avoiding disadvantage.

If PvP is supposed to be competitive, then fair matchups should be welcomed, not feared – speaking of fear, I look forward to watching Horde Warlocks and Priests get shredded by Undead Rogues. Maybe then we’ll see a sudden willingness to discuss much needed nerfs to racials like WOTF.

I fear that Xfaction will cause players to lose their sense of belonging and honor. While it appears to be one team fighting another, in reality, individuals will feel no attachment to the team, nor will they have any desire to win or lose. At least now, everyone has a common enemy: the opposing faction. Even so, many players don't care about winning or losing. But if this common enemy no longer exists, I don't know what players will be fighting for on the battlefield. When there is no desire to win, the level of combat in the battlefield will decline sharply. Of course, this feeling is not based on any evidence and is unreliable, but that is my concern.

When the battlefield is non-Xfaction, You will face a stable group of "enemies" with a stable group of "friendly parties". But when the battlefield is Xfaction, "friends" and "enemies" cease to exist, and you'll find no meaning in the fight.

author: Moomoobro
subject: Re: PvP Reward Overhaul & New Gear
content_md:
Hi all

I'd like to add a suggestion that builds on what has already been raised.
Turtle has already introduced spec-based variants of Tier 1 to 3 PvE gear so that each class can obtain items that fit their intended role (e.g. Holy/Prot/Ret for Paladins). It feels like a missed opportunity that similar **spec-based variants for PvP gear** do not exist.

A Holy Paladin who commits to the long grind for epic PvP gear should be able to obtain plate that supports a healing playstyle through healing power and spell crit.

In a similar way, there should be **more healing focused Rank 14 weapon options**. A shield with healing power for example would make the Rank 14 grind far more rewarding for dedicated healers. At the moment the climb to Rank 14 is not especially attractive for a healer because only a few of the final rewards are suitable for healers.

Introducing healer oriented Rank 14 items together with role specific PvP armour would make the entire PvP journey far more appealing. I believe this would attract more healers into battlegrounds which would make matches more enjoyable for everyone. Healthy healer participation always improves match balance and helps the whole system feel more dynamic.

Why this would be beneficial
• It brings PvP rewards in line with the existing philosophy used for PvE gear.
• It rewards healers for the significant time and effort required to push high PvP ranks.
• It strengthens battleground balance by supporting all roles properly.
• It creates clear motivation for more players to queue as healers which improves gameplay for everyone.

author: Matches
subject: Quitting AV - PvP problematic
content_md:
I've given up on AV.  I will not play again.

I enjoy AV as a large-scale PvE event; big team, open map, goals.

The PvP part was never anything for me.

PvP I find now is unavoidable, because to come within 30 yards of a ranged character is to die in a few seconds; stun/slow/polymorpth/whatever, then death.

It seems to me if I want PvE, I need to start an AV at the very beginning, so I can get past all PvP to the first GY; if that opportunity is missed, or if you do meet an enemy player (perhaps on defence), then you're back at the start and then you have to wait until SP GY is taken to be able to move forward again, which takes a relatively long time.

In any event, the frustration of PvP is now so great and so difficult to avoid that AV for me is unplayable.

author: Thaladar
subject: Discipline Priests and Burst Damage
content_md:
Priests have traditionally always added moderate offensive support. In arenas and battlegrounds they could throw out instant casts on the move and, if they weren’t healing, they could still pressure with Smite, DoTs or Mana Burn. Leaving a priest unchecked was always a mistake because they would slowly turn the fight in their team’s favor. The twist was that priests are the least mobile class. Once a melee was on you, you were stuck unless your team peeled.

On Turtle WoW, healing priests now deal burst damage that rivals or even exceeds pure DPS specs. This comes mainly from Searing Light giving instant-cast Smites on critical hits. You often see a Smite cast followed by an instant Smite, both critting, which can delete an opponent in seconds.

No other healing class comes close to this level of damage. This playstyle always, always trumps traditional pressure like Mana Burn. At the start of my PvP journey against priests I thought, “Are you really going to damage me with Smites while I mana burn you?”

Guess what? Deleting an entire health pool beats removing small amounts of mana with a three second cast time. That spell is no longer even accessible in the Discipline tree for the 2.5 second reduction, making Mana Burn a niche option compared to just blowing someone up.

I've also started abusing rank 1 holy novas when getting targetted by melee classes to fish for instant proc smites, which usually generates a considerable amount of instant smites, letting me kill melee classes with ease. It feels very wrong to do this.

Instead of pure burst power, I’d rather see more skillful tools added back to the priest arsenal:

 * Add a self-damage spell like Shadow Word: Death to help avoid CCs (either introduce a new spell or revamp Mind Spike by letting it have this mechanic + reduce its CD to 10 sec)
 * Return Improved Mana Burn to the Discipline tree for strategic play
 * Improve mana management, because priests spend 90% of their playtime drinking, which is ridiculous

I hear you. Healing paladins and resto druids don’t come close to this kind of damage output, and even resto shamans only really contribute to burst indirectly through things like Windfury totems. Disc priests, on the other hand, can personally delete people in seconds. That’s the core issue I’m pointing out in this thread.

On the burst meta overall, I’m writing this because I want devs to have a balanced view on PvP. I’m not here to nerf only what hurts priests (like my WOTF thread). In this thread, I’m pointing out that Disc priest burst is not necessary. It’s fun, and it helps in PvE and leveling, but in PvP it warps the meta by letting a healing spec delete players in seconds.

That’s why my suggestions focus on adding skillful tools that counteract the burst meta, not on making priests weaker overall:

 * Better mana sustain – more relevant in a meta with less burst, since right now priests must kill quickly or go OOM fast
 * A Shadow Word: Death-style mechanic – to break CCs like Poly or Blind when no cleanser is nearby
 * Making mana burn viable as a pressure tool

We are healers with strong damage potential, but we are still healers first.

I don’t share that view at all. Discipline is fundamentally a healer tree. It gives us tools to prevent damage through shields, reduce incoming damage, and improve our healing efficiency. That defensive foundation is why Discipline has always been considered a healer spec, not a DPS spec.

What makes it feel different on Turtle WoW is the burst potential tied to instant Smite procs. Right now, the best choice 99% of the time is to just spam Smites, which pushes us away from using our full support toolkit like offensive/defensive dispels or Mana Burn.

We are healers with strong damage potential, but we are still healers first.

In my humble opinion there are couple of problems with pvp on turtle wow.

 1)Unnesesary creation of tel'abim as pvp server.

 - tel'abim should been HC realm with transfer to other servers if player reach lvl 60 and chooses to transfer.

 - population of pvpers on nordanaar before of creation of tel'abim was more healthy, players that both pvped and pved had best of both worlds, more people to do pve with and more people to pvp with, in both open and instanced situations.
I wouldn't be suprised if there was more pvp action on nordanaar than in tel'abim.

 2) Strange pvp balance, I know its hard to balance pvp in an mmorpg, MUCH harder than balancing pve, but still, you should try do it, turtledevs. cc2 changes had devastating consequences on turtle wow, why you just didn't copied talents from tbc with some small changes? things would be so much better...

 3) Recent warmode changes - WHY? So unnesesary and pointless...

Devs, please dont focus only on pve, youur server is probably best option to play wow right now, and could be much better if you focused on pvp too.

Horde base has multiple stacked chokepoints such as IB GY hill, the multiple narrow paths leading into the main fortress, and towers with archers covering every angle. Alliance has no clean way in.

Hello everyone. I apologize in advance for my English, I did this with a translator. I am a bad writer and this is my first post.

I'm opening this because no one else has done this and I want to know everyone's opinion. My main character is a mage and alt priest. I consider myself a very skilled mage player and pretty bad priest, so I'll give my opinion on mage and a little bit on priest.
I think durability changes are a terrible idea because these changes only work in a vacuum with the abilities you changed yourself. Some abilities really have a toxic design like arcane missiles(u still have counter play to that for every class), overtuned dots and etc. In the previous patch, almost every class had a burst that could kill another character in seconds and in my opinion, each of these characters could be countered or outplayed if you knew how. Yeah, the balance was off, but it was fun (maybe because I'm wearing the best gear in the game), but still. What did damage reduction and healing bring to this game? I can't speak for all classes, but I can definitely speak for the mage and a little bit for the priest. The mage was not changed except for the arcane branch, and when all the damage was cut, not only did everyone's least favorite arcane got worse, all other mage abilities that have very poor scale and were not changed from vanilla classic became absolutely unusable. So right now if you want to compete as a mage you have no options, you just cant use AoE abilities and only hard cast abilities for 2.5 seconds, but for this patch when rogues run 100% move speed and they have at least 5 buttons to break CC, well and other classes have interrupts and CC, you just can't do it, but if u still managed to do ur 2.5 cast you still dont have damage to even scratch the enemy. The post is already too long I think, so I'll say a few non-professional words about the priest in this patch. I feel like priest is in a really good spot (maybe little bit op), after shaman nerfs on purge and durability patch, they are almost invincible for some classes to kill. For example shields wasn't nerfed so warriors right now have no rage at all when attacking priest. You have 10% all magic reduction so for mage its impossible to kill priest too (and basically mage cant kill anything in this patch, but i can cry forever so im waiting good mage player opinion on patch). Right now its only class that can dispel and have biggest amount of buffs in the game. Not nerfed shield, nerfed shaman (against priest), makes this character super strong. Reduced healing doesnt matter that much because heals was already super strong(on my priest i have crits for 4+k ez). To sum it up, the absence, if you remove burst damage from the game, healers will become invulnerable, characters with hard cast will be unplayable.

To sum it up, the absence, if you remove burst damage from the game, healers will become invulnerable, characters with hard cast will be unplayable, but overtuned dots will be meta (it is already, but its just insane how big of an issue for pvp dots was before this patch, but after its too strong even for this server). And i dont understand rogue buffs, it was one of the best pvp character, but rn its broken. Their run speed is so fast they just teleporting with desinc to me. Its not even funny see people running mount speed for 30 secs can break all cc's and nuke people. And keep an eye on blind, because i feel like its a mistake with code or something, but when they did change blind to phys effect diminish cd doesnt not exist anymore. So you can be blinded for 20 secs straight.

Thanks all for reading. Maybe this post is too long and boring but im glad if u read this all. I will really glad if you guys place your opinion on durability patch here, on every character and how it feels like.

author: Snoof
subject: Re: Durability patch
content_md:
It's just made the game that much more unplayable for people who don't have top tier gear.

My warrior's in T1, and don't get me wrong, I wasn't exactly popping off every game before the patch either, but I **was** doing **something**. If a squishy got careless and let me get on them while their shields were down, I could still punish that.

Now though? Nothing dies. The only targets I'm even remotely able to damage are the poor fucks in the same camp as me. I dump my entire combo into priest shields twice without breaking them, because apparently we nerfed damage and healing but left shielding the same? It kind of just sucks to play.

I totally get the thought process behind a general damage squish, but it's just way too simplistic of a solution. It feels like an underbaked attempt at a band-aid fix for something that, realistically, needs to be worked on exhaustively if TurtleWoW is ever going to have anything approaching 'good' PvP.

Could start by disabling all the broken consumables & profession items. Bit tired of watching tiny, CC immune and unkillable druids rocket across WSG with my flag at 240% MS.   neutral_turtle_head

author: Thaladar
subject: How do you actually counter Warlock + Infernal in arena?
content_md:
I keep running into Warlocks with Infernals in arenas and I genuinely don’t see the counterplay. The Infernal alone is hitting for around 1k a swing, and at the same time the Warlock is free to apply DoTs and chain CC. Even if you try to play defensive behind a pillar, the damage just keeps coming.

Some people suggest “just kill the Infernal,” but as a caster that feels nearly impossible with Curse of Tongues making every cast so slow. If I turn to attack the Infernal, my partner is still under pressure, and meanwhile the Warlock continues to cast freely.

Is the only practical answer really to have a Warlock on your own team to Banish it? Was this interaction actually intended for arena / pvp?
