author: Hammerfall
subject: HOW TO FIX PVP IN TURTLE WOW!!!
content_md:
right now twow pvp feels like its lacking all kinds of love. its been years that this server has been out and we're JUST NOW getting some kind of pvp update for arenas and gear changes ect...i really hope the devs see this and take it into consideration.

HOW TO FIX PVP

ARENAS
 ---
 1. add arena queue system to the global list where players can queue up ANYWHERE around the world. not just in a vague hidden room inside the capital cities. there were many times players would ask and wonder "where can i queue arenas?" thats bad. make it to where players and queue ANYWHERE.

 2. if you dont plan to have conquest points be a thing, PLEASE make it to where arenas give GOOD honor gains so it gives players an incentive to do them. theres a reason your new custom bg never gets queued because there is no incentive to even do it. if your new custom bg gave alot of honor per win/loss players would wanna do it. and same applies to arenas. make it to where arenas give GOOD honor. not just 200 per win and 50 per loss...should be maybe like 2000 per win and 1000 per loss as an example. you just need to make sure whatever it is you want players to do for pvp there is a good reason for them to do it. if the only way to get pvp gear is honor. why waste your time doing something that gives little to no honor?

 3. add a global leaderboard for the top 2v2 and 3v3 teams that players can see to add more competitive feel to arenas. maybe add the leaderboard somewhere noticable in the main city or as a ui component people can check at the bare minimum.

BATTLEGROUNDS
 ---
 1. battlegrounds seem ok there isnt much that needs to be changed for bgs. BUT it would be nice to see a new bg that is smaller in scale like maybe a 5v5 bg so its more skill based rather than numbers based when it comes to fights.

WORLD PVP
 ---
 1. consider maybe adding objectives around the map that give good honor gains for players. because right now the only thing players do for honor is bg bg bg...we need something different besides spamming bgs. some ideas for objectives could be maybe honor/marks of honor airdrop system that drops a couple of airdrops randomly around the world where players from each faction could compete to capture for rewards, and the loot goes towards whichever faction loots or captures the airdrop ect

 2. maybe also increase the amount of honor gained from kills in the open world compared to bgs and arenas so players feel a better reason to get honorable kills in the open world rather than only in bgs and arenas.

PVP GEAR
 ---
a big issue with pvp gear right now is that its generally weaker than pve gear in most cases. and we dont even have good pvp off pieces like rings, capes, trinkets ect that are better than pve off pieces which forces alot of pvp players that DONT wanna raid or pve to start raiding in order to have "BIS" gear...and it sucks. pvp players dont log in to pve...they wanna pvp. thats it. so here are ways to fix that.

 1. we need to adjust the pvp gear stats. i know some people complained that adding resil to gear will cause a divide and now pve players wouldnt be able to compete much in pvp ect with their hard earned tier gear. so an easy fix is to NOT have resil and instead adjust the pvp gear stats to match tier gear. pvp gear should have the stats of tier gear in pvp and weaker in pve. for example a rank 8 chest piece should have the same base stats as a tier 2 chest piece and the equip and set bonuses should only count towards pvp, so to compare...a rank 8 chest piece equip effect gives +50 healing done in pvp just like how a tier 2 chest gives +50 healing done BUT in pve the pvp armors equip effects dont count much because it only works in pvp so they arent as strong in pve. or instead of making the pvp gear equip effect and set bonuses not work for pve you can make it weaker in pve like +50 healing in pvp and only +15 healing in pve ect

Rank 7-10 rare blue pvp gear/weapons should have the base stats of tier 2 gear and the equip and set bonus power level of tier 2 gear ONLY towards players in pvp.

Rank 12-13 epic purple pvp gear/weapons should have the base stats of tier 3 gear and the equip and set bonus power level of tier 3 gear ONLY towards players in pvp.

if you impliment this system, pvp players can focus on farming ONLY pvp gear without being forced to raid..and still have an even chance against pve players with tier gear. and PVE PLAYERS will also have a chance to still compete in pvp if they want with their tier gear because there is no resilience involved ect.

PS: PLEASE ADD PVP RINGS, NECKS, CAPES, AND TRINKETS with this same system i just mentioned above in mind, rank 7-10 pvp off pieces should also be as strong as tier 2 pve gear and rank 12-13 off pieces should be as strong as tier 3.

THATS ALL. DO THIS AND PVP WILL IMPROVE DRASTICALLY ON THE SERVER.  turtle_in_love_head

PS: if you need any advice on balancing or any other pvp stuff im willing to help the dev team with those ideas for pvp aswell.

author: Torze
subject: Re: HOW TO FIX PVP IN TURTLE WOW!!!
content_md:
I really like the ideas already mentioned, and I’d love to expand with a few more that could add variety and depth to PvP without breaking the classic feel:

- **Outdoor/Open-World PvP objectives that grant BG reputation**
Hold towers/banners, flip supply depots, or secure crossroads checkpoints in contested zones. Rewards: a small amount of WSG/AB/AV rep (plus modest honor/marks) so world PvP feeds into BG progress. *Safeguards:* per-day cap, diminishing returns on repeat flips, and a short “hold” timer to prevent ping-ponging.
- **Daily/Weekly PvP quests**
Examples: “Win 3 WSG,” “Earn 25–50 HKs in contested zones,” “Escort a supply caravan,” or “Disrupt an enemy objective.” Rewards could be honor, BG marks, rep, or light consumables. *Anti-cheese:* level-appropriate HKs only and account-wide lockouts for the weekly.
- **Smaller BG designed for lower brackets (no mounts)**
A tight 5v5 or 8v8 map for 19/29/39/49 brackets with 8–12 minute rounds and simple objectives (King-of-the-Hill or a short flag run). No mounts; emphasis on utility and skirmishing so newer players learn objectives before larger BGs.
- **Faction Supply Runs / Escort Missions**
Periodic caravans moving between outposts; both factions get a zone-wide ping when one spawns. Attack/defend for honor/marks/rep, with shared credit to encourage grouping. Scales to zone level so lowbies aren’t griefed.
- **Rotating “Call to Arms” zone**
Each week, one contested zone offers bonus honor/rep/objective credit. Moves weekly to keep hotspots fresh and spread the action around the world.
- **PvP currency-sink vendors**
Cosmetics and fun utility purchased with BG marks/honor: faction banners, tabards, camp standards, duel flags, city recall pennants, etc. Purely cosmetic/QoL to avoid power creep while giving long-term goals.
- **Profession-linked PvP missions**
Engineers craft temporary barricades or gyro-turrets for world objectives; Alchemists deliver field rations/medkits; Tailors/Leatherworkers turn in supply crates. Lets non-combat roles contribute meaningfully to PvP efforts.
- **Underdog honor scaling**
If one faction is under-represented in BG participation that week, grant a small, temporary honor/rep bonus (that tapers as balance returns). Helps queues without punishing the majority.

Rewards: a small amount of WSG/AB/AV rep (plus modest honor/marks) so world PvP feeds into BG progress. Safeguards: per-day cap, diminishing returns on repeat flips, and a short “hold” timer to prevent ping-ponging.
  • Daily/Weekly PvP quests
    Examples: “Win 3 WSG,” “Earn 25–50 HKs in contested zones,” “Escort a supply caravan,” or “Disrupt an enemy objective.” Rewards could be honor, BG marks, rep, or light consumables. Anti-cheese: level-appropriate HKs only and account-wide lockouts for the weekly.
  • Smaller BG designed for lower brackets (no mounts)
    A tight 5v5 or 8v8 map for 19/29/39/49 brackets with 8–12 minute rounds and simple objectives (King-of-the-Hill or a short flag run). No mounts; emphasis on utility and skirmishing so newer players learn objectives before larger BGs.
  • Faction Supply Runs / Escort Missions
    Periodic caravans moving between outposts; both factions get a zone-wide ping when one spawns. Attack/defend for honor/marks/rep, with shared credit to encourage grouping. Scales to zone level so lowbies aren’t griefed.
  • Rotating “Call to Arms” zone
    Each week, one contested zone offers bonus honor/rep/objective credit. Moves weekly to keep hotspots fresh and spread the action around the world.
  • PvP currency-sink vendors
    Cosmetics and fun utility purchased with BG marks/honor: faction banners, tabards, camp standards, duel flags, city recall pennants, etc. Purely cosmetic/QoL to avoid power creep while giving long-term goals.
  • Profession-linked PvP missions
    Engineers craft temporary barricades or gyro-turrets for world objectives; Alchemists deliver field rations/medkits; Tailors/Leatherworkers turn in supply crates. Lets non-combat roles contribute meaningfully to PvP efforts.
  • Underdog honor scaling
    If one faction is under-represented in BG participation that week, grant a small, temporary honor/rep bonus (that tapers as balance returns). Helps queues without punishing the majority.

I support reverting Hand of Sacrifice to its original CC-break behavior.

From a class-design standpoint, Paladins rely on reactive support mechanics to remain competitive. Removing the CC-break made HoSac strictly weaker than equivalent tools available to other TWOW classes:

Warriors keep Berserker Rage (fear/charm break)
Priests retain Fear Ward + instant defensives
Rogues / Hunters maintain reset mechanics (Vanish / Feign Death)
Mages still have layered CC + self-cleanse

HoSac was Paladin’s only ally-oriented anti-CC trigger, giving tactical depth in PvP and coordinated play.
Without it, the spell becomes a net loss: damage transferred to the Paladin with no compensating utility for the target.

Technical recommendation:
Restore the CC-break on damage,
or introduce a controlled variant (e.g., internal cooldown on CC-break activation).

This preserves Paladin support identity and aligns with the defensive tools other classes retain.

– Sybril Dawnbreaker, Knight-Champion of the Light, Nordanaar

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: FIX HAND OF SACRIFICE PLEASE!!!
content_md:
To be fair, Paladins are one of the best healers in the game currently, so them not having this is probably reasonable from a balancing perspective. I don't like passive effects like this that are almost entirely uncounterable (unless dispelled) counter a lot of CCs without even thinking.

One good example of a reactive spell that breaks certain CC effects on allied players is Chastise - but that costs a global CD and a potential interrupt. This is a good trade-off. HAS didn't really have any negative trade-offs and that feels wrong.

The thing is tho, Warrior fear has a lot of counters:

 * Tremor
 * Wotf
 * Fear ward

Without these counters, yes, Warrior fear is extremely powerful. However, this is usually not the case.

Blind on the otherhand, it almost always secures 1n1 wins for Rogues since if you trinket kidney, you are blinded and the Rogue resets. Not to mention in group plays where blind can be used to shut down other players, and where the rogue can make other hack plays like vanish + sap them since they will probably be out of combat.

As a Priest with maxed survability (almost max resilience, 40% armor mitigation with innerfire, almost 5.5k HPjust waiting for R12 now which will unlock even more stamina + more resilience), geared Rogues hit extremely hard still and are impossible to fend off myself, especially if they are Undead. Having this amount of oppressive DPS along with extremely potent CC and with arguably the best survability in the game (stealth which allows you to choose favorable positions) makes for a really powerful mix.

However, on the other hand, balancing has always felt like they try to balance melees vs frost mages. From that POV, I understand a lot of the Rogue changes, but this means that it makes Rogues even more oppressive against immobile classes like Priests. Again, its a team game I know that, but I do feel like its important to lift these things. Personally, I would not mind this change as much if they gave other classes more tools like:

 * Priest Pain suppressions
 * Priest / Warr iceblock/divine shield mass dispel
 * More instant heal casts (Prayer of mending, lifebloom)
 * Shadow word death mechanic where you can skillfully use it to get out of polys (or sap)

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: PVP DAMAGE MIGHT STILL NEED MORE OF A NERF?
content_md:
As a Priest with the following PVP-centric gear:

 * Almost maxed resilience
 * 5.5k HP w sta buff
 * 40%  armor mitigation w inner fire

I would have to say that I survive a lot better when getting focused by geared players - casters or melee. In TBC with maxed resilience I could often survive against two players for quite some time, but not here. I think it's fair to go down vs two DPS.

However, mana is a big issue behind this spec. Mana runs out quickly and this is usually what kills me. On the other hand, I see a lot of raid gear healers without this mana issue, like other Priests and Druids. On the other hand, they die like flies when focused. Paladin and shaman healers seem to be absolutely unkillable tho if played correctly and they seem to have very little mana problems.

Also, I do think that LOS is an extremely important aspect here vs casters. If you face casters in the open, your odds of winning decrease substantially. So, you need to be around LOS-objects in order to mitigate a lot of the damage. This is not always available tho.

content_md:
I haven't played arenas on new patch yet but I have seen they are in poor state. I mean, everything in this patch was high quality and tested except the PvP content.

On day 1 there was a bug that you couldn't kill a person from same faction in xfaction arenas. That means, the xfaction arenas weren't even properly tested in terms of "is everything working right?". If 2 teams joined Arena and they all were from same faction, the game couldn't be finished! Devs had to disable arenas for a short time because of that.

Rated arenas were also bugged. If your team won, the system would count it as a lose and decrease your rank.

These 2 bugs lead me to conclusion that the Arenas were added in rush and they weren't even in alpha state. They were literally unplayable. This is not quality I would expect from Turtle WoW.

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: is it true that only horde cries about interracial battlegrounds??
content_md:
I would love to see to see statistics on BGs with:

Baseline - as is
Scenario - pause all racials

Of course the Horde is going to win a lot more simply due to the fact that they have extremely overtuned racials like WOTF and now also fear ward. As an Alliance priest, this has sealed way too many games in the Horde's favor since fear bombing is simply not an effective strategy against Horde. However, the Horde can employ this strategy without getting WOTF countered. I wrote a big thread about this here: [viewtopic.php?t=20248&start=70](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=20248&start=70)
CCing packs of players win games, and if one faction can simply remove it with ease, then it doesn't take a nuclear scientist to understand which team is going to prevail.

However, I do agree with a lot of posters here that usually Alliance classes like Paladins do not use their entire toolkit like cleanse. When I rank, this is a daily occurence: getting polied infront of 5 paladins, that totally ignore me hahaha.

With this said, it needs to also be said that a Shaman at noob level performs better than a Paladin at noob level since the Shamans have so many oppressive tools that dent the team much more. Shocks, tremor/slowtotem/grounding totem and purge are very effective and will probably always be used by Noobs. Noob paladins, on the other hand, will probably only use their DMG abilities + stun + rep + bubble on themselves.

author: Matches
subject: Tried AV after changes
content_md:
Tank, 60, 5k health, 423 defence, mostly the best epics you can get from crafting/AH.

The PvP nerfs have not made a difference.  It seems to me players have come to be doing *so* much damage that a 20% nerf doesn't make a noticeable difference.  I was killed from 5k by a mage casting arcane missiles twice - died half way through the second cast.  His missile crits were doing 808 damage - I guess before they were doing 1k damage. subject: Re: so whats the play vs rogues
content_md:
> **Yavamar1 wrote: Thu Sep 11, 2025 5:26 pm**
> I've always felt like stealth is kind of a bullshit mechanic. It doesn't even require you to be stealthy, you basically just walk around in the open completely invisible unless someone happens to get right up on you.

Its particularly bad on turtle wow actually, because the server's polling rate for stealth detection seems to be about 1 second. Either that, or the actual detection distances are completely wrong, could be either. I've had perception popped against a rogue with no +stealth gear and no +stealth talents, and he walked right up to my face and opened on me from the front without me detecting them, its really annoying. I've genuinely given up trying to bother detecting rogues, and I just try to break them out with abilities

Also, its 4 second cheap shot, 6 second kidney, not 3 and 5.

Cheap shot -> hemo -> hemo -> 5 second kidney -> hemo -> blind -> restealth -> sap to wait out cheap shot DR -> back to cheap shot -> hemo -> hemo -> cold blood eviscerate.

That's the subtlety rogue rotation, assuming at least cold blood and blind are up, so 5 hemos and about 15 second of autoattack on you worth of damage, plus the guarnateed crit eviscerate. Most people can't survive the full chain, and if you trink the blind, you have about 2 seconds before they prep and re-blind, but that burns a 10 minute cooldown to do that, so really only a handful of times per bg. It also assumes you can spend at least 45 seconds uninterrupted in a BG, which is highly unlikely.

I've run across far more backstab rogues in pvp rather than the full combo sub rogues, they just stun you and backstab you twice and you just get deleted, but that's a gear diff at the end of the day. Just like getting windfuried by a shaman with hand of rag.

content_md:
> **Thaladar wrote: Thu Oct 09, 2025 6:29 pm**
> Played BGs yesterday and I’m convinced now more than ever that
>  decurse needs a big buff. I spent the entire BG spamming decurse, using 2 GCDs and 2x more mana due to this ridiculous double curse nonsense  warlocks have .

I think dots need a significant overhaul in pvp in general. They are too oppressive, and deal far too much damage for such a tiny action economy investment.

I can think of a few ways to do it. Significantly reduce dot duration on players, kinda like how sap and sheep were made to only be half duration vs players, but give it a slight dps boost to compensate for the added need to recast more often. This would make it so that dots require actual intent to maintain on someone rather than a fire and forget tab dotting of the entire enemy team.

Alternatively, limit dots to a single player, if you cast a dot on a new player, all instances of your dot on other players are immediately removed.

Neither of these changes would affect pve either, so no complaints from the pve crowd for that.

While I understand the sentiment I think this suggestion is taking it too far. However I agree that warlock dots feel just too oppressive, on top of their dark harvest nuke. Affliction warlocks have talents where they can put 2 curses in one GCD (works for certain curses, but I feel like these are used all the time). On top of this, they have dispel protection talents.

Priest dispel is quite good since it removes 2 magic effects, however decurse classes can just remove 1 curse per GCD. With the double curse talent where you get 2 curses in 1 + dispel protection, a Druid or mage needs to spend 2.3 GCDs removing this from one target. But locks spam dots on several targets so you’re left with a choice: either you waste all cds dispelling curses
Or you let them be active, which begs the question of why we even have decurse if it doesn’t counter curses?

They could get hit with a kick, and need to stand still, but dot classes just stay at max range spamming their spells with zero repercussions. My suggestions either make dots a single target problem, or make them require more active investment to maintain. I would be fine for something like even a 20-30% increase in dps, but reducing the overall damage of a full set of dots down to like 2k. That way they actually need to maintain them rather than just going afk and picking their noses for 30 seconds while their dots do the work.

content_html:
I think dots need a significant overhaul in pvp in general. They are too oppressive, and deal far too much damage for such a tiny action economy investment.

I can think of a few ways to do it. Significantly reduce dot duration on players, kinda like how sap and sheep were made to only be half duration vs players, but give it a slight dps boost to compensate for the added need to recast more often. This would make it so that dots require actual intent to maintain on someone rather than a fire and forget tab dotting of the entire enemy team.

Alternatively, limit dots to a single player, if you cast a dot on a new player, all instances of your dot on other players are immediately removed.

Neither of these changes would affect pve either, so no complaints from the pve crowd for that.
While I understand the sentiment I think this suggestion is taking it too far. However I agree that warlock dots feel just too oppressive, on top of their dark harvest nuke. Affliction warlocks have talents where they can put 2 curses in one GCD (works for certain curses, but I feel like these are used all the time). On top of this, they have dispel protection talents.

Priest dispel is quite good since it removes 2 magic effects, however decurse classes can just remove 1 curse per GCD. With the double curse talent where you get 2 curses in 1 + dispel protection, a Druid or mage needs to spend 2.3 GCDs removing this from one target. But locks spam dots on several targets so you’re left with a choice: either you waste all cds dispelling curses
Or you let them be active, which begs the question of why we even have decurse if it doesn’t counter curses?
I mean, I think dots in general are just too problematic in pvp, there's a reason why resilience specifically targeted them in future wow expansions. Right now, a full suite of dots, something like 2-3 gcds from a dot class (spriest or warlock) can do upward of 6k damage. 6k damage for a set of casts that are not interruptable, can be done on the run, and can be done from max casting range, and they can then focus entirely on being defensive while their dots do all the work.

Like, at least mages when the pull off their nuke combos need to charge up a spell, then channel a follow up spell. They could get hit with a kick, and need to stand still, but dot classes just stay at max range spamming their spells with zero repercussions. My suggestions either make dots a single target problem, or make them require more active investment to maintain. I would be fine for something like even a 20-30% increase in dps, but reducing the overall damage of a full set of dots down to like 2k. That way they actually need to maintain them rather than just going afk and picking their noses for 30 seconds while their dots do the work.
IDK I don't think all DOT classes should be compared to Locks, Spriests have 1 dot, not 1000 like Locks do for instance. Problem with Locks is that they just have way too many tools on top of this absurd damage

author: madferret
subject: Sooo... AV NPCs
content_md:
Are we ready to admit that fully upgraded Champion NPCs stats, combined with their insane 1min respawn rate, is just unbearable to play? Once fully upgraded, turtles turn into purely bot pvp, where you're just trucking against these insanely fast respawns while also dealing with the defenders of the opponent team.

I didn't like the Resources mechanic introduced in later expansions, felt like a cheap way to solve the issue of eternal turtles, but I do think that there is room for improvement. Here are a couple suggestions off the top of my head, feel free to shoot them down and add yours:

 - The obvious one: increase the respawn timers for base NPCs such as roaming guards and archers. GY guards are more manageable and they play an important role in strategy, but the roaming NPCs do not add anything to the experience and feel more like a chore than a mechanic. A horribly dull chore at that.

 - Alternatively, remove Champion upgrades, and limit them to Veteran rank. That is still an incentive for players to upgrade NPCs, but the result is more manageable. I still believe the respawn rate is the main issue though.

 - Another one could be turning off the respawn rate altogether in very specific circumstances -turtling related ones. For example, if both towers/bunkers are burning, and still there's no progress being made, and HKs do not yield honor anymore, make base NPC guards gradually stop respawning, the same way archers stop respawning in destroyed towers/bunkers. Maybe the trigger could be "X amount of defending players die in their base", similar to Reinforcements, but in a way that losing all your Reinforcements doesn't automatically win the game. This wouldn't remove turtles on its own, but it would allow for the deciding factor to be player vs player combat, and not this nonsensical race against the respawn timer of both NPCs and players.

IDK, call me naive, I do not care about ranking up efficiently, and I like moderate turtle AV more than flat out "ignore each other and full on PvE race to the finish line", but the amount of NPCs in Twow AV, their power, and their respawn rate just make turtles plain unfun after 1h~

author: Itztravels
subject: Warrior PvP Under-tuning in Patch 1.18 Scars of the Past
content_md:
Warrior PvP Under-tuning in Patch 1.18 Scars of the Past
Summary

Warriors lack any root or immobilize in PvP. Hamstring remains a melee slow with cooldown, rage-cost, and miss penalties. Result: severe inability to stick to targets.

Current state (Patch 1.18, released August 15, 2025)

Patch 1.18 added new zones, dungeons, PvP tweaks—but no Warrior control tool changes indicated. Counterattack remains removed.
Turtle WoW
Turtle WoW

No signs of restored Improved Hamstring or any root in talent trees.

Core issues

No root/immobilize. Warrior has zero control tools for movement disadvantage.

Hamstring limit persists. Still a melee-range, rage-cost 50% slow with 6s cooldown and subject to dodge/parry/miss.

Rage dependency. Warriors get no rage from ranged or absorb hits—rage remains pay-to-act and must be earned through melee.

Engagement gap. Charge remains OOC; Intercept costs rage. Resources spent to engage slow down your follow-up.

Competitive contrast

Other classes maintain consistent, ranged peel/control tools:

Hunter: Concussive Shot, Wing Clip (proc roots, 3s CD).

Rogue: Crippling Poison II slows 70%.

Shaman: Frost Shock—50% slow, ranged.

Mage: Multiple frost slows/root abilities.

Warriors have nothing comparable in patch 1.18. No ranged gap closer. No root. No talent slow alternative.

Proposed solutions

Restore Improved Hamstring as root talent. Even imperfect chance would introduce control.

Remove Hamstring cooldown. At least allow repeated pits on connect.

Make Intercept resource-neutral or rage-generating. Ensures arrival doesn't drain rage needed for control.

Add in-combat Charge via talent. Provide gap closer without penalizing combat flow.

If miss occurs on Hamstring, grant fallback. Example: short self-speed buff on fail to reduce zero-control dead-time.

Behavioral scenarios to illustrate the problem

Duel: Warrior fails Hamstring → target peels, stays out of melee, completely nullifies threat.

BG/world PvP: Warrior engages, pays rage for Intercept, swings once, slow lands or not—target uses trinket or kite space. Warrior has no tool to re-engage or stick.

Any class matchups: No class is forced to stay in melee. Every class can reposition or range away indefinitely.

author: Donfel
subject: Re: Nerf rogue's dissolvent poison
content_md:
Dissolvent poison by itself isn’t really an issue — the problem is how the spec works. You are gona use Envenom to spent combo points, which gives you +30% poison proc chance. That’s why everyone is using fast weapons. But the funny part is that 1 CP = 12 seconds. It literally requires zero setup — you open with stun, ambush, or garrote, and you already have a 12+ second buff. In that time, you can kill anyone.

I respect team for trying something new with Assassination, but this is just a bad idea. When your passive ability does over 60% of your total damage, there’s clearly a problem. You just can’t design it that way.

The simplest and fast “nerf/fix” before reworking the spec. would be to make Dissolvent deal physical damage — but that wouldn’t solve the main issue.

Poisons should be supportive, not your main source of damage.They should rework Envenom to be like in TBC/WotLK — I mean a buff that increases your poison proc chance based on combo points, 1s+1 second per CP. If rogues want to use Dissolvent after that for more passive damage, that’s fine. But for more damage over time or in PvE, you’d use Deadly Poison like in TBC/WotLK. Envenom can still hit hard, but it should require proper setup.

author: Therokh
subject: New player looking for advice
content_md:
Hello! I'm new around here and I'm looking for some advice for PvP.

Before we start let's get some things out of the way: I'm both a PvE and PvP player, favoring PvP a bit more. Yes, I read all the complaints about the state of PvP, yes I know the devs are mostly focused on PvE content. I don't pretend to have an amazing open world PvP experience or anything like that, I'd be content with having a good experience in BGs and Arenas. Yes, I know PvP gear is lacking. As I mentioned, I enjoy PvE as well so I wouldn't mind getting my gear there.

Also, I've never player classic, only TBC onwards and I haven't touched WoW at all in a while so I'm a bit rusty on everything.

That being said, I'll list the classes/specs I like playing so maybe you guys can orient me on what's viable here:
 - Frost mage, my beloved. I love the poking playstyle and the defensive tools it has to keep the melees away. I've read about the addition of icicles and it seems like using that on PvP would be the worst idea ever, am I reading that correctly?
 - Warlock, my second beloved. I like playing around LoS, poking out to reapply dots and sneak in channels while my demon pesters my opponent. I favor affliction locks and I don't really like playing the bursty builds, so if that's the only viable option I'm probably not going to play warlock.
 - Shadow priest, not my absolute favorite but really fun spec. I read that fears are quite underpowered rn, is that so? If so, is this spec viable? It depends a lot on its fears.
 - Rogue, the only melee I tolerate playing. It seems like the PvP spec was remade into a support spec, so I guess I'm not playing rogue at all? Is there any PvP viability? How is the new Assassination spec?
 - Shaman. I've never played Shaman, but I heard good things about it. The elemental spec is the only one that catches my eye, so if it's viable and it has OK tools to keep the melees away, I might give it a go. I remember them having a nasty AoE stun totem that always got me when playing rogue vs them, but I'm not sure if that's in classic or what other tools they have.

Thanks for reading if you made it this far.

author: Thaladar
subject: Resto Druids Are Bottom Tier – They Need Love
content_md:
I have been running a lot of arenas lately on both my disc priest (geared) and a resto druid alt (bad gear but still playable with the right teammate). And honestly resto feels like the weakest healer choice right now.

 **From my priest’s perspective it is a free win.** Priests strip every HoT. Shamans used to purge them dry, and even with the new purge CD (which helps a little) they still have plenty of ways to interrupt casts and negate CC. Paladins are even worse, because BoF and Cleanse remove every bit of CC and control a druid has. On top of that the recent buff to Blind means Abolish Poison no longer clears it. That was one of the few skillful counters druids could pull off and now it is gone.

 **TWOW has already taken plenty of abilities from later expansions.** Shamans got Water and Earth Shield. Priests got Chastise and Fear Ward baseline. Paladins gained buffs and quality-of-life improvements. Meanwhile resto druids got nothing. They need some form of unique advantage that makes it worth playing them, because right now there simply is not one.

 **In battlegrounds it feels even worse.** Facing mass locks stacking DoTs, I cannot understand why HoTs are not stackable. Why? If a warlock dots a team against a druid he should be worried that HoTs will negate that pressure. Instead druids crumble. Warlocks have too many tools. Endless DoTs, pets that silence, death coil, fear chains, curses. Meanwhile the druid toolkit offers nothing in return.

 **Back in TBC arenas I hated facing druids with Lifebloom and Cyclone.** They were oppressive. But in TWOW it feels like they actually need those tools just to have value. And honestly I think it would even be healthy for the current meta. Right now everything is so bursty that matches often end in mindless tunnel damage wiping people instantly. Cyclone would pause that flow, forcing players to think twice before charging headfirst into a druid team.

 **Some ideas that would make resto viable**

 * Cyclone for resto (and maybe balance) so they at least have one reliable CC and a way to slow down the burst meta
 * Barkskin usable while CC’d so they are not helpless vs deep fury warriors
 * Abolish Curse to deal with lock spam the same way Abolish Poison deals with poisons
 * Swiftmend tweaks like not consuming a HoT or being usable off the GCD
 * Another HOT like lifebloom + talents with anti dispel embedded (why do locks get this for their dots but not druids for their hots?)

And if I would be so bold, give druids a unique tool entirely. Something like a stun ward, akin to Fear Ward for priests, that would remove or prevent a stun once. Rogues are out of line right now, and a stun counter would be a perfect way for druids to carve out a unique identity.

Resto druid is meant to be the HoT healer but in the current bursty meta with constant dispels, warlock spam, and rogue stun chains this design just does not work. Unless they are given something to stand out they will remain an afterthought which is sad for a spec that should feel unique and rewarding.

Then there is the gear situation. The honor set is feral. The arena PvP sets have no leather healing options. I was planning to gear up my resto druid through PVP, but with the current state of the class it just feels pointless. Every other healer has a PvP path and druids got left out.

 **What do you guys think, have you managed to make resto work or is it really as bad as it seems?**

author: Eveq
subject: PVP in Tel`Abim
content_md:
What the hell, guys?

I used to play Horde in Battlegrounds and couldn't understand why Alliance had such problems in PvP. In percentage terms, Alliance wins only 15% of all Battleground fights. Now I've experienced it firsthand. And here's what I discovered:
 1. Shamans are overemphasized. Throughout the entire fight, they press four buttons, dealing incredibly high damage that can't be reduced or controlled. In raids, they heal with just one button.

 2. Rogues. I don't know who came up with the idea of ​​making an already easy class with their primary poison spells so powerful.

 3. Druids, in Moonken form, press just one button throughout the entire fight and heal just as well.

Where do you get this idea from?
You can't make the PvP world so unbalanced.
Have you guys ever played Battlegrounds for the Alliance during testing? People are leaving for other projects because this unfairness is unbearable.

By the way, I'm thinking about it too. I'm not particularly offended. I can press the right buttons and fight back. But I think this imbalance towards the Alliance is unfair.

You're trying to balance this system. You're creating a ton of patches, but you can't fix what's most important to all the players who come to this server. The PvP content here is simply terrible.

I've never seen such a factional imbalance on any project.
Why should one faction have to endure these tough fights, while another just comes in and wins without putting in any effort.

The project is good, but the PVP content here is a complete disaster. It's no wonder there are no more than 2,500 online players, while the PVE servers are thriving. Tel'Abim isn't a PVP game, it's a one-sided game...

author: Silverhand2156
subject: Re: PVP in Tel`Abim
content_md:
Despite how much horde whines about paladins, the difference between the two faction exclusive classes is pretty massive.

Paladins are very durable but no chasing power, no kiting power and virtually no range. Meanwhile shaman have an extreme amount of all three of these, while being able to do enough ranged damage to kill multiple people before getting into trouble. And they're still more than durable enough to handle getting into trouble for a bit unlike most casters.

There are a lot of paladins on alliance side but more than a few of them in a BG is almost a guaranteed loss as it means horde ranged players are just mostly safe from harm, severely crippling any chance for the alliance team to actually inflict crippling losses on the horde team

author: Vaikaris
subject: It's shocking you haven't implemented crossfaction pvp yet
content_md:
You have this wonderful server where it's about 100% perfect and everyone more or less agrees and then you just let the turd that is PvP on ambershire fester and stink the same way pvp on Nord ended up. You even have a decent sized pvp community here - fine, you treat us like garbage, you spit on us by removing warmode and even in its current state leaving it bugged for months (it still switches itself off after log off or even BG). Fine, you promise us updates and they never come. Fine, you tell us you're testing resilience and will implement it and years pass. Fine, you introduce a cool system like the arena, pay no attention to how overtuned the gear is, patch it up with making it hugely difficult and not balanced still and leave it as is. Fine, you keep buffing classes that dominate in pvp claiming they're "bad" and need help.

Ok, you made a PvE server because all pservers were pvp and you're not happy people want to pvp here. I get it. We all do. It's fine.

But why, for the love of god, have you not introduced crossfaction queues yet!? How is that even possible? For years pvp on Nord has taken a very clear direction that shows faction dominance completely ruins the whole thing. It makes casuals quit, it makes it extremely annoying to rank because you either lose a lot or have to play like crazy with long queues. Hell, it even creates ALL the imbalance issues - shamans will one-shot everyone while insta healing at no mana cost and having all the tools in the game so everyone knows they're awful to play against while shamans themselves are most OP at whining and they whine about paladins. These are the faction specific classes. Literally all that is instantly solved with crossfaction queues, done, dusted, fine, nobody will care any more.

And I know I'll probably get some mysterious explanation about how "it's coming" or "pvp update on its way" but jesus christ, we know you won't do it, we've been playing here long enough, we know the attitude towards pvp, ITS FINE, just do crossfaction queues. Just do it. Remove the tumor before it completely destroys pvp on Ambershire which is already 90% of the way to Nord status where there's 0 fun, tons of anger and nobody is happy. I don't know how simple crossfaction queues are to implement but the amount of work cannot be NOT worth saving thousands of your player's sanity, goodwill and interest.

author: Zvyrhol
subject: Re: It's shocking you haven't implemented crossfaction pvp yet
content_md:
Lore stands against cross-faction idea and that's a big thing on RP-PVE server. While it would be good in terms of game balance (Paladins and Shamans for both teams and unified queue), lore reasons are impossible to ignore. That concerns ALL battlegrounds except Arenas.

In Warsong Gulch we have conflict between Orcs who want to settle and cut down the Night Elves' sacred forest.
In Alterac Valley we have conflict between Frostwolf Clan that is allied to the Horde and Stormpike Guard. It's leader is Drek'Thar who was Thrall's tutor. And Stormpike Guard is expedition sent by King of Ironforge.
In Arathi Basin similar situation.

Allowing Night Elf to help Orcs claim their sacred forest is absurd.
Fighting against Frostwolf Clan and its leader Drek'thar as an Orc - the friend of Trall - is absurd.

The problem is that all these conflicts are connected with Horde and Alliance.
In normal lore-friendly world if such Nigh Elf returned to Darnassus, he would be hanged or whatever.
Same with an Orc who sabotaged his own faction.
content_html:

In Arathi Basin similar situation.

Allowing Night Elf to help Orcs claim their sacred forest is absurd.
Fighting against Frostwolf Clan and its leader Drek'thar as an Orc - the friend of Trall - is absurd.

The problem is that all these conflicts are connected with Horde and Alliance.

subject: Re: the Shaman hybrind ench/ele problem.
content_md:
I think both sides are kinda correct.
Let's be honest, a build with respectably high SP shouldn't have 6000+ armor and a custom instant strike which scales off SP (next to the 5 sec CD shocks).
Even if we ignore things like shaman utility, (now bad) purges, interrupts, slows etc, you get something which kills you from afar and outlives you if you close up the range.

But yeah, TWOW initial push for pala made the class way too popular. PVP is somewhat rock-paper-scissors and if 70% of the playerbase at Alliance plays the same class, Horde classes countering that class will eat up Alliance teams because of bad comps.

I think enh-ele is a bit overtuned but also, Alliance team comps are just bad.

author: Steakhouse
subject: Which server is best for BG levelling ?
content_md:
Hello, I'm interested in levelling whilst doing BGs, including arenas. Basically I want to always be in a BG queue while I level, and join whenever they pop, questing only during the downtime ; however, ideally, I'd like questing to be the smaller part of my XP: the more BGs the merrier. If you're familiar with that, I'm thinking a similar experience as when Tel'Abim opened : I reached rank 4 before level 10 because arenas were constantly popping, and that was AWESOME !!

I'm especially interested in a server than doesn't have too much twinking, as they immediately defeat my interest in BGing at that bracket. I would much rather fight, and cooperate with, other players that are, like me, simply BGing to level. Of course, running into a twink every now and then is fine, but for instance, it's my understanding that the 10-19 bracket of Nordanaar is infested with twinks, which simply isn't my cup of tea.

I played for about an hour on both Ambershire and Tel'Abim and did not see a single BG start for any level bracket. Have announcements for BGs been removed, was I unlucky, or do the English-language servers simply not offer the possibility to level through PvP ?

I also speak Spanish so the SEA servers are an option, if they would fit that bill ! :)

Thanks for reading !

author: Terrydavis
subject: Alliance strategy guide for AV
content_md:
Hi
I will keep this as short as possible:

 1. this map was ruined by some angry pro horde dev roughly 1.5-2 years ago
 2. all other devs dont seem to give any fucks

i could go into detail about how the map was ruined, what mistakes were made and such but see #2.

this will only end with cross faction. turtle wow has accumulated such an insane horde bias over the years there is no more fixing it with minor changes. that bridge was burned long ago.

here is the problem reduced to the minimum:
 **horde defending their base automatically wins them the game.**
this always works. all you need to do as horde is let 5 people defend and you win with almost certainty.
this is because of #1.

so horde does this every single game now.
since the 90% horde winrate has existed for an entire year now i assume no one here gives a fuck about AV anymore.

so what is the correct alliance strategy?
its very simple actually. **you want to lose as fast as you can.** this is the mathematically correct way to play the map now. trying is a mistake and just wastes time. its simply not a fair map anymore.
---
 -do not lose ibgy under any circumstances

 -when initially attacking ibgy dont be greedy and rush towers. we will lose anyway so we can take those later.
just dont die and get sent north. just sit at ibgy and wait for the flag before doing anything else

 -do not attack TP, the horde abuses their spawn now to defend that shit every game. just dont bother anymore.

 -refuse to fight horde => this one is very important. do not let horde defenders have fun killing you. theyre griefers. ignore them, dont fight them. just let them sit there. if they dont leave their npcs just go afk at ibgy. make them quit the game. do not play into their hands. their entire strategy revolves around baiting you into their endless hordes of npcs. thats all they do every game.

 -dont actually try to win, that will just be frustrating. **just do galv and go afk after that and let horde end.**

author: Thaladar
subject: Rogue stunlock kill condition is out of control
content_md:
It has reached a point where the stun-lock kill condition from rogues is completely disproportionate. If a rogue opens with Cheap Shot into Kidney Shot, many classes have no functional counterplay. The fight ends before the opposing player is allowed to act. That design philosophy removes skill expression from the interaction.

If rogues are allowed to maintain this instant kill pressure while the opponent is stunned, every class needs significant buffs to protection mechanics. Examples include:

• Nature’s Grasp or Bear Form should trigger while stunned.
• Warriors should be able to activate a shield while stunned.
• Priests should be able to apply shield while stunned and/or get tools like pain suppression.
• All classes should have at least one reactive survival tool that is not disabled by the stun itself.

The stealth advantage remains the strongest opener in the game. If the design team considers it acceptable that rogues can erase someone from full health during a stun lock, the inverse must also hold true: when a rogue loses stealth and is caught, the kill condition should be fully reversed onto them. Fairness requires symmetry. If they get to delete others with zero interaction, they should be just as vulnerable when the situation flips.

The intent here is not to demand a direct nerf, but to demand balance in how combat initiations and crowd control function across classes. Either reduce rogue opener lethality or bring all classes up to a level where counterplay is actually possible.

If the developers truly believe this level of one-sided stunlock gameplay is acceptable and does not require adjustment, then at least provide an optional battleground queue without rogues. Those who enjoy stealth-based hide-and-seek can fight each other and express their “skill” through stunlocks, while the rest of the player base can participate in PvP without being instantly deleted before pressing a single button.

This change is not aimed at bringing in new players, or pushing engagement metrics by forcing arbitrary goals on players. The players sitting in queue for 3 hours are already accessing pvp, and are already (trying to be) engaged, this change is just making them spend more time actively doing the activity they want to be doing, rather than sitting around in a queue.

An analogous change aimed at accessibility and engagement would be something like giving loot boxes from pvping that contain high end pvp gear at the end of each match. Engagement: force people to pvp now for rewards when they were previously just pvping for fun. Accessibility: spam ungeared players with gear so they can participate in pvp (welfare epics).

Now, that being said, I'm actually all for increasing accessibility to pvp, though I think the above method would be an absolutely atrocious path to do so. I've already participated in numerous threads discussing ways to make pvp more accessible without ruining the landscape of the rest of the game, but that's beyond the scope of this thread.

author: Odlnn
subject: Restrict Premades!!!
content_md:
Hello everyone,

You all know that feeling: you wait in a 30-minute queue, only to lose the game in just 5 minutes. When this happens, it just makes you want to stop playing.

How is this fair? We're all here to farm honor, and when we get matched against players who get a free win, it feels like a huge injustice. Allowing premades in random battlegrounds corrupts the entire ranking system.

 **Objection: "A five-person premade can't have a huge impact in a 10v10 or 15v15."**
This is wrong for many reasons, but the most important one is that battlegrounds are often unbalanced. We frequently play 5v5, 7v8, or 6v8. Even in a 15v15 battleground like Arathi Basin, a premade can bring 3-4 healers while we have one, or even none.

 **Objection: "Just create your own premade."**
Premade games are an entirely different type of game. It's not the same as a random queue. You have to form a team, set up a Discord channel, inspect everyone, assign roles, and so on. The way you play in a premade is completely different.

But I don't want to do that. I just want to play the game after work. I want to play, not lose 5-0 in Arathi Basin in just 3 minutes.

In conclusion, I want to say this: I am not food for worms. I would gladly wait five times longer in a queue than go through this experience. Many people feel the same way. When we face the same premade over and over, we just stop playing. And when this happens, it kills the battlegrounds activity. Please notice this.

 **My Suggestions:**

 1. Restrict premades by making them only play against other premades. This might mean they never get to play, but you could create a separate ranked battlegrounds system with bonus honor to accommodate them.

 2. Restrict premade groups to a maximum of 2 people. Even two coordinated players can be tough to beat in a situation like 4v6 in Warsong Gulch, but it is at least acceptable.

I know many people enjoy playing in premade groups, but on our server (Ambershire), it has simply become a tool for farming honor unfairly.

author: Azcron
subject: Re: Restrict Premades!!!
content_md: If we’re going to argue that premades in battlegrounds are unfair and should be restricted, then we need to apply that same logic to guilds raiding together. Guilds are essentially long-term premade groups with massive advantages: they coordinate strategies, assign loot, optimize class balance, and run content on a schedule. Compared to pugs, guilds can farm BiS gear with far greater efficiency and consistency. Pugs wipe more, struggle with communication, and often get locked out of progression entirely. If fairness is the priority, then allowing guilds to raid together is just as “unfair” as premades in PvP. But we don’t ban guild raids, we accept that teamwork and organization lead to better results. Battlegrounds should be no different. The real issue isn’t that people play together, it’s that the system doesn’t account for the imbalance. Let’s fix matchmaking and honor incentives instead of punishing players for forming groups.

content_md:
I see you all are very smart, talking about philosophy, the social aspects of MMORPGs, and other intellectual theories.

But with all due respect to these high-minded ideas, you are missing a simple point:

 **The existence of premades kills all PvP activity the moment they start playing**. Let me explain it in simple terms:

A formed premade **kills** 10vs10 and 15vs15 Battlegrounds from the moment they queue. When people face the same premade for 2-3 times **THEY STOP PLAYING**. The result is simple—Battlegrounds like Arathi Basin and Warsong Gulch just disappear from the queue. I have even reported this issue to the GMs.

I know it's very cool to talk about philosophy, but the consequences of allowing premades are not healthy for the game.

author: Ellifta
subject: Mass Hordoid Exodus in Nordanaar PvP
content_md:
Back in summer I shared my experiences PvP'ing on Alliance side and explained how we'd lose 80% of our matches due to several factors, but mainly due to lack of player skill and gear on Alliance side, overpowered shaman specs and discrepancy of caster ratio on Alliance vs Horde side.

Since the announcement of cross faction battlegrounds, suddenly Alliance is winning a lot more than before. Sometimes with big score differences too. I would go as far as saying my experiences have been flipped playing the last 2 WSG and AB day. Alliance still is majority melee, but seems like a lot of good Alliance players made a come back.

Was this cross-faction announcement in itself enough to tip the balance in favor of Alliance? Obviously my experiences in last 2 weeks as one person doing moderate amount of PvP (150-200k honor) is not a big sample size. Yet, I've seen the typical Horde premades not playing anymore and straight up giving, suiciding when they realize they aren't fighting 2.6k HP retribution paladins anymore. It really blew my mind to see people who used to pubstomp a few months ago now AFK'ing in graveyard when they lose the first flag in WSG, without even attempting to fight back.

Are shaman players that used to auto winning every game with their broken specs that, the chance of meeting another one scared them bad enough to stop playing or even trying altogether? Are they afraid of having a green geared protection paladin with 2.8k hp on their team instead of 7k hp shaman? If someone has any other explanations as to why suddenly Alliance is stomping in WSG and AB, please say so, otherwise it seems like sealclubbers scattered away like the rats they are upon fighting equally geared and skilled opponents.

I don't disagree with anything you said, but I think you're looking at it from the wrong perspective. Cross faction PvP makes PvP more fun by spreading good players around. It also takes care of melee-heavy Alliance and caster-heavy Horde we're so used to. I don't think it was meant to make classes more balanced. All it does is put up new scenarios that didn't exist before (shaman+paladin in same team) and massively shake up the usual players you'd see on one side.

Weak classes will still stay weak, but now it's less likely that you will get curbstomped due to class imbalances. Your team is as likely to have strong classes/players as the other team. This doesn't mean it will always work, but beforehand it was heavily in favor of Horde with both better players and stronger classes. Now people can't pile up on Horde with race changes and whatnot.

I did about 12 battles so far, both have been pretty... unique so to say. At least it's a fresh experience and entertaining for now. It seems extremely chaotic at times, but I've yet to make a conclusive comment about scenarios like shaman getting healed by paladin while fighting another shaman scenarios.

In other words, what you are criticizing wasn't the intent of the change so I think your criticisms are not valid.

author: Snippao1
subject: Is THIS the PVP problem?
content_md:
HI guys,
ive seen lots of topics about how broken or weak some classes are and here is the sum up:

 1- Rogues: Stunlock and kills you with bugged poisons
 2- Shamans: insta kill with burst in elemental spec OR can tank and cast like a mage in enhanc spec.
 3- Paladins: hero class. Stun, bubble, bless for every situation and hits hard.
 4- War: Very high physical dmg and their weakness to roots seems to be gone
 5- Lock: Infernal and doom wrecks in arenas. Not a real problem in BGs.
 6- Mage: Seems to be somewhat balanced. Frost has always been the CC master. Fire we ignore. Arcane has a huge dps but u have to stand still with your very low HP pool making this a fair tradeoff.
 7- Hunter: A joke in pvp. Like a bonus kill. The team with more hunters lose the match.
 8- Druid: Healer is ok. Kitty is nothing compared to rogues. Bear is decent. Boomkin needs his opponent to wait for like 10 procs to happen for him to cast his starfire and have his 15-20% chance to actually BOOM his oponent. Still less BOOM than ele shammy.
 9- Priest: Dont really know about it.

is this accurate guys? What would u add to this list?

author: Turboman
subject: Re: Is THIS the PVP problem?
content_md:
I will speak for druids only.
 1) Resto is dogshit, even with dedicated gear and talents our HT cast speed is too slow to try to keep teammates alive and regrowth costs a lot of mana to be viable. Hots are getting immediately dispelled/purge by priests and shamans with a minimum of 60 iq, so casting them most of the time is a waste of mana.
 2) Cat is actually in a good state, very good dmg output thanks to the new energy regen talents. Comparing them to rogues is silly because rogues are overtuned right now (a rogue with white daggers should not be able to kill t3 warrior in seconds, but i quess devs have a different vision).
 3) Bear is very good
 4) Moonkin is mediocre in both game mods. The dmg output in pvp is laughable, spells hit like a wet noodle, heals cost a ton of mana, on the other side there is a shaman that can literally one shot you with fast flameshock+molten blast combo while healing like crazy with cheap and fast heals. I main moonkin in pvp and it sucks in comparison to pretty much every class including other "hybrids" shaman and paladin, even fury warriors now have more fucking mobility then druids. In bgs outside of FC and point defense, moonkins are pretty much useless.

Things are a bit better for us since the inclusion of xfaction, but still balance druids could use a little bit of a buff of raw numbers.

author: Bau
subject: Re: Is THIS the PVP problem?
content_md:
I’ll be honest: PvP is unbalanced because of all the ridiculously explosive damage.
Every class has it, and as hard as it may be for you to believe, it feels like being in a pre-TBC environment.

Old vanilla wasn’t perfectly balanced either, but even a full-green character could survive two or three hits. Here, if you’re a fresh level 60, some classes can literally one-shot you (like a critical Arcane Rupture from a mage, for example).
PvP clearly hasn’t been tested enough, and it really shows. The mechanics aren’t what they used to be, where fights involved a lot more strategy, even in 2v1 or 3v1 situations. Now you just get smacked way too hard, even if you’re skilled.
Ask the people who made vanilla PvP history none of them play here, not even the die-hard vanilla fans.

You can make up a thousand excuses, because I see everyone defending their own class. Obviously a rogue will never say rogues need nerfs. Well, I say everything needs nerfs.
There’s way too much nonsense making the game absurdly explosive.
Believe whatever you want, but the population is dropping not only in PvP but also in PvE, where bosses don’t even get to enter their mechanics because of how much damage is being thrown at them.

author: Snoof
subject: Re: Is THIS the PVP problem?
content_md:
1 - Pretty much. Not necessarily OP in PvP (although those poisons **ARE** messed up right now), but their CC spammy playstyle is the gameplay equivalent of giving anybody who runs into one 1v1 crotch rot.

 2 - Beyond broken. It's really quite ridiculous for the best support class in the game to also be able to 1-shot everybody with their basic rotation, and between their high armor class and stoneskin totem they're practically immune to physical damage while doing it. I think the devs need to make a final decision about whether they want enhancement to be a DPS spec or a tanking one, because as long as it's allowed to be both you're just not gonna be able to balance this class for PvP.

 3 - Every bit as bullshit as Shaman for many of the same reasons. Practically unduelable, they have a spell to answer nearly every situation, they're extremely good at supporting other classes when they can be bothered to (although at least they don't do it just by existing to the extent that shamans do) and they can whack you with one of the longest stuns in the game from range in spite of being a melee class. They also get high burst that ignores armor on top of all that because why not, I guess. Only class in the game I can't think of a single bad matchup for. Tools to break bubble need to be introduced to the game if you want to balance the class without making Retri unviable in PvE.

 4 - Not bad, but the barrier for entry warriors have to be competitive in PvP is astronomical since gear is absolutely everything for them. They're also pathetically reliant on teammates and consumables to do basically anything that isn't bursting an isolated Priest, and have the survivability of wet tissue paper without dedicated PvP gear. Rotten duelists, too. The CC vulnerability is very much still there; there's a talent that lets warriors cleanse roots with berserker rage on TWoW, but it's largely irrelevant in PvP since it's so deep in the Fury tree that Arms warriors can't access it.

 5 - Curses are extremely obnoxious and affliction warlocks can absolutely ruin the day of any class that doesn't have self-healing without even fighting them because they're able to apply multiple dots with one spell cast, but overall I don't think they're unbalanced. I do wish the duration on curses was reduced on player targets though; still having debuffs on you from a Warlock you fought 5 minutes ago is absolute cancer.

 6 - Generally fine, although the fact that mages' channeled spells (icicles, arcane missiles) can't be broken through LoS and seem to stretch their range to infinity while being cast makes them extremely unfair to fight against in some scenarios. Frost mages might be just a touch *too* good at fucking over melees with constant frostbite procs, but they get dunked on by other casters so I guess that's a kind of balance - not what I'd call a good one, rock paper scissors is a pretty dull formula for PvP IMO, but a kind of balance.

 7 - Yeah Hunters just suck in PvP. Everything a ranged hunter can do a casters can do better, and survival hunters are completely unviable as melees due to not having any reliable gap closers to get onto the ranged and being too low armor to square up against the other melees. I'm sure there's something they beat, but I'd generally rather be on a team with no hunters.

 8 - Obnoxiously good at carrying flags in WSG, but the same thing that makes them really good at that one thing makes them pretty mid at everything else. Druids in PvP are made to kite and run away, but since there's usually very little incentive to chase a Druid around the map in any non-WSG flag carrier scenario, it's a pretty mediocre strength to have. Balance druids' damage takes way too long to come out, feral druids die at lightspeed in Cat form where they do damage but are invincible in Bear where the most they can do is be kind of annoying. Resto is not too bad, but their reliance on shifting to bear for survival makes them pretty bad under pressure compared to other healers, especially if you're not a Tauren with access to war stomp.

 9 - Priests are generally pretty good and have a lot of unique tools that make them extremely valuable to have on your team, but they're balanced to rely a little too much on fears - probably the least reliable form of CC in Turtle PvP - to stay alive in group fights and tend to melt very easily under pressure. I think they'd be in a good place if some of the more ubiquitous fear cleansers like Will of the Forsaken and Tremor Totems were nerfed for PvP.

author: Surtugal
subject: Re: Is THIS the PVP problem?
content_md:
Guys, I don’t know why you make such a fuzz about vanilla(+) WoW PvP in 2025.

Vanilla PvP is asymmetrical, unbalanced and unfair BY DESIGN. Even though it’s called World of Warcraft, the gameplay core is heavily PvE focused. Unlike Guild Wars (same era), PvE bleeds heavily into PvP, to such an extent that it dominates the Battleground.
It’s not a question of „Who outplays whom“, WoW PvP is simply „who outgears whom“ (including consumables, enchants etc).

The only way to even try resolving that issue is a completely seperate system for PvP and PvE.

author: Yoraeryu
subject: Suggestion to give a time limit to Warsong Gulch
content_md:
Hello all. I doubt this is the first time someone has brought this up, but since I couldn’t find the exact topic here easy I decided to post about it myself.

It has become increasingly frustrating how long Warsong Gulch matches can take. People “turtle” a lot because nobody wants to risk losing. I understand that, but it feels like we are wasting the time of many PvP players. Some are here for reputation, others for marks, and some just want to finish and either stop or move on to Arathi, Alterac or Arena without having to forfeit the match.

This doesn’t happen every game, but there are times when a Warsong match can go on forever. I think a 20–30 minute limit per match would make things much better, and would also help reshuffle players more often. Some say a flag debuff would be a better solution since with a time limit people could still turtle to win – but honestly, they already do that now, and matches last forever anyway. I would rather lose a match and be done than sit in a game that never ends. I don’t mind queuing again if I know there is actually an end in sight.

This idea could also apply to other battlegrounds where turtling becomes a problem, but I mainly wanted to talk about Warsong Gulch since that’s where it feels the worst. Whether people agree with the suggestion or whether it’s taken into consideration is another matter, but I wanted to put the idea out there.

Thank you for your time, and have a great day everyone!

Thanks for your comment. I’ll be honest though, the tone you chose kind of proves part of the issue. I made a suggestion about match pacing, and instead of keeping things civil you jumped straight into personal remarks (“listen sister,” “pee drawers”). That doesn’t strengthen your argument, and it reflects a defensive attitude that pops up a lot in PvP discussions. It’s very possible to disagree without getting personal. ![🙂](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f642.svg)

Anyway, onto the actual points:

 1 “Longer WSG = more fun” is only true for a specific type of PvP-purist players, and they tend to be the loudest.
Not everyone enjoys 45–90 minute stalemates. Some players want rep, marks, honor, or simply a match that actually ends, this  isn’t “anti-fun”, it’s just a different definition of fun.

 2 A time limit doesn’t stop good matches from happening.
Strong teams can still have intense, competitive games,  just without them dragging on forever because both sides are afraid to make a move or cant push. Eternal turtle games punish both sides equally.

 3 “Just leave the match” isn’t a solution.
Leaving punishes your team, wastes your queue time, and feels bad. Asking for a system that avoids very long lockouts is far more constructive. And this was simply a suggestion, no need for anyone to get salty about it.

 4 Not everyone queues for the same reasons.
Some people PvP for the thrill of it, some for rewards, some for progression or rep. These are all valid. Acting like there’s only one “correct” reason to play doesn’t help the discussion.

 5 Class balance and match length are separate issues.
Yes, class balance needs work. But that doesn’t affect whether matches should last 20 minutes or 90. Both problems can be addressed independently.

 6 Accessibility doesn’t kill PvP,  it keeps it alive.
You mentioned the community is old. Exactly. Older players have jobs, families, responsibilities, and limited play windows. Healthier pacing keeps battlegrounds populated instead of scaring people away with hour-long slogs.

Lastly:
I never attacked anyone for liking long games. I get that people enjoy them. I only pointed out that not everyone enjoys endless stalemates, that was my entire point. There’s no reason for the discussion to turn personal.

I PvP because I enjoy it, but I don’t enjoy when a match becomes a time sink with no progress. And I’m not doing it for leveling or “easy ranking”; I often lock my levels to play different brackets, and my 60s leveled mostly through quests. Please don’t assume who I am just because I made a suggestion.

Everyone has the right to offer ideas. People can disagree, that’s totally fine  but keeping it constructive makes the conversation better for everyone. The people above you shared their counterpoints clearly and respectfully, and even if I disagreed with some of it, I could fully understand where they were coming from.

Have a nice day!

author: Crake
subject: Re: are rogues the devs friend now
content_md:
Poisons have always ignored armor.

I need a copypasta about how a noxious assault rogue can't even get a full stun combo out without gaps, not to mention they can't put up all the buffs they need while keeping someone stunlocked, and they also don't have the energy to do more than 2-3 noxious assaults in a full combo, of which they get about 3-3.5k damage in tops. Mages one shot you for more damage than that, and that ALSO ignores armor

Also, cheap shot lasts 4 seconds, and kidney lasts 6 if done at 5 combo points.

 **A noxious assault rogue's opener would look like this:**

Cheapshot (60 energy) -> Noxious Assault (45-4 energy for poison procs)
At this point the rogue has 9 energy, and needs to wait 3 energy ticks to recoup enough energy for another noxious assault + kidney. This means the rogue must either kidney at 4 combo points, losing 2 seconds of the stun, or they can barely squeeze in another noxious assault to get to 5 combo points, but leave a gap for a retaliation (psychic scream, mortal coil, stun, some kind of dot on them to make resetting more difficult, eating the poison mushroom so you can trinket kidney and break the blind, pop a fap etc) before they get the next energy tick for a kidney. IF THEY'RE LUCKY they might get enough energy from poison procs, but without envenom, their proc chance isn't amazing.

Lets say they get a full kidney off cause you were bad. They now have 28 energy and 6 more seconds, which means 3 more ticks. That is a whole 2 more noxious assaults, and 3 total combo points on you with 6 energy left in the tank, meaning you get ANOTHER chance to retaliate before they have the energy to pop a blind on you and try to go for a full reset.

so the full combo looks like this:
Cheap shot -> Noxious assault -> Noxious assault -> stun gap -> kidney shot -> noxious assault -> noxious assault -> stun gap -> blind -> reset

You get 2 chances to save yourself if they're going full zug. If they're NOT going full zug, they you should be able to live through the 2 noxious assaults unless your gear is absolute dogwater.

 **On the other hand, a hemo rogue's combo will look like this:**

Cheap shot -> hemo -> hemo -> full kidney (no stun gap) -> hemo -> hemo -> blind -> if you counter or retaliate, they prep and reblind, or if you're low, they just vanish -> cheap shot -> cold blood -> eviscerate. All that with no gaps, and no energy issues.

Oh, and they're also auto attacking you with poisons on their weapons exactly the same as the noxious assault rogue the whole time.

 **tl;dr:** if you're dying to a noxious assault rogue, its because you got pve zugged, and that's a skill issue. Pvp specced sub rogues are still way more deadly, and they've been playing the exact same for decades at this point.

A BG is a series of fights and having this available 4-5 times during them means that this item probably helps turn the tide of the battle very often, wouldn't you agree? author: Crake
subject: Re: Spell Reflection is getting out of hand.
content_md:
Here's why physical reflector wont be a thing:

Arcane reflector protects vs: Moonkin, Arcane Mage
Shadow reflector protects vs: Warlock, Spriest
Frost reflector protects vs: Frost mage
Fire reflector protects vs: Fire mage, some warlock spells
Nature reflector protects vs: Elemental shaman, some moonkin spells

Meanwhile, a theoretical physical reflector would protect vs: All warriors, all rogues, feral druids, hunters, paladins, and enhancement shaman.

That's all dps options from 4/9 classes, and half the dps options from the remaining 2. That is easily more than 50% of the likely dps you're going to run into. It ceases to be a niche item at that point, and would just become mandatory

Nature reflector protects vs: Elemental shaman, some moonkin spells

author: Silverleafeon
subject: Does cross-faction PvP break the lore?
content_md:
One of the things that drew me to Turtle WoW was its dedication to quality. To staying true to the lore. To making me feel like I was actually stepping into a living, breathing fantasy world where my choices and my character mattered.

When cross-faction dungeons were added, I was initially hesitant, but I eventually convinced myself it could make sense. Adventurers far from civilization might have to put aside their differences to survive. A Human and an Orc, miles from safety, might temporarily cooperate to defeat a greater threat, a grudging truce of convenience. That kind of alliance fits within fantasy storytelling, and even in Warcraft lore, grudges can be set aside in the face of danger.

But PvP is different. Battlegrounds like Warsong Gulch, Arathi Basin, and Alterac Valley aren’t just random skirmishes. They’re expressions of the ongoing war between Horde and Alliance. Night Elves defending Ashenvale should not be fighting alongside Orcs; Humans in Arathi should not be standing shoulder-to-shoulder with Undead. Cross-faction battlegrounds break that narrative, undermining the sense of tension and stakes that makes PvP meaningful.

I’m not a hardcore PvPer. I enjoy battlegrounds from time to time, but PvP is part of a larger whole for me: it enriches the world, ties into quests, and reinforces the story. But with Cross-Faction battlegrounds, that experience will feel diluted and hollow. Imagine questing through Ashenvale as a Night Elf, defending your forests against invading Orcs, only to queue for WSG and end up fighting alongside those same Orcs. It’s immersion-breaking.

Yes, I could switch to Tel’Abim where PvP is the focus and cross-faction won't be an issue, but that’s not really an option I want to pursue. Moving characters or starting from scratch is inconvenient, and I don’t want to play on a realm where world PvP dominates every aspect of gameplay. I want a balanced experience: questing, dungeons, and the occasional battleground, all tied into a coherent world.

So, I’m curious, does anyone else feel the same way? Do you think cross-faction battlegrounds make sense within the Warcraft world, or do they undermine the story and immersion that make Turtle WoW special?
