author: Silverleafeon
subject: Re: Does cross-faction PvP break the lore?
content_md:
> **Alfredostfu wrote: Sat Dec 13, 2025 7:49 pm**
> Lore isn't worth it at the cost of gameplay.
>
>  What's the point of staying lore accurate if noone can pvp because we don't have enough time and we are stuck with 1 hour queues?
>
>  Unless we want twow to be a dead game to stay lore accurate.

I don’t think this has to be an either/or choice, and that’s where I fundamentally disagree.

Turtle WoW didn’t grow because it chased pure gameplay efficiency. It grew because it offered a cohesive experience where gameplay, atmosphere, and lore reinforced each other. That’s the whole reason people were willing to accept slower pacing, longer leveling, and even inconvenience, because the world felt meaningful.

If lore truly “wasn’t worth it at the cost of gameplay,” Turtle WoW wouldn’t exist in the first place. There are already servers that optimize everything for queues, balance, and instant access. People came here specifically because this project valued immersion and world integrity alongside gameplay, not as an afterthought.

Long queues are a real problem, but sacrificing the faction war, one of the core pillars of Warcraft PvP, isn’t a neutral fix. It changes what battlegrounds are. WSG and AB aren’t abstract esports maps; they’re narrative battlefields. Once you strip that away, you’re not just solving a queue issue, you’re redefining the game’s identity.

And I’d argue that undermining that identity is just as dangerous to the long-term health of the server as long queues are. Players don’t stay on Turtle WoW because it’s the fastest or most convenient option. They stay because it feels like a living world with stakes and meaning.

So yes, gameplay matters. Queue times matter. But so does the soul of the game. Treating lore and immersion as expendable “nice-to-haves” is how you slowly turn a unique server into just another one.
content_html:
Lore isn't worth it at the cost of gameplay.

What's the point of staying lore accurate if noone can pvp because we don't have enough time and we are stuck with 1 hour queues?

Unless we want twow to be a dead game to stay lore accurate.
I don’t think this has to be an either/or choice, and that’s where I fundamentally disagree.

Turtle WoW didn’t grow because it chased pure gameplay efficiency. It grew because it offered a cohesive experience where gameplay, atmosphere, and lore reinforced each other. That’s the whole reason people were willing to accept slower pacing, longer leveling, and even inconvenience, because the world felt meaningful.

If lore truly “wasn’t worth it at the cost of gameplay,” Turtle WoW wouldn’t exist in the first place. There are already servers that optimize everything for queues, balance, and instant access. People came here specifically because this project valued immersion and world integrity alongside gameplay, not as an afterthought.

Long queues are a real problem, but sacrificing the faction war, one of the core pillars of Warcraft PvP, isn’t a neutral fix. It changes what battlegrounds are. WSG and AB aren’t abstract esports maps; they’re narrative battlefields. Once you strip that away, you’re not just solving a queue issue, you’re redefining the game’s identity.

And I’d argue that undermining that identity is just as dangerous to the long-term health of the server as long queues are. Players don’t stay on Turtle WoW because it’s the fastest or most convenient option. They stay because it feels like a living world with stakes and meaning.

So yes, gameplay matters. Queue times matter. But so does the soul of the game. Treating lore and immersion as expendable “nice-to-haves” is how you slowly turn a unique server into just another one.

author: Maxe71
subject: WSG – How to: Perspective from Sybril
content_md:
When I enter Warsong Gulch, I am not thinking about kills. I am thinking about time. Time is rank, and rank is discipline. Every action that does not move the flag closer to a capture is wasted effort.

The first thing I look for is the Flag Carrier. If we do not have one assigned before the gates open, we are already behind. In Classic, the Druid is king. Mobility decides everything. Armor does not save you, damage does not save you. Movement does. A slow carrier is a dead carrier, and a dead carrier is a lost match.

Once the carrier is chosen, the healers fall into place. One healer belongs to the Flag Carrier and nowhere else. Not midfield, not chasing kills, not padding meters. Their job is to keep that carrier alive through shields, dispels, and positioning. If that healer drifts, even for a moment, the enemy will feel it and punish it.

The rest of the team is not there to fight for glory. They are there to control space. Midfield is the heart of Warsong Gulch. Whoever owns midfield controls the pace of the game. I want slows, roots, fears, and pressure applied there constantly. A Warrior keeping Hamstring up, a Mage freezing the ground, a Hunter tracking movement. This is where games are won quietly, long before the flag reaches the base.

At the start, we move with intent. The carrier pushes immediately with support. Two players stay back on defense, not to farm kills, but to delay. Delay is victory in small pieces. The rest of the team takes midfield and holds it. If midfield collapses, the match becomes a chase, and chasing costs time.

When we engage the enemy Flag Carrier, we do not rush. The first target is always the healer. Always. Crowd control, grenades, pressure. Once the healer is gone, the carrier falls quickly. Anyone tunneling the carrier while the healer stands free is playing the wrong game.

Defending our own carrier is about anticipation, not reaction. Dispel before the stun lands. Peel before the burst comes in. Use Free Action Potions before the choke, not after. Swiftness is for breaking contact, not for panic. A clean escape is better than a heroic last stand.

Recoveries must be fast and decisive. Rogue scouts ahead. Hunter denies stealth. Mage controls the ground. If a recovery takes more than half a minute, we have already given the enemy too much time.

Consumables are not optional. In ranked Warsong, they are part of your kit. Free Action, Swiftness, healing and mana potions, bandages. Engineering tools are standard issue. If you walk in without them, you are asking your team to carry you.

Communication stays short. Clear. Functional. No speeches, no arguments. “FC tunnel.” “Healer down.” “Cap in ten.” Anything more is noise.

Warsong Gulch is not about proving how strong you are. It is about proving you can follow a plan. Fast wins matter. Clean execution matters. Ego does not.

That is how you rank. That is how you win.

author: Maxe71
subject: AB – How to: Perspective from Sybril
content_md:
When I enter Arathi Basin as Alliance, I remind myself of one fundamental truth: this battleground is not symmetrical in how it is played, but it is perfectly symmetrical in how it is won. Pressure creates reactions, and reactions create openings. The team that understands where not to fight usually wins.

Geography is the first teacher. From the Alliance side, Stables is our anchor. It is close, defensible, and rarely the point where games are decided. Blacksmith is the crossroads, Lumber Mill the eyes of the map, Farm and Gold Mine the pressure valves. (For the Horde, Farm plays the same anchoring role as Stables, with the same logic applied in reverse.)

Lumber Mill deserves constant strategic attention. If we control it, we see almost everything. Rotations toward Blacksmith, pressure moving to Farm, even reinforcements leaving Stables. Vision allows us to move first. (For the Horde, LM serves the same purpose, especially to track movement toward Farm and Blacksmith.)

But strategy is not only about holding. It is also about reacting correctly when pressure builds. If the enemy commits heavily to Gold Mine, that tells me something important: they are not defending elsewhere. In that situation, I do not reinforce blindly. I look to the opposite end of the map. If Lumber Mill is not ours, that is where pressure should go immediately. Force them to choose between finishing an attack or losing a base they are not watching. (For the Horde, a heavy Alliance push on Gold Mine should trigger a counter-attack on Lumber Mill or Stables.)

The same logic applies everywhere. If Stables is under heavy assault and reinforcements are already moving, the correct play is often not to overcommit there, but to apply pressure at Farm. Stables is close and easy to retake; Farm is not. Trading time at one node for a capture at its opposite creates long-term advantage. (For the Horde, pressure on Farm should be answered by threats on Stables.)

Blacksmith sits at the center of this logic. It is rarely the correct response to send everyone there. Blacksmith is a pivot, not a destination. If it is heavily contested, look at what is being ignored. Lumber Mill and Farm often open up when Blacksmith turns into a brawl. (For the Horde, the same distraction effect applies.)

This is where class roles become decisive. Stealth classes are not there to duel. Rogues and Druids should constantly look for undefended or lightly defended bases. A single sap or opener at the right moment can flip a node while the enemy is busy elsewhere. Stealth wins Arathi Basin quietly. (This applies identically to Horde stealth players.)

Mages and Hunters are ideal for Lumber Mill duty. Slows, roots, knockbacks, and line of sight abuse turn LM into a fortress. Their job is not to kill, but to delay and inform. Every second they survive is a second the team can rotate. (For the Horde, these classes fulfill the same role on LM.)

Warriors, Paladins, and other plate wearers excel at anchoring nodes like Stables or Farm. Their strength is not mobility, but stubbornness. They buy time. They force enemies to commit resources. They hold flags under pressure. (For the Horde, this role is usually filled at Farm.)

Healers should think defensively, not heroically. A healer on a flag, keeping defenders alive and calling incoming early, is more valuable than one chasing fights at Blacksmith. Survival creates options. Death creates problems. (This is universally true for both factions.)

Rotations must always consider distance. Stables is easy for Alliance to retake; Lumber Mill is not. Farm is easier for Horde to reinforce; Stables is not. When deciding where to fight, always ask: if we lose this base, how fast can we get it back? Fight hardest where recovery is slow. (Each faction has its own “far” and “near” nodes.)

The greatest strategic error in Arathi Basin is mirroring blindly. If the enemy zergs one base, do not zerg back to the same place unless it is absolutely critical. Pressure the opposite side of the map. Force splits. Force decisions. Arathi Basin rewards teams that think laterally.

Finally, discipline matters more than brilliance. Holding three bases with calm rotations will beat a stronger team that chases kills and reacts late. Awareness, early calls, and respect for map geometry win more games than any individual play.

That is how you control Arathi Basin.

author: Thaladar
subject: Rogues in PvP: This Isn’t Vanilla Anymore
content_md:
**TL;DR**

 * Rogues’ new poison talents push their burst far beyond “high” into “unhealable.”
 * Priest PvP is now literally unplayable against them.
 * Druid tools don’t fix it — even with detection, they kill you instantly.
 * Their kit has too much: CC, damage, mobility, ranged kick, unremovable Blind.
 * They’re overtuned in PvE and PvP.
 * If rogues delete people in 1–2 seconds, the entire concept of stealth loses meaning.

This needs to be tuned. Something needs to give.  **Suggestion:**
Just revert this new poison spec or tune its damage to match the other rogue builds. Right now it’s overtuned to the point of breaking PvP. I know the ongoing lawsuit must be taking priority and PvP isn’t the main focus right now, but please just retune rogues so the game becomes fun to play again.

 **Priest journey in PVP**

I’m fully aware that vanilla WoW was never a balanced game. Gear matters, skill matters, racials matter. Every class has its highs and lows. But throughout all of WoW’s history, rogues have been the outlier. It's the class that performs well even without gear. Fine. That’s part of their identity. What we’re dealing with now in TWOW is something completely different.

I started PvP on my Night Elf Priest. I got destroyed at first, naturally.
But over time I collected PvP gear, resilience bonuses, raid gear etc. Eventually I reached that point where I could tank a rogue if I played perfectly - and kill them if they werent UD. I still felt immobile, lacked defensive cooldowns, but at least I could play the game.

Not anymore.

Right now, the moment a rogue makes contact with any target; cloth, plate, bear, whatever.
Unhealable deletion. As a Priest I can’t heal through it. As a Druid I can’t heal through it.
I can’t save my teammates. I can’t save myself. At this point, if the enemy team has a rogue, my Priest may as well AFK at the GY. That’s how useless the class feels.

And yes, everyone knows me. I’ve been around long enough. I’ve played through Horde’s overtuned racials, through WotF/Tremor/Horde fearward nonsense, through a meta that has always been rough for Priest. But this isn’t “rough.” This is unplayable.

 **“Just reroll” and so I did. And guess what?**

I rerolled Druid. More mobility, more utility, stealth detection, Faerie Fire. The tools you’d expect to counter a stealth class. But detecting a rogue changes nothing.

People see me pop a rogue out and go “omg he’s dead.” No. He’s not. Because:

 * he still has all cooldowns
 * he still has absurd reach
 * he still reaches me regardless
 * and I’m dead in 1–2 seconds anyway

Even being the counter-class doesn’t counter them. This kit is doing way too much. The new poison talents pushed it over the edge. A rogue now has:

 * absurd damage
 * too much CC
 * a ranged interrupt that also slows
 * Blind that can’t be removed anymore
 * the best opener in the game
 * the best escape in the game
 * the best ability to pick any fight
 * and the best ability to avoid any bad fight

If you’re going to give a class THIS much damage, then something else in their kit needs to go.
Right now, they do everything better than everyone. If they kill everything on contact… why do they even need stealth? Genuinely. With my FF's they still run around killing people. Others in this forum act as if them getting FF'd destroys them completely. If the moment they reach a target that target is dead, what’s the role of stealth anymore? What’s the counterplay? What exactly are the rest of us supposed to do? Right now the only viable thing to do is to bring your own Rogues and have them stunlock enemy rogues to death.

Viable lvl 60 pvper is several weeks of raiding. For less dedicated player is might be several months.

author: Firewi33
subject: Ambershire PvP balancing issue - Balance Shamans
content_md:
When Arathi Basin regularly ends up with 2 premades running 5 Shamans, it’s clear there’s a balance problem. This pushes more players to reroll Shamans and hurts class variety in PvP.

In large fights, Shamans can quickly kill even 6k HP defenders with shocks and burst damage. When several Shamans do this at once, defending objectives becomes nearly impossible, no matter the gear or positioning.

If this keeps going, PvP will become predictable and people will stop queuing.

Balancing Shamans the same way Paladins were adjusted feels like the logical next step. Ignoring this might be ok in the short term, but it risks long-term damage to PvP and the overall health of the server.

author: Bau
subject: I’ve Read All the PvP Complaints...
content_md:
Dear PvP friends of Turtle WoW, this message is for everyone who enjoys PvP, whether you play it seriously or just for fun and not for competition.
I have read many topics that mostly reflect individual opinions, and I have to disagree with them because they often lack fairness. Since the talent and skill update patch, every topic seems to talk about the same things over and over again. One player says that all classes are too strong except hunters.
Another says that every other class is ridiculously overpowered and that paladins deserve more attention. Another claims that priests have no space to play because all the other classes can do everything better. And so on, you can easily imagine the rest.

Then there are people who try to make class rankings that are sometimes mostly fair, but they still end up denigrating the classes they clearly do not play themselves.
I am not trying to be the voice of truth or someone who must be right, but take a moment to think about this. It is useless to throw dirt on every class except the one you play.
A more honest approach would be to admit that the patch, which was meant to improve PvE and actually did so, has had too much impact on PvP balance, which was already fragile before.
Unfortunately, when patches are designed to balance damage, healing, skills and mechanics for PvE, those changes inevitably spill over into PvP.
Like many of you, I believe it would have been better to design PvP-focused changes that then affect PvE, because for PvE players the difference would be minimal.

Why do I say that it would not change much? It is simple. If you are like me and played the original vanilla before private servers even existed, you know exactly what I mean. PvE has always been a complex strategy of numbers, consumables, calls and rotations.
No matter how much damage your class did, whether too little or too much, almost no one ever complained that a boss was too hard and needed to be nerfed, except in very rare or specific cases.

In PvP, however, the experience is completely different. Those who played old vanilla know that even if it was poorly balanced, players always found their own way to play against other classes. I am not saying that if you are good you automatically win, but I am saying that in some ways it was better when it was worse. Complaints existed back then too, but they were far more constructive. Now I mostly see people saying only that other classes are stronger than theirs.

Saying things like that leads nowhere if we all apply the same reasoning to every class.
In the end there are only two possibilities.
Either we accept that the classes are fine as they are and end the discussion, or we admit that all classes, and this is my personal opinion, have been overbuffed.
I would rather go back than continue down this path. At least before I knew what kind of game I was playing. With the current patch, I honestly do not know if this is a poorly functioning TBC or a damaged version of vanilla plus.

author: Solaire0726
subject: warlock will be the bomb in 2v2(1.18.1)
content_md:
This content is about the strength of the Warlock class in PvP on the Turtle WoW server and the consequences of the rated arena opening in version 1.18.1.

In the current evaluation of 2v2 arenas, the Warlock class is the strongest, for the following reasons:

 1.High Health Pool: A fully geared Warlock can reach over 5000 HP (those prioritizing damage typically have around 5000 HP, while those stacking Stamina can even reach 7000). For example, on Nordanaar, I encountered a Warlock named Tapkalol with 6.8k HP. Before a 2v2 arena match begins, the Warlock can sacrifice their Voidwalker to gain a shield, effectively adding even more health. Combined with a Healthstone, this grants the Warlock exceptionally strong survivability. PS: Only a Rogue might be able to quickly take them down, and even then, they must be careful not to be detected by Detect Invisibility.

 2.Reliable Crowd Control Chain: In 2v2 arenas, Warlocks can summon a Felguard, which has an Axe Toss ability for reliable crowd control. This pairs with the Warlock's own Death Coil to form a control chain. Within those few seconds, they can quickly burst down a target with over 5000 HP. Additionally, the Felguard has an ability to break crowd control and a high-damage Shadowstorm skill, making it overwhelmingly powerful in 2v2 arenas. Even if they forgo the Felguard for a Felhunter, the Warlock remains a caster killer, though it feels less oppressive than facing the Felguard and causes less frustration.

 3.Consistent and High Damage: The Warlock's damage over time (DoT) effects, combined with Shadow harvest (or Soul Harvest), are instant casts like a Mage's Arcane Missiles. Once applied, they can only be stopped by interrupts, and during this time, your health drops rapidly. Paired with their crowd control, this creates an unparalleled sense of frustration—you enter the arena ready to outplay your opponent, only to be locked down and drained to death.

These three factors make the Warlock a monstrous presence. If no adjustments are made after the introduction of rated arenas, I believe a Warlock + Holy Paladin composition will dominate everything. I hope the Turtle WoW class designers see this post. If a single class possesses all three of these advantages, it becomes nearly impossible to counter or contain. (For example, the Flame Shaman in version 1.18.0 disrupted the PvP environment with high armor and burst damage, but it could still be controlled through crowd control. With the changes in 1.18.1, Flame Shamans may no longer be viable in PvP, as the condition for melee to trigger damage buffs is too demanding.)

If adjustments are to be made, I hope the development team will consider limiting powerful summons like the Felguard in rated arenas, while also reducing the damage of Warlock DoTs combined with instant nukes in PvP. This would address the issue of dealing massive damage without any cost (such as casting time). Alternatively, the survivability of the Warlock itself could be nerfed. I hope we can discuss this rationally.

content_html:
This content is about the strength of the Warlock class in PvP on the Turtle WoW server and the consequences of the rated arena opening in version 1.18.1.

In the current evaluation of 2v2 arenas, the Warlock class is the strongest, for the following reasons:

1.High Health Pool: A fully geared Warlock can reach over 5000 HP (those prioritizing damage typically have around 5000 HP, while those stacking Stamina can even reach 7000). For example, on Nordanaar, I encountered a Warlock named Tapkalol with 6.8k HP. Before a 2v2 arena match begins, the Warlock can sacrifice their Voidwalker to gain a shield, effectively adding even more health. Combined with a Healthstone, this grants the Warlock exceptionally strong survivability. PS: Only a Rogue might be able to quickly take them down, and even then, they must be careful not to be detected by Detect Invisibility.

2.Reliable Crowd Control Chain: In 2v2 arenas, Warlocks can summon a Felguard, which has an Axe Toss ability for reliable crowd control. This pairs with the Warlock's own Death Coil to form a control chain. Within those few seconds, they can quickly burst down a target with over 5000 HP. Additionally, the Felguard has an ability to break crowd control and a high-damage Shadowstorm skill, making it overwhelmingly powerful in 2v2 arenas. Even if they forgo the Felguard for a Felhunter, the Warlock remains a caster killer, though it feels less oppressive than facing the Felguard and causes less frustration.

3.Consistent and High Damage: The Warlock's damage over time (DoT) effects, combined with Shadow harvest (or Soul Harvest), are instant casts like a Mage's Arcane Missiles. Once applied, they can only be stopped by interrupts, and during this time, your health drops rapidly. Paired with their crowd control, this creates an unparalleled sense of frustration—you enter the arena ready to outplay your opponent, only to be locked down and drained to death.

These three factors make the Warlock a monstrous presence. If no adjustments are made after the introduction of rated arenas, I believe a Warlock + Holy Paladin composition will dominate everything. I hope the Turtle WoW class designers see this post. If a single class possesses all three of these advantages, it becomes nearly impossible to counter or contain. (For example, the Flame Shaman in version 1.18.0 disrupted the PvP environment with high armor and burst damage, but it could still be controlled through crowd control. With the changes in 1.18.1, Flame Shamans may no longer be viable in PvP, as the condition for melee to trigger damage buffs is too demanding.)

If adjustments are to be made, I hope the development team will consider limiting powerful summons like the Felguard in rated arenas, while also reducing the damage of Warlock DoTs combined with instant nukes in PvP. This would address the issue of dealing massive damage without any cost (such as casting time). Alternatively, the survivability of the Warlock itself could be nerfed. I hope we can discuss this rationally.
And 1 thing important，Ultra-Flash Shadow Reflector cant reflect shadow harvest and dot dmg.Theres just no way to counter it—outside of interrupts and debuff cleansing, youve got nothing.

content_html:
This content is about the strength of the Warlock class in PvP on the Turtle WoW server and the consequences of the rated arena opening in version 1.18.1.

In the current evaluation of 2v2 arenas, the Warlock class is the strongest, for the following reasons:

1.High Health Pool: A fully geared Warlock can reach over 5000 HP (those prioritizing damage typically have around 5000 HP, while those stacking Stamina can even reach 7000). For example, on Nordanaar, I encountered a Warlock named Tapkalol with 6.8k HP. Before a 2v2 arena match begins, the Warlock can sacrifice their Voidwalker to gain a shield, effectively adding even more health. Combined with a Healthstone, this grants the Warlock exceptionally strong survivability. PS: Only a Rogue might be able to quickly take them down, and even then, they must be careful not to be detected by Detect Invisibility.

2.Reliable Crowd Control Chain: In 2v2 arenas, Warlocks can summon a Felguard, which has an Axe Toss ability for reliable crowd control. This pairs with the Warlock's own Death Coil to form a control chain. Within those few seconds, they can quickly burst down a target with over 5000 HP. Additionally, the Felguard has an ability to break crowd control and a high-damage Shadowstorm skill, making it overwhelmingly powerful in 2v2 arenas. Even if they forgo the Felguard for a Felhunter, the Warlock remains a caster killer, though it feels less oppressive than facing the Felguard and causes less frustration.

3.Consistent and High Damage: The Warlock's damage over time (DoT) effects, combined with Shadow harvest (or Soul Harvest), are instant casts like a Mage's Arcane Missiles. Once applied, they can only be stopped by interrupts, and during this time, your health drops rapidly. Paired with their crowd control, this creates an unparalleled sense of frustration—you enter the arena ready to outplay your opponent, only to be locked down and drained to death.

These three factors make the Warlock a monstrous presence. If no adjustments are made after the introduction of rated arenas, I believe a Warlock + Holy Paladin composition will dominate everything. I hope the Turtle WoW class designers see this post. If a single class possesses all three of these advantages, it becomes nearly impossible to counter or contain. (For example, the Flame Shaman in version 1.18.0 disrupted the PvP environment with high armor and burst damage, but it could still be controlled through crowd control. With the changes in 1.18.1, Flame Shamans may no longer be viable in PvP, as the condition for melee to trigger damage buffs is too demanding.)

If adjustments are to be made, I hope the development team will consider limiting powerful summons like the Felguard in rated arenas, while also reducing the damage of Warlock DoTs combined with instant nukes in PvP. This would address the issue of dealing massive damage without any cost (such as casting time). Alternatively, the survivability of the Warlock itself could be nerfed. I hope we can discuss this rationally.
And 1 thing important，Ultra-Flash Shadow Reflector cant reflect shadow harvest and dot dmg.Theres just no way to counter it—outside of interrupts and debuff cleansing, youve got nothing.
https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=3387

It would be nice to have a spell damage equivalent to this, that lets you continue physical attacks while under its effects, like spell casters can continue their attacks under LIP.

Warlocks with LIP are a little diabolical right now. It would at least be cool if I could pop something to counter it, to have a chance

subject: Remove the GCD on shadow form. / shadow mend changes
content_md:
Right now, as I believe, the shadow priest in PvP has VPT and power word: shield as survival abilities in shadow form. The problem occurs mainly when getting locked against melee. To leave shadow form it takes 0.5 sec, cast heal, *enter shadowform*, takes another 0,5 sec. This makes it kicked on shadow = death.
 1. Make the GCD lesser when entering leaving shadowform
 2. Making a disc/holy talent in the upper rows that allows for more frequent application of shield.
 3. Make shadow mend usable on yourself.

I believe that 1 of one of these changes would greatly improve the priest in the current meta and improve the current survial ability issues that, as I see, the class in PvP currently has.

content_md:
You are correct, the incentive to queue Sunnyglade is still very low.

Around 1 year ago I suggested increasing the honor gain because it was so bad. Devs increased it but the change wasn't satisfying. Now on Sunnyglade bonus day, winners receive 1.5k honor and losers 1k. Average game lasts about 15 minutes. I think WSG is a bit longer on average but awards twice as much honor (I might be wrong, I don't know exact numbers).

Reputation farm in this BG is a pain, you get 150 rep by winning if I remember correctly. Black Morass is way better.

The truth is most of the players that queue into battlegrounds do it for honor farm. They don't care about how it is played, they do care about efficient farming. If the incentive to play specific battleground is low, they won't queue for it. I think that current Sunnyglade Valley with all its faults could still be widely played if the incentive would be high enough. 2k honor for losing, 3k honor for winning (on SGV bonus day) would be OK. Also, 500 rep for winning and 250 for losing.

Another reason why Sunnyglade isn't played as often is requirement of 12 queued people. In comparison WSG requires only 6 or 8 people to maintain the game.

BTW they remove Sunnyglade Valley because they can't open the map in Noggit. That means they can't edit the map. Further edition of the map is impossible so only complete rework can save it.

 **NEW BATTLEGROUND — THORN GORGE**

Teams capture flags and bases until they reach the maximum resource points needed to win.

Questions:
 -at which level range is the bg first available?
 -are there designated new rep factions?
 -are there any reputation or token rewards?
 -where are the battlemasters/camps for this bg?

 **Sunnyglade valley**

 -removed until its reworked.

 **Dampening Debuff**

introduced in 1.18.0 will now have dynamic reductions of Magical and Physical damage based on your class / spec instead of a flat number for all classes.

More information regarding numbers will be given at a later date.

Developer Comment: Turning these values class-dependent means that we will be less restricted in Design space of making all specs come to life and be viable without adding Player-target exceptions on a lot of spells.

content_html:
Posted on 2025 - December 3 by Torta viewtopic.php?p=161485#p161485
Level One Lunatic and the challenges UI on creation were introduced on November 1 2023 in patch 1.17.2 (the first stage of release, a few months before the actual ToK raid), while War Mode was changed in August 2025. We've been receiving many reports about "cinematic kills", not only from Nordanaar but also from other realms and regions. It gradually grew into a massive problem we could no longer ignore.

Again, I can't say whether War Mode will be changed in the future, but if it is we'll still protect tutorial towns to ensure that the very‑very early experience isn't ridiculed in a way that drives newcomers away from the server.

Please keep in mind that, while the Level One Lunatic challengers is an adorable little community, it still represents only a tiny fraction of the overall population. Consequently, we can't design massive features solely around their needs. The current format is something we're happy with, at least for now.
Even if something with warmode will change, lunatics won't be able to farm newcomers during cinematics. So effectively, you won't get that you assking here.

author: Biggamehuntard
subject: Warmode still doesnt make leveling with pvp viable
content_md:
Hey guys, Ive never made a forum post but id like to point something out:

On Nordanaar, With nobody using warmode to level in the open world and all the actual juicy xp tied to objectives in bgs and twinking, theres nothing to actually allow for the average joe to get ANY xp from the pvp system. The world pvp scene is completely dead and in bgs, all xp gain in tied to objective completion if you disregard the tiny sliver you get at the end of it for winning or losing. Its like 10% of the total potential value, worse yet, you get things like level 19,29, and 59 twinks that sit and camp honor at their bracket preventing you from ever actually getting objectives done. AB is your best bet and even then if you dont have any twinks of your own, you're not getting any through the tiny trickle of resource points that you'll get as the guy in several thousand gold of gear slams you again and again.

So, my proposal is pretty simple. Reduce the xp gain on objectives and add a small amount for pvp kills in bgs. that way when you gang up and kill enemies, you can actually still make up for objectives being insurmountable again our really expensive friends without removing twinking as a whole from them. WE all know nobody is getting the pvp kill xp in the world anymore and with everything being moved to bgs anyway, why isnt that feature already present?

Additionally, Allow me to suggest pvp quests for getting honor kills in bgs, objective capture, and maybe even something like "capture 3 flags in warsong gulch yourself" or "play a bg without dying once" or something that also rewards xp and is on quartermasters for pickup.

I dont think these are too big of an ask and it wouldnt impact much of anything. Thanks for reading! :D

author: Ellifta
subject: Remove and gut zookeeper spec for good.
content_md:
In this picture we can see one shockadin with 3 "The Lost" pets + spirit wolves we don't see in the screenshot. The Lost set in particular is extremely oppressive, each add has 3k HP and they do 200 damage attacks, there's no limit to how many one person can have other than pure luck.

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/spmgTfd4/zookeeper.png)

Considering this Lost set can be bought from AH set for outrageous prices, it should be gutted entirely and made useless. It's the biggest problem in PvP at the moment apart from class balancing. An item set someone can just buy from AH shouldn't be impossible to counter and magically give someone 600 DPS extra. I don't care what replacement stats it gets, but the pets it summons should be gone, period. No one can come up with a justification as to why this pet should be this good and have no ICD on how many you can summon.
